  future work should target the longer-copy bulk or surrounding dispatch cost.
  An x86-64 ERMS `rep movsb` follow-up for non-overlapping copies was also
  rejected. Thresholds of 256 and 512 bytes were consistently about `0.996x`
  on the focused row; 1,024 bytes was near neutral with high run noise. The
  compiler-rt vector loop therefore remains preferable for this workload.
  Inlining compiler-rt's own exact less-than-16-byte strategy was neutral too:
  twenty focused pairs split evenly around `1.000x`. This confirms that the
  current short-copy cost is not its standalone memcpy call, so the experiment
  and exhaustive temporary boundary test were removed.
  The high-tree literal loop now loads the two context bytes once per insert run
  and advances them in registers as literals are emitted, matching upstream's
  stateful context shape without changing block-switch or tree-selection rules.
  Existing LSB6/MSB6/UTF-8/signed context tests and the full upstream matrix pin
  behavior across context modes. Twenty fixed-CPU-2 complete-matrix pairs keep
  every checksum, improve `clustered_q8` by `1.0104x` with 20/20 wins, and
  improve the row-median geometric mean by `1.0044x`; every non-target median
  remains at or above `0.9942x`.
  Hoisting literal block state and context-map selection once per block-local
  insert chunk was rejected. It preserved the context-mode tests but added an
  outer chunk loop to predominantly short insert runs; twelve fixed-CPU-2 pairs
  all lost on `clustered_q8`, with a median near `0.987x`. The simpler per-byte
  block-boundary check remains faster.
  Summary instrumentation now also accounts decoded literal bytes by all four
  RFC context modes, and the reference gate checks that literal, LZ77, and
  static-dictionary bytes exactly cover each compressed benchmark payload. The
  locked `clustered_q8` stream has 16,741 literal bytes, all in UTF-8 mode. The
  high-tree decoder therefore preflights whether every declared literal block
  uses UTF-8 mode and, when true, bypasses the per-literal four-way mode switch
  while retaining the same two lookup tables. An exhaustive 65,536-byte-pair
  oracle pins the specialized context value against the generic implementation,
  and a classifier test covers homogeneous and mixed modes. Twenty fixed-CPU-2
  same-layout full-matrix pairs preserve all checksums, improve `clustered_q8`
  by `1.0138x` with 20/20 wins, and improve the row-median geometric mean by
  `1.0040x`; every non-target median remains at or above `0.9975x`.
  A compile-time UTF-8 dispatch was rejected: specializing a third copy of the
  roughly 1.5 KiB high-tree payload loop removed the per-literal mode branch but
  reduced `clustered_q8` to about `0.939x` in twelve same-layout pairs (0/12
  wins). The smaller single-loop runtime dispatch remains the better I-cache
  tradeoff.
  Caching the current literal block type and 64-entry context-map slice inside
  that single loop was rejected too. The existing per-byte block-switch check
  already optimizes well; twenty fixed-CPU-2 focused pairs measured about
  `0.996x` with only 1/20 wins, so the extra live state was removed.
  Building complex inline literal Huffman tables directly into their final
  header slots was rejected despite a real header-only gain. A caller-owned
  `initSparseTrustedInto` prototype preserved dense/sparse table oracles and
  improved twenty clustered header pairs by roughly 5--8%, but twenty complete
  decode-matrix pairs left `clustered_q8` neutral at `0.9987x` and regressed
  structured q4/q11 to `0.9626x`/`0.9388x`. The temporary shared API and
  Brotli routing were removed rather than optimizing a proxy stage at the cost
  of end-to-end decode.
  Returning embedded dictionary bytes directly for identity transforms was
  rejected as well. It removed one short scratch-to-output copy for transform
  zero and passed representative addresses across all word lengths, but twenty
  fixed-CPU-2 `clustered_q8` pairs fell to about `0.990x` with 0/20 wins. The
  extra transform branch/aliasing cost outweighed the avoided copy, so the
  decoder retains one uniform scratch contract for all 121 transforms.
  Writing high-tree static-dictionary transforms directly into the final output
  when at least 64 bytes remained was rejected too. Although it removed the
  subsequent 5--37-byte copy, twenty fixed-CPU-2 focused pairs measured about
  `0.984x` with 0/20 wins; growing the hot payload branch cost more than the
  tiny avoided copy. The stack scratch path remains unchanged.
  A Zstd `LiteralOnlySection` caller-owned return prototype was rejected after
  the `numbered_json` profile attributed roughly 31% of cycles to its 1,152-byte
  return copy. The copy disappeared and twenty five-row profile pairs improved
  geometrically by `1.0034x`, but the 5,161-sequence `huffman80k` control fell
  to `0.9790x` with 0/20 wins while `numbered_json` gained only `1.0076x`.
  The experiment was removed: a future ownership redesign must isolate the FSE
  execution layout instead of shifting every downstream hot function.
  Zstd sequence-table parsing now builds each compressed FSE table directly in
  `parseSequenceModeSpec`'s final local storage. This removes the three possible
  4 KiB builder-return copies while preserving the existing full-spec return and
  sequence-execution layout. A dirty-destination regression compares every
  reachable entry from two independently initialized caller-owned tables for the
  fixed libzstd `numbered_json` offset-FSE frame. Thirty alternating fixed-CPU-8
  five-row ReleaseFast pairs improve median decode time by `1.0301x` for
  `numbered_json`, `1.0083x` for `huffman80k`, `1.0115x` for 512 KiB JSON, and
  `1.0091x` for mixed binary; the zero-sequence ASCII control is neutral at
  `0.9988x`, for a `1.0139x` row-median geometric mean. A separate twenty-pair,
  100,000-decode run confirms `numbered_json` at `1.0251x` and `huffman80k` at
  `1.0079x`. Broader variants that also returned the whole 12 KiB mode spec
  through caller storage or made the generic cursor borrow its tables were
  rejected: despite roughly `1.36x` target gains, they regressed the 5,161-
  sequence `huffman80k` row to `0.944x`--`0.965x`. A dedicated mode-`0x20`
  execution branch was rejected too because unrelated `huffman80k` and mixed-
  binary rows fell to about `0.978x` and `0.991x`.
  Extending the existing linear FSE-table builder from 256/512-state tables to
  the 32/64/128-state tiers was also rejected. Exact table oracles covered all
  added widths and the first twenty-pair matrix looked mildly positive, but the
  longer fixed-CPU rerun was neutral: `numbered_json` had only 10/20 wins with
  a `1.0019x` median (`0.9974x` geometric mean), while `huffman80k` had 6/20
  wins at `0.9984x`. The compact sorted constructor remains preferable for
  small tables; the linear implementation stays limited to 256/512 states.
  Removing the apparently redundant by-value `SequenceModeSpec` argument from
  the two existing large-sequence helpers was rejected after inspecting the
  generated `0x3060`-byte entry copy. Although the candidate reduced both helper
  stack frames by roughly 12 KiB and improved `numbered_json`/large JSON by
  about `1.051x`/`1.026x`, twenty fixed-CPU-8 complete-matrix pairs reduced the
  5,161-sequence `huffman80k` median to `0.9095x` with only 2/20 wins. The local
  by-value copy evidently gives the long FSE loop materially better table
  locality/code generation than repeatedly reaching through the embedded
  cursor state, so the helper contract remains unchanged.
  Compacting only `SequenceModeSpec.offset_fse` from 512 entries to the
  specification's 256-state OF maximum was rejected too. The cross-block table
  state stayed full-width and conversions were bounded to Repeat_Mode restore
  and continuation commit, but twenty fixed-CPU-8 complete-matrix pairs still
  put the all-FSE `huffman80k` row at `0.9749x` with 0/20 wins. The target
  `numbered_json` row improved to `1.0735x` and large JSON to `1.0407x`, but
  those gains do not justify a stable regression in the main sequence-heavy
  control; the uniform decode-table layout remains.
  Shrinking `decodeFseTable`'s normalized-count scratch from 256 entries to the
  53-symbol maximum of sequence alphabets was rejected despite preserving all
  downstream hot-function addresses and sizes. The helper's stack frame fell by
  400 bytes, but thirty fixed-CPU-8 complete-matrix pairs improved the row-
  median geometric mean by only `1.0012x`; a longer 100,000-decode target run
  put `numbered_json` at `0.9956x` with only 7/20 wins. The generic scratch stays
  in place because the change is below the retention threshold.
  Extending `resolveSequenceModeSpec`'s early return from all-predefined tables
  to every mode tuple without Repeat_Mode was rejected. The shortcut is
  semantically valid and a direct mixed-mode test preserved the missing-prior-
  table error for Repeat_Mode, but it grew the inlined decode body by 48 bytes.
  Thirty fixed-CPU-8 complete-matrix pairs left `numbered_json` at only
  `1.0055x` and reduced `binary_mixed` to `0.9887x` with 5/30 wins. The narrower
  all-predefined early return retains the better overall layout.
  Extending unchecked FSE state lookup from the two specialized large-sequence
  loops into the generic sequence dispatcher was rejected. Initial states and
  transitions are already range-proven, but removing the three cold checks
  shortened the inlined decode body by 80 bytes and shifted downstream helpers.
  Thirty fixed-CPU-8 complete-matrix pairs put `huffman80k` at `0.9920x` with
  only 4/30 wins and left `numbered_json` neutral at `0.9992x`; the checked
  generic path remains the better measured layout.
  The compact FSE builder now replaces per-symbol stable sorting with a 32-bit
  state mask for tableLog-5 tables. Spread positions are unique, so clearing
  the least-significant set bit enumerates the exact ascending order without a
  general sort; 64/128-state tables retain the original sorted construction and
  256/512-state tables retain the established linear builder. A deterministic
  oracle compares 3,328 valid randomized 32-state distributions entry-for-entry
  against the independent linear implementation. Thirty alternating fixed-CPU-8
  complete-matrix pairs improve `numbered_json` by a median `1.0206x` with
  21/30 wins; `huffman80k`, 512 KiB JSON, mixed binary, and the zero-sequence
  ASCII control remain neutral to positive at their medians. Twenty longer
  target pairs confirm `numbered_json` at `1.0263x` with 17/20 wins, while the
  `huffman80k` control remains neutral at `0.9996x`. A fixed-counter run also
  reduces target instructions by about 2.0% and cycles by about 1.5%.
  Replacing only the all-FSE/Huffman helper's embedded-table cursor with the
  small streaming cursor was rejected as well. The helper still received its
  by-value local table copy, but changing cursor field offsets and caller layout
  reduced `huffman80k` to `0.9460x` and the unchanged FSE/FSE/RLE
  `binary_mixed` row to `0.9301x`, both with 0/30 wins. The specialized helpers
  therefore keep the established full `SequenceDecodeState` layout.
  Keeping that layout but delaying its embedded-spec assignment until after the
  two specialized sequence branches was rejected too. The specialized helpers
  retained their original local table copy and stack layout, yet the changed
  caller grew by 208 bytes and thirty fixed-CPU-8 complete-matrix pairs reduced
  `huffman80k` to `0.9748x`, `binary_mixed` to `0.9888x`, and `numbered_json`
  to `0.9884x`. Eager cursor construction remains.
  Skipping the otherwise unused Huffman-tree state commit on a terminal block
  was rejected. A retention-aware parser preserved multi-block treeless reuse
  and left the inlined `decodeFrameInto` size unchanged, but thirty fixed-CPU-8
  complete-matrix pairs reduced `huffman80k` to `0.9208x` and `binary_mixed` to
  `0.9426x`, both with 0/30 wins; the additional parser entry disturbed the
  surrounding hot layout more than the roughly 1 KiB saved copy.
  Moving the complete compressed-block decoder behind a `noinline` boundary
  was not worthwhile by itself. It reduced the caller's generated body from
  roughly 14.6 KiB to 2 KiB and improved 512 KiB JSON by `1.0203x`, but thirty
  fixed-CPU-8 complete-matrix pairs left `numbered_json` at `0.9939x` and the
  row-median geometric mean at only `1.0018x`. The standalone boundary was
  removed; it remains useful only as a controlled isolation mechanism for a
  future tree-builder experiment with a substantially larger local gain.
  Combining that full compressed-block isolation with the previously rejected
  rank-count/rank-start Huffman decoder was measured under matched 4 KiB-aligned
  dispatcher and sequence-helper sections. Against an equivalently isolated
  baseline, thirty fixed-CPU-8 pairs improved `numbered_json` by `1.4898x`,
  `ascii64k` by `1.0340x`, and 512 KiB JSON by `1.0269x`, while `huffman80k`
  and mixed binary stayed slightly positive. However, the actual production
  combination versus unisolated `HEAD` still reduced `huffman80k` to `0.8976x`
  and mixed binary to `0.9379x`; the section placement cost dominates those raw-
  literal sequence kernels. The prototype and isolation remain rejected until
  the decoder can be partitioned without changing their cache placement.
  Zstd level-1 large-block arbitration now screens the legacy single-duplicate
  fallback with a conservative Huffman lower bound before rebuilding a complete
  literal tree for every indexed match candidate. When the remaining low-byte
  literals need at least as many one-bit code bytes as the current winner, the
  one-sequence candidate cannot win even before its omitted headers and sequence
  bits. Inputs containing high bytes retain the exact former path because their
  indexed score has a deliberately conservative raw-literal shortcut. A
  64-shape, 8--32 KiB low/mixed/high-entropy oracle compares the production
  selector with the forced complete search byte-for-byte, and a separate score
  oracle checks competitive indexed winners. In a same-binary, alternating
  fixed-CPU-8 30-pair matrix, all 20 case/level rows retained their output sizes
  and checksums; level-1 JSON improved by a median `1.1548x` with 29/30 wins,
  while the weakest non-target row was `0.9964x`. The final ReleaseFast gate
  keeps its 640-byte JSON frame; an isolated fixed-CPU production run reported
  about 24.0 MiB/s versus the prior 20.6 MiB/s baseline. All 20 encode rows,
  91 stage rows, and 273 bidirectional libzstd 1.5.5 cases pass.
  The lower-bound scan now derives the minimum match length needed to beat the
  current winner and stops once later source positions cannot reach it. It
  returns to exact scoring as soon as any predecessor can meet that threshold,
  while high-byte inputs retain the existing conservative fallback. Sixteen
  generated 8 KiB blocks compare the threshold result against the previous
  full maximum-match scan across eight winner limits, and the existing 64-case
  selector oracle remains byte-exact against disabling the bound entirely. A
  same-binary 30-pair 20-row matrix preserves every size/checksum and improves
  level-1 JSON by `1.0773x` with 30/30 wins; non-level-1 rows remain within
  about 0.7% noise.
  Deferring the complete level-1 duplicate index behind a smaller exact-key
  threshold prefilter was rejected. The prefilter retained the bounded index's
  sampled candidates and conservatively fell back on high-byte, capacity,
  or uncertain cases; its oracle proved every prefilter prune was also pruned
  by the complete indexed scan. A production profile removed the former
  `DuplicateMatchIndex.buildBounded` entry (about 12% of sampled cycles), but
  the prefilter plus long-match extension consumed about 14% instead. A
  same-binary 30-pair 20-row matrix preserved every wire/checksum but reduced
  level-1 JSON to `0.9898x` with only 4/30 wins, so eager bounded construction
  remains.
  Expanding repeat-beam's indexed collision guard from its existing fourth-byte
  check to a complete four-byte prefix was rejected. The minimum-three path
  retained the old guard, a mismatch-position oracle covered all four prefix
  bytes, and thirty fixed-CPU-8 primary-stage pairs preserved every counter and
  wire. Text/JSON were neutral at about `0.9994x`, while binary consistently
  fell to `0.9886x` with 0/30 wins: the 4,096-bucket four-byte hash already
  correlates the other prefix bytes, so the wider load did not pay for itself.
  Pruning repeat-beam's second indexed transition when it targeted the same
  `(position, rep0, token)` at an equal-or-higher modeled cost was rejected. A
  16-shape, minimum-match-3/4 oracle showed byte-identical tokens and statistics.
  A runtime-switch 30-pair stage matrix appeared positive (`1.031x` text,
  `1.021x` JSON, `1.015x` binary), but independent final binaries exposed the
  code-layout cost: the best of three cost-comparison formulations reduced JSON
  to `0.987x` with 0/30 wins, while earlier forms fell to about `0.960x`. The
  original duplicate update remains faster once benchmark branching is removed.
  Automatic native-frame arbitration now bounds the delayed raw/RLE shape scan
  by the already-materialized compressed-frame length. Before the first
  qualifying 12-byte run, every consumed byte is irrevocably raw; once the
  frame header, checksum trailer, one raw-block header, and that prefix exceed
  the compressed candidate, the raw/RLE contender cannot win and scanning stops.
  Equal lengths still complete exact inspection and preserve raw-on-equal ties.
  A 24-shape oracle covering random, structured, narrow-alphabet, mixed, RLE,
  four block boundaries, checksum on/off, and nine winner limits verifies that
  every early exit corresponds to a strictly larger exact raw/RLE frame. Thirty
  alternating fixed-CPU-8 pairs against an independent `HEAD` binary preserve
  all 20 frame sizes/checksums and improve text by `4.62x`, level-1 JSON/binary/
  tradeoff/multiblock by `1.029x`/`1.042x`/`1.102x`/`1.019x`; every row median
  is positive.
  Reusing repeat-beam's existing four-byte predecessor chain to replace level
  one's separate single-match index was rejected. A generated oracle proved its
  negative result conservatively implied the complete eight-byte index bound,
  but walking full collision chains and validating long matches cost more than
  the 1.3 MiB bounded-index write it removed: a same-binary 100-encode JSON
  sample fell to `0.743x`. The prototype was stopped before a full matrix.
  Splitting repeat-beam index construction into a branch-free four-byte-anchor
  body plus a three-slot sentinel tail was rejected as compiler-neutral. The
  existing compact-index/reference oracle remained exact, but thirty independent
  `HEAD` stage pairs measured text/JSON/binary at `0.995x`/`0.999x`/`1.000x`.
  LLVM already makes the optional tail check effectively free in this loop.
  Switching only repeat-beam's 4-byte hash from Vort's current middle product
  bits to upstream zstd's high-product-bit formula was rejected. All locked
  stage counters and wires stayed equal, but thirty independent `HEAD` pairs
  measured text/JSON/binary at `0.976x`/`0.994x`/`1.004x`; the upstream hash's
  small binary gain did not offset regressions on narrow structured inputs.
  Packing four lazy match-length validity bits into each duplicate predecessor
  count was rejected. It removed per-candidate sentinel writes without growing
  `DuplicateMatchIndex`, and the bounded/full index oracle preserved all
  predecessors and selected matches. Binary index construction improved
  `1.033x`, but text/JSON builds fell to `0.994x`/`0.993x`; more importantly,
  thirty independent stage pairs reduced actual text/JSON/binary single-match
  evaluation to `0.985x`/`0.980x`/`0.963x`. The simple u16 sentinel stays.
  Moving `max_byte_frequency` from the duplicate-index input loop to a final
  256-counter reduction was rejected despite improving isolated bounded-index
  construction by `1.076x`/`1.053x`/`1.030x` on text/JSON/binary. The actual
  single-match stage was mixed, and thirty independent full-matrix pairs reached
  only `1.0015x` geometrically: level-1 JSON was `1.0039x`, while text and the
  tradeoff corpus fell to `0.9908x`/`0.9979x`. The incremental maximum remains.
  The duplicate index now stores positions with non-empty predecessor buckets
  as one dense ascending array instead of writing a reverse-linked next-position
  entry for every source byte. Suffix queries binary-search their first legal
  position and then read the dense list sequentially, preserving candidate order
  and all match-score ties without increasing `DuplicateMatchIndex`. A 16-shape
  oracle independently reconstructs the dense list, checks lower-bound starts,
  compares full/bounded fields, and preserves selected matches at four suffixes.
  Thirty independent fixed-CPU-8 stage pairs improve bounded-index construction
  by `1.027x`/`1.011x`/`1.026x` on text/JSON/binary. The corresponding 30-pair
  20-row frame matrix preserves every size/checksum, improves level-1 JSON by
  `1.0138x` with 26/30 wins, has a `1.0012x` row-median geometric mean, and
  keeps the weakest control at `0.9956x`.
  The same index now stores each sampled predecessor and lazy match length in
  that dense row, replacing its sparse four-wide per-position tables. This also
  makes the established pair-sampling policy explicit instead of depending on
  a narrow inferred integer in the former packed state: each hash's first
  occurrence is retained, its second emits one row, and the process repeats. A
  16-shape oracle independently reconstructs every pair and keeps full/bounded
  queries equal; a 64-frame public-API audit is byte-identical to the prior
  implementation. `DuplicateMatchIndex` falls from about 1.32 MiB to less than
  384 KiB. Thirty fixed-CPU-8 stage pairs improve index construction by
  `1.428x`/`1.413x`/`1.347x` and single-match evaluation by `1.005x`/`1.049x`/
  `1.080x` on text/JSON/binary. A 30-pair 20-row independent-binary matrix
  preserves every size/checksum, improves level-1 JSON by `1.037x` with 29/30
  wins, and reaches a `1.0182x` row-median geometric mean with the weakest row
  at `0.9962x`. A true
  four-deep repair was not selected as the default: it improved 7/64 generated
  level-1 frames by only nine bytes total but reduced JSON level 1 to `0.892x`
  and levels 3/9/22 to about `0.629x`/`0.628x`/`0.627x`.
  A second attempt to defer level-1's duplicate index used a fixed-length
  64-bit rolling fingerprint rather than extending matches. Equal windows must
  share a fingerprint, while hash collisions, high bytes, and table saturation
  conservatively fell back to the indexed scorer; a generated oracle confirmed
  every negative proof against the complete scan. Even so, a same-binary
  100-encode JSON sample measured only `0.9756x`. Maintaining the rolling hash
  and open-addressed table still cost more than eager bounded-index construction.
  Replacing repeat-beam's one-element `matchesAt` output with a dedicated
  optional-return `firstMatchAt` helper was also rejected. A per-position oracle
  matched the old result, but thirty independent stage pairs reduced text/JSON/
  binary to `0.960x`/`0.941x`/`0.977x`; the generic slice/count form produces
  substantially better optimized code on the current compiler.
  Four-way striped byte-frequency collection inside `DuplicateMatchIndex` was
  rejected too. It preserved the full/bounded index oracle and improved isolated
  text/JSON index construction by only `1.007x`/`1.005x`, while binary fell to
  `0.993x`; actual JSON/binary single-match stages measured `0.991x`/`0.994x`.
  The extra four-lane merge and stack footprint outweigh the shorter dependency
  chains at this scale.
  Expanding repeat-beam's fixed two-state loop into separate slot-zero and
  optional slot-one calls was rejected. A 16-shape token/statistics oracle and
  same-binary stage pairs were positive (`1.014x` text, `1.020x` JSON, `1.031x`
  binary), but an independent-binary 30-pair 20-row matrix reached only
  `0.9995x` geometrically, improved level-1 JSON by just `1.0024x`, and reduced
  multiblock level 22 to `0.9798x`. The compact dynamic slice loop remains.
  Splitting repeat-beam's checked one-candidate lookup into a separate unchecked
  hot-loop helper was rejected. A per-position oracle preserved every returned
  match, but thirty independent primary-stage pairs reduced text/JSON/binary to
  `0.984x`/`0.952x`/`0.986x`; the extra helper boundary outweighed eliminating
  two already-predictable range checks.
  Caching each repeat-beam predecessor's complete four-byte hash key alongside
  its compact `u16` link was rejected. It avoided reloading candidate prefix
  bytes after hash collisions and preserved all locked stage outputs, but doubled
  predecessor-entry traffic; thirty independent stage pairs reduced text/JSON/
  binary to `0.953x`/`0.985x`/`0.967x`. The compact link-only index remains.
  Compacting the repeat-aware beam state was rejected after testing both natural
  layouts. Removing its reconstructible `Token` reduced the state from 16 to 12
  bytes and improved the isolated level-1 JSON beam by `1.026x` with 29/30 wins,
  but a 30-pair 20-row end-to-end matrix regressed the level-1/3 tradeoff corpus
  by about `1.4%`/`1.1%`. Packing the 1--258-byte backtrack length and prior
  two-state slot into one `u16` reduced each state to eight bytes, but the same
  isolated beam fell to `0.962x` with only 1/30 wins. The original 16-byte state
  remains; its power-of-two stride is evidently preferable to the saved traffic
  on the current x86-64 code generation.
  Level-1 duplicate arbitration now builds only the bounded pair-sampled
  predecessor rows consumed by its single-match search and Huffman lower bound.
  The full per-position hash chain is reserved for budgets that can enter mixed
  lookahead; writing it and clearing its 64 KiB latest-position table was dead
  work at level 1. A 16-shape oracle compares every bounded candidate position,
  predecessor, lazy-length field, and selected match against the full builder.
  The stage tool
  now receives the candidate's actual search budget so its `duplicate_index` row
  mirrors this production choice. Thirty alternating fixed-CPU-8 stage pairs
  improve index construction by a median `1.259x` with 30/30 wins. A same-binary
  30-pair 20-row frame matrix preserves every size/checksum, improves level-1
  JSON by `1.0267x` with 26/30 wins, and keeps the other nineteen medians within
  about 0.35% of control.
  Fusing repeat-beam's complete predecessor-index build into its forward DP was
  rejected. Because the DP visits positions monotonically, an online insert/
  lookup produced identical matches at every position across sixteen 32 KiB
  structured/copied inputs and all repeat-beam tests retained exact tokens.
  Nevertheless, thirty fixed-CPU-8 isolated JSON stage pairs measured only
  `0.9991x` with 13/30 wins; interleaving hash-table mutation into the hotter DP
  loop outweighed removing the separate linear prepass. The compact offline
  index remains.
  Reusing optimal's compile-time 32 KiB fixed-distance cost table in the repeat
  beam was rejected as below threshold. It exactly replaces the scalar `log2`
  formula and improved thirty isolated JSON stage pairs by `1.0248x` with 21/30
  wins, but a same-binary 30-pair 20-row frame matrix showed only `1.0033x`
  geometric mean and `1.0022x` on the target level-1 JSON row. All wires were
  identical and the weakest control was `0.9989x`; the marginal result does not
  justify another global lookup in the beam loop.
  Hoisting the indexed match's direct-distance cost out of repeat-beam's two-
  state loop was rejected too. A focused transition oracle matched the existing
  helper for repeat and direct offsets at minimum, typical, and maximum match
  lengths, but thirty fixed-CPU-8 isolated JSON stage pairs fell to `0.9785x`
  with only 12/30 wins. The extra live value/helper path costs more than the
  duplicated small integer `log2` calculation on this target.
  Hoisting repeat-beam's per-position fixed literal cost out of its two-state
  loop was rejected as well. Although the value is identical for both active
  states and all token tests stayed exact, thirty fixed-CPU-8 isolated JSON
  stage pairs fell to `0.9863x` with only 11/30 wins. The existing inlined
  expression gives LLVM the better hot-loop schedule.
  Running the level-1 repeat beam before greedy and skipping greedy for an
  absolute 1/32 beam result was rejected on correctness/ratio evidence before
  benchmarking. A generated 512-block audit found a deterministic 26,626-byte
  low-alphabet case where the 379-byte beam satisfied the threshold but the
  existing greedy-first arbitration emitted 375 bytes. The 1/32 rule therefore
  remains valid only for skipping the more expensive optimal parser after
  greedy has established its candidate; it is not a proof that beam dominates
  every linear parser.
  Replacing repeat-beam's 8 KiB head-table sentinel clear with a 512-byte
  initialized bitmap was rejected. All eight beam tests preserved exact tokens,
  but the extra bitmap load/branch/write at every indexed position reduced the
  isolated JSON stage to `0.9822x` with only 8/30 fixed-CPU-8 wins. The simple
  contiguous head clear remains cheaper than making the hot index-build loop
  conditional.
  Repeat-beam's explicit recent-offset probe now checks its four-byte minimum

  index oracle and all 19 beam tests remained exact, and thirty beam-stage pairs
  improved text/JSON/binary by `1.0084x`/`1.0070x`/`1.0118x`. The 20-row matrix
  fell to `0.9987x` geometrically, however, with text level 1 and JSON level 3 at
  `0.9920x`/`0.9919x`. The explicit defensive condition remains for better
  whole-encoder layout.
  Combining a full four-byte repeat-beam collision check with match extension
  starting after that verified prefix was rejected. This avoids rereading the
  prefix on true matches while filtering collisions earlier; a 259-boundary
  mismatch oracle, compact-index oracle, and all 20 beam tests stayed exact.
  Thirty primary-stage pairs nevertheless reduced text/JSON/binary to
  `0.9248x`/`0.9825x`/`0.9799x`. The cheap fourth-byte filter plus shared
  full-range matcher remains substantially better on current code generation.
  Returning immediately from `matchesAtZstd` after filling its fixed one-element
  output was rejected without changing the public/internal slice-and-count API.
  The compact-vs-generic index oracle and all 19 beam tests stayed exact, but
  thirty primary-stage pairs reduced text/JSON/binary to `0.9931x`/`0.9789x`/
  `0.9903x`; keeping the ordinary count increment and loop exit gives LLVM the
  better inlined beam body.
  Expanding only repeat-beam's indexed collision guard from the fourth byte to
  bytes two and three was rejected. Unlike the earlier full-u32-plus-tail
  experiment it retained the shared match extender from byte zero; an exhaustive
  mismatch oracle and all 20 beam tests stayed exact. Thirty primary-stage pairs
  were nevertheless `0.9991x`/`1.0032x`/`0.9958x` on text/JSON/binary, so even
  the extra 16-bit comparison does not repay its load on this hash distribution.
  Raising the already-16-byte `RepBeamState` size from natural four-byte to
  explicit 16-byte alignment was rejected. The benchmark hot function retained
  exactly the same address, size, and instruction count; only four allocator
  alignment immediates changed. Thirty primary beam-stage pairs were correspondingly
  neutral-to-negative at `0.9989x`/`0.9995x`/`0.9996x` for text/JSON/binary, so
  the natural alignment remains.
  A fixed-parameter Zstd-only double-fast instance was rejected too. It folded
  the constant four-byte minimum and 258-byte maximum while retaining only the
  block-dependent 32 KiB window; a 16-shape oracle matched generic tokens and
  statistics exactly, and all 12 focused tests passed. Thirty primary-stage
  pairs nevertheless measured JSON/binary at `0.9909x`/`0.9955x`, with text
  neutral and only wide input at `1.0025x`. The generic options path remains.
  The large sequence-free four-stream Huffman decoder now carries the existing
  `buildComplete` proof into its bulk loop and reads the proven-initialized
  lookup entries directly. Incomplete or hostile trees still use the checked
  lookup path, while the common valid path avoids constructing an optional and
  testing its validity bit for every symbol. Nine alternating fixed-CPU-2
  independent-binary pairs on the 64 KiB printable-ASCII frame improved median
  caller-buffer decode from `794.69` to `831.65` MiB/s (`1.0465x`, 9/9 wins).
  Hardware counters over five repeats reported about 10.2% fewer instructions,
  55.6% fewer branches, and 4.6% fewer cycles. A five-pair 13-row matrix improved
  `1.0051x` geometrically; its weakest control was the raw-literal/FSE
  `huffman80k` row at `0.9924x`, while `large_json` improved `1.0081x`. All 65
  focused Huffman tests, the full root test/check builds, 237-case native frame
  probe, 273-case libzstd 1.5.5 compatibility matrix, and all six upstream
  decodecorpus campaigns remained green (5,400 frames and all 64 LL/OF/ML mode
  tuples).
  A follow-up compact X1 lookup indexed at the tree's actual width was rejected
  after three placements. It consistently improved the same `ascii64k` target
  by roughly `1.068x`--`1.087x` over the validated direct-entry baseline, but
  embedding the path reduced `numbered_json` to `0.8965x`; isolating the helper
  and then isolating both Huffman decode bodies still left `numbered_json` near
  `0.901x`. The narrowest call-site dispatch retained `1.0680x` on `ascii64k`
  but produced a `0.9888x` 13-row geometric mean, with `numbered_json`,
  `huffman80k`, `large_json`, and `large_text` at `0.8945x`/`0.9643x`/
  `0.9677x`/`0.9644x`. The extra decoder instance and dispatch were removed;
  future compact-table work needs whole-decoder layout control rather than
  another local helper placement.
  Replacing exact `memcpy` for non-overlapping Zstd matches of at most 16 bytes
  with explicit first/tail 8/4/2-byte loads and stores was rejected as well. A
  generated oracle covered every match length 1...16 and every legal distance
  through 32 after first exposing and correcting a 15-byte tail bug in an
  earlier additive implementation. Despite exact output and 81 focused sequence
  tests, nine fixed-CPU-2 `numbered_json` pairs reduced median caller-buffer
  decode from about `179.2` to `159.8` MiB/s (`0.892x`). The compiler/runtime
  `memcpy` path remains preferable for exact bounded copies.
  A fresh upstream `decodecorpus` campaign (seed `104729`, 2,000 frames) exposed
  a public sequence-inspector state bug that did not affect actual decode:
  replay stopped after reporting an all-Predefined sequence block without
  retaining those active tables, so a later block using Repeat_Mode was rejected
  as corrupt. Inspection now commits predefined tables before returning its
  summary. A compact two-block regression pins Predefined-to-Repeat replay, and
  the exact 925-byte upstream seed `3157610632` frame is retained as a fixture;
  it checks seven-block structure, the Predefined/Repeat/compressed transitions,
  3,047 decoded bytes, and CRC-32 `0xdf866e7a`. Two further fresh plain/dictionary
  campaigns (seeds `1618033` and `271828`, 3,000 frames total) also pass.
  A forced-compressed 1 KiB-block campaign (seed `130363`, 1,000 frames) then
  exposed an incremental direct-output boundary: a 46-byte frame containing six
  compressed blocks that regenerate zero bytes returned `need_output` for the
  caller's necessarily empty output slice and could accept the frame after its
  first block. The direct path now allows zero-output compressed blocks to run
  without output capacity and advances whenever the current block is non-final,
  independently of cumulative decoded length. A regression generated from the
  exact standalone seed `1066298653` covers complete direct decoding, deliberate
  corruption of the second block after preflight, and 3-byte-input block
  streaming under a 16-byte compressed-buffer limit. The complete 1,000-frame
  forced campaign now passes one-shot and incremental decoding. The established
  273-case libzstd 1.5.5 matrix, 237-case native frame probe, and six-campaign
  5,400-frame suite remain green.
  Auditing the LZ4 probe found that its 63 cases labeled `lib-generated` still
  called Vort's dependency-free frame encoder after the runtime system-codec
  facade had been removed. The test-only liblz4 wrapper now dynamically loads
  `LZ4F_compressFrameBound`, `LZ4F_compressFrame`, and `LZ4F_decompress`; no
  system dependency is added to the Vort library. The public probe now covers
  120 real liblz4-generated frames across levels 0/3/10, all four block-size
  IDs, linked/independent modes, content/block checksums, omitted content size,
  empty and generated payloads, and a 300 KiB multi-block case. Every frame is
  decoded through Vort's one-shot, caller-buffer, reusable, chunked, and
  incremental APIs, and each matching Vort-produced frame is independently
  decoded by liblz4. The probe reports the runtime liblz4 version; CI installs
  `liblz4-dev` explicitly so missing reference coverage cannot silently pass.
  The equivalent Snappy audit found that the existing runtime comparison was
  performance-oriented and one-way: both decoders consumed only Vort-generated
  raw blocks, with no libsnappy-generated input and no framed-stream coverage.
  A shared test-only runtime facade now loads `snappy_compress`,
  `snappy_uncompress`, `snappy_max_compressed_length`,
  `snappy_uncompressed_length`, and `snappy_validate_compressed_buffer`. The new
  required probe covers eight payload shapes in both raw-block directions,
  including empty, 64 KiB incompressible, and 160 KiB multi-chunk data. Copy
  tokens must occur in both encoders' outputs, and both decoders must reject a
  truncated form of every reference block. Genuine libsnappy blocks are
  wrapped in standard masked-CRC-32C framed chunks and
  decoded through Vort's one-shot, exact-size caller-buffer, split-input, and
  incremental APIs; every compressed block in matching Vort frames is also
  validated and decoded by libsnappy. CI installs `libsnappy-dev`, while the
  production library remains dependency-free.
  A follow-up audit found that `run-zstd-decodecorpus-gate` accumulated the
  compat probe's global sequence-mode mask, which also included its fixed 273
  built-in cases, rather than a mask attributable solely to the generated
  corpus. The probe now tracks and reports separate `decodecorpus_*` maximums,
  sequence-count tiers, and LL/OF/ML mode masks; the gate carries only that
  corpus-specific mask between campaigns. Three new deterministic campaigns add
  2,000 forced content-sized RLE frames (seed `32452843`), 2,000 raw frames with
  blocks capped at eight bytes (seed `49979693`), and 500 compressed frames with
  blocks capped at 16 bytes (seed `67867979`). The last campaign independently
  reaches all 64 sequence-mode tuples in 500 frames, with up to 1,045 blocks per
  frame. Together with the prior six campaigns, the reproducible upstream suite
  now contains 9,900 byte-exact one-shot and incremental decode cases.
  The test-only libzstd loader now also accepts an explicit shared-library path,
  and the compat/decodecorpus drivers expose `--libzstd PATH` so cross-version
  evidence cannot be redirected silently by the platform loader. After building
  `~/Work/zstd/lib/libzstd.so` from commit `5233c58e`, the complete 273-case
  compatibility matrix passes with zero unsupported frames against upstream
  libzstd 1.6.0 as well as the system libzstd 1.5.5. The corpus gate records
  both the explicit path and actual `ZSTD_versionString`, and requires one
  stable version across all campaigns.
  A q3-fast adaptive lazy-parser experiment was rejected despite materially
  better compression. For 1,024--4,096-byte inputs it performed one-step lazy
  lookahead only when the current match was three bytes; a specialized probe
  proved the next position had a four-byte match without finding its complete
  length. Token/stat oracles showed that probe was equivalent to the complete
  lazy search for the selected policy, reusable-scratch tests passed, and the
  fast JSON/source/log rows shrank from 92/130/113 bytes to 62/91/83 bytes
  (libbrotli q3: 62/86/87). However, twenty-one alternating ReleaseFast pairs
  on fixed CPU 8, using independent baseline and candidate binaries, measured
  only `0.6187x`/`0.6340x`/`0.5927x` median throughput versus the existing fast
  parser. Their geometric mean was `0.6149x`, far below the `0.8x` retention
  threshold. Five non-target controls kept identical sizes and reached a
  `0.9790x` median-ratio geometric mean (`0.9669x` floor; 32 KiB source
  `0.9945x`). The length dispatch, lazy limit, specialized lookahead, scratch
  API, and tests were removed; future q3 size work must avoid a second hash-chain
  traversal on the fast path.
  A Zstd level-1 narrow-JSON double-fast shortcut was also rejected after four
  progressively smaller routing layouts. The motivating 32,797-byte NDJSON row
  moved from the 643-byte single-state result to a 694-byte double-fast frame,
  still 17.2% smaller than libzstd 1.5.5's 838 bytes, while 31-pair fixed-CPU-8
  ReleaseFast runs improved throughput by roughly `5.6x` with 31/31 wins. A
  64-case JSON/log/source/CSV audit kept every non-target wire exact; a separate
  24-case target family selected 11 blocks behind a 44:1 compressed-size rule,
  with each selected block within 12.5% of complete level-1 arbitration. Eight
  real JSON/source/configuration files also retained exact sizes and measured a
  `1.0012x` median-ratio geometric mean with a `0.9951x` floor. Nevertheless,
  integrating the shortcut changed whole-binary code placement: the best final
  layouts left repetitive text level 1 near `0.975x`, and one layout reduced
  multiblock level 22 to `0.9845x`. Exact single-state wire validation erased
  the target gain, and section isolation did not restore all controls, so all
  production routing and oracle code was removed. The Zstd encode benchmark's
  new repeatable `--path` and bounded `--limit` inputs remain for future real-file
  experiments using the same measurement and bidirectional-decode harness.
  The native Zstd candidate-stage benchmark now accepts the same repeatable
  `--path` and `--limit` inputs, and records `input_bytes` in every row so a
  truncated real-file run is self-describing. Its dedicated smoke covers two
  files, stable names, exact truncation, case/candidate/stage filtering, the CSV
  schema, empty input, a zero limit, and unknown arguments. Profiling the first
  128 KiB of Ghostty's `Terminal.zig` through this surface attributes the level-1
  primary bottleneck to the exact optimal candidate: 31,739 encoded bytes at
  roughly 18.45 ms/block, versus greedy's 34,304 bytes at 5.50 ms/block and
  double-fast's 39,648 bytes at 3.65 ms/block. This provides a reproducible
  real-source target for exact-wire optimal-parser work instead of relying only
  on synthetic 32 KiB rows.
  A Zstd level-1-only four-byte optimal hash anchor was evaluated and rejected.
  A 128-shape, 4--124 KiB oracle proved that modeled cost never rose, improved
  at least once, replayed every token stream, and retained consistent
  statistics; 128 KiB boundary and allocation-failure tests also passed. On
  CPU 8, eleven interleaved ReleaseFast pairs over five source files and all
  twelve Silesia 128 KiB prefixes improved the isolated optimal stage by
  `1.374x` geometrically (`1.125x` floor, 17/17 wins), while aggregate candidate
  size fell from 695,449 to 694,776 bytes. Fifteen complete-frame pairs over
  Ghostty `Terminal.zig` and the twelve Silesia prefixes improved `1.163x`
  geometrically (`1.0017x` floor, 13/13 wins), with aggregate output falling
  from 606,640 to 606,193 bytes; Terminal itself improved `1.217x` and shrank
  from 31,748 to 31,718 bytes. However, even after restricting the route to
  blocks above 64 KiB and moving the new parser/emitter behind independent
  noinline sections, a 21-pair, 512-iteration short-text control fell to
  `0.9807x` at level 1 and about `0.987--0.988x` at levels 3/9/22 despite
  byte-identical output. The stable non-target/layout regression violates the
  `0.99x` control floor, so the production code and proposal-specific tests
  were fully removed rather than exchanging broad latency for one large-block
  gain.
  Zstd's five performance executables now emit self-contained provenance with
  every CSV row: exact input and executable SHA-256, ReleaseFast mode, Zig
  version, target architecture/OS/ABI/CPU, host CPU model, process affinity and
  CPU count, outer benchmark thread count, codec-internal thread policy, and a
  percent-encoded command line. Decode reference/profile builds are now pinned
  to ReleaseFast just like encode/stage/schedule instead of inheriting a Debug
  default. Each gate requires one consistent provenance tuple and verifies the
  executable digest against the exact build artifact; the two path smokes also
  recompute truncated-input hashes and compare inherited affinity. The unified
  competitor report advances to schema v2, retains per-metric input hashes,
  exposes per-source provenance, and distinguishes partial coverage from the
  all-loaded-sources condition. Its initial 63-check smoke covered partial and complete
  provenance plus missing columns, inconsistent rows, Debug data, invalid CPU
  counts, unsafe commands, and malformed executable/input hashes.
  The same capture code is now a codec-neutral build module used by the formal
  LZ4, Snappy, Brotli encode, and Brotli decode comparison executables as well
  as Zstd. Those four builds are pinned to ReleaseFast, append exact per-case
  input hashes and the common provenance tuple, and pass their exact Zig
  artifact to the gate for an independent executable SHA-256 check. A shared
  Python validator keeps the provenance rules identical across the four gates;
  its initial 13-check smoke covered positive validation, cross-row inconsistency,
  artifact tampering, malformed hashes, CPU affinity ranges/counts, thread
  policy, and CSV-safe commands. The unified report smoke now performs 64
  checks, and a fixed-CPU-8 real report contains 274 metrics in 25 groups with
  all 134 metrics from the six Zig benchmark sources carrying input hashes.
  Provenance coverage is therefore 6/8 rather than the prior 2/8. The two
  remaining Deflate inputs use Python orchestration, a Vort executable, and a
  generated Cargo release runner over local fdeflate/miniz_oxide sources; they
  must use a verifiable artifact-set manifest in the next slice instead of
  misleadingly assigning the existing single-executable digest to only one
  component.
  Deflate encode/decode now close that final evidence gap with provenance v2.
  Both helpers are pinned to ReleaseFast and expose a machine-readable
  `--benchmark-provenance` record; each Python harness builds its Cargo release
  runner once with `-C target-cpu=native` and executes the stable binary
  directly. A canonical artifact-set manifest covers ten independently
  revalidated inputs: the Python driver, interpreter and shared provenance/
  corpus modules; the Vort helper; generated Rust source and release binary;
  and complete fdeflate/miniz_oxide source trees with commit and dirty state.
  The formal gates validate the full 210-row encode and 120-row decode matrices,
  exact per-case input hashes, repeat counts, and recomputed elapsed seconds,
  throughput, and encode ratios. The unified report is schema v3, requires
  provenance in its formal build step, rejects cross-source environment
  mismatches, and now reports 8/8 consistent sources with all 274 normalized
  metrics carrying input SHA-256. Shared provenance smoke coverage is 23 checks
  and competitor-report smoke coverage is 77 checks. A separate 15-check
  Deflate matrix smoke covers duplicate/missing rows, input hashes, repeat
  counts, elapsed nanoseconds, throughput, and ratio derivation without a long
  benchmark run. The formal unified-report build now depends on all eight
  benchmark gates; use fixed affinity with `-j1` so it cannot consume stale
  artifacts or overlap benchmark producers.
  The Deflate decode comparison now uses `std.heap.c_allocator` for Vort's
  timed owned-result rows, matching the process allocator used by Rust `Vec` on
  the Linux benchmark host; both policies are recorded in the v2 manifest. The
  prior `init.gpa` helper reached the page allocator and made stored-block
  allocation look like a codec gap even though caller-buffer decode was already
  far ahead. Thirty fixed-CPU-8 interleaved pairs against the frozen page-backed
  helper preserve every checksum and improve stored raw alloc/exact by
  `11.5891x`/`11.7149x`, zlib alloc/exact by `6.3570x`/`6.3776x`, and gzip
  alloc/exact by `1.6844x`/`1.6861x`. The no-allocation raw/zlib/gzip controls
  remain near neutral at `0.9904x`/`1.0109x`/`1.0102x`, confirming the change
  corrects allocator methodology rather than claiming a codec-core speedup.
  Reusing repeat-beam's previous indexed match length at the next position was
  evaluated and rejected. The reuse is exact only when the next predecessor is
  the previous candidate plus one and the prior match ended at a real mismatch
  rather than the 258-byte or input-tail cap. That condition covered about
  89.8% of indexed JSON matches and 96.9% of binary matches, but only 0.68% of
  text matches because 99.3% of those hit the maximum length. All 15 focused
  repeat-beam tests and every stage/frame byte/checksum remained exact. The
  first cached-Match form improved 11-pair isolated JSON/binary stages by
  `1.1103x`/`1.0546x` while text fell to `0.9505x`; its 30-pair complete
  20-row matrix reached `1.0090x` by row-median geometric mean, but level-1
  JSON improved only `1.0061x` and binary level 1 was `0.9925x`. A compact
  next-candidate/next-length form measured `1.0996x`/`1.0690x` for JSON/binary
  stages, but an 11-pair full matrix reached only `1.0036x` and reduced text
  levels 1/22 to `0.9858x`/`0.9867x`. Both forms were removed: the extra cache
  state and branch perturb production rows that cannot use the recurrence, and
  the target gain does not clear the 1% retention bar.
  The corrected allocator benchmark exposed a real `overlap-rle` inflate gap,
  and a bitstream audit found a new boundary distinct from the rejected
  semantic-table, global fill, batch-four, and run-grouping attempts. The final
  dynamic block has exactly one literal plus EOB and length 258 in a complete
  `2/2/1` literal tree, and exactly distance symbols zero/one in a `1/1` tree.
  Those canonical codes make every payload token two bits. Caller-buffer raw,
  zlib, and gzip decode now proves that complete shape from the existing compact
  table before building the 9-bit literal or 8-bit distance fast table, then
  consumes the four possible tokens in an isolated final-block loop. The route
  requires no dictionary and non-overlapping input/output; all other stream and
  reader shapes retain the generic path. Tests cover policy rejection,
  distance-one and distance-two tokens, invalid initial matches, exact/short
  output, truncation, reader-state equivalence, and full dynamic-frame token replay;
  Python zlib independently decodes the raw/zlib/gzip fixtures to the same
  32 KiB SHA-256. Thirty fixed-CPU-8 interleaved independent-binary pairs gave
  target caller-buffer medians of `3.8339x/4.6415x/3.7848x`, all 30/30 wins.
  Thirty non-target codec/API row medians had a `1.0081x` geometric mean and
  `0.9972x` floor. A separate alloc/exact/into target matrix won all 270 pairs.
  Formal repeat-3 throughput reaches `10,992.78/21,480.23 MiB/s` for Vort zlib
  alloc/into versus `7,257.16` for fdeflate, and
  `13,356.35/34,052.81 MiB/s` for Vort raw alloc/into versus `6,988.75` for
  miniz_oxide raw; only the owned-result rows are direct allocator-semantic
  comparisons.
  Profiled the remaining Zstd `binary_mixed` caller-buffer gap against the
  fixed-CPU ReleaseFast decode profile. Its four compressed blocks are not one
  uniform first-block shape: block zero is raw-literal FSE/FSE/RLE with 2,044
  sequences, while blocks one through three are raw-literal FSE/RLE/RLE with
  2,048 sequences each. Hardware counters measured roughly 2.65 billion cycles,
  12.56 billion instructions, and only 0.24% branch misses across 5,000 decodes;
  the call graph attributed the dominant cost to the generic reverse-bit/FSE
  sequence loop, not match copying. A dedicated FSE/RLE/RLE raw-literal loop
  removed per-sequence mode dispatch and unused OF/ML state updates while
  preserving checked literal/match boundaries, repeat offsets, terminal bits,
  and retained tables. A direct generic-versus-specialized oracle covered output,
  state, short output, and an invalid offset. Twenty target pairs initially
  improved by a `1.3285x` median with 20/20 wins. However, three dispatch/layout
  forms all failed the independent 13-row reference matrix: the first reached
  `1.3494x` on `binary_mixed` but reduced tiny to `0.9758x`; section-isolating
  the helper reached `1.3815x` but reduced `huffman80k` to `0.9744x` with 0/30
  wins; preserving both existing fast dispatches byte-for-byte and appending a
  cold new condition still left `huffman80k` at `0.9796x` with 1/30 wins while
  the target reached `1.3402x`. All production and oracle code was removed. A
  future FSE/RLE/RLE optimization needs a dispatch boundary that demonstrably
  preserves the generic raw-literal all-FSE loop's placement; do not repeat the
  three local-condition layouts above.
  A Brotli high-tree regular-distance reservoir fusion was evaluated and
  rejected. The candidate combined the existing fast reader's refill,
  extra-bit extraction, and RFC distance arithmetic behind one out-of-line
  boundary. A temporary exhaustive oracle covered all four NPOSTFIX values,
  every encodable NDIRECT value, every regular distance symbol, zero/maximum/
  mixed extra values, all eight starting bit alignments, exact cursor advance,
  and one-bit-short truncation. Returning the distance through the error union
  was slightly negative on the target. A caller-owned result variant improved
  fifteen fixed-CPU-2 independent-binary `clustered_q8` pairs by `1.0067x` at
  the median with 15/15 wins, but the complete 13-row matrix reduced ordinary
  structured decode to `0.9908x`. Placing the helper in a dedicated ELF text
  section still produced only a `1.0069x` target median and left structured at
  `0.9906x`, with several q3/q11 controls around `0.993x`--`0.997x`. Every
  candidate preserved encoded size and checksum, and the formal libbrotli gate
  passed, but the target gain was below 1% and the control regression violated
  the established floor. The helper, routing, and oracle were removed; retain
  the shared regular-distance path until a design changes more than its call
  boundary or code placement.
  A Brotli ratio-mode three-type literal entropy split was also evaluated and
  rejected. The proposal refined an already-profitable two-way split into three
  consecutive regions, then retained the candidate only when its complete wire
  image beat the selected baseline. Temporary direct and ratio-path tests
  covered exact `2048/4096` boundaries over three disjoint 16-symbol alphabets;
  the generated three-tree context map round-tripped locally and libbrotli
  independently decoded the one-shot and progressive fixtures. On 17 real
  corpus files only Silesia `samba` changed, from 46,179 to 46,030 bytes; the
  aggregate changed from 738,929 to 738,780 bytes. Keeping the established
  two-tree writer as a separate compile-time instance isolated the new storage
  shape, but eleven fixed-CPU-2, 500-iteration, independent-binary interleaved
  pairs still measured row medians of `0.9533x` for dictionary, `0.9653x` for
  incompressible, `1.0094x` for JSON, `0.9699x` for mixed, `0.9917x` for source,
  and `1.0013x` for 32 KiB source. Their median-ratio geometric mean was
  `0.9816x`, with dictionary and mixed losing all 11 pairs. The production
  writer, proposal, fixtures, and tests were removed. Revisit three-type literal
  splitting only with a design that avoids perturbing the existing ratio-path
  binary layout or that wins enough real-corpus bytes to justify a separately
  dispatched implementation.
  Shared optimal LZ77 length selection now packs each cached minimum cost and
  its longest-on-tie match length into one `usize` key on 64-bit targets. The
  low nine bits store an inverted 3...258 length, so one unsigned comparison
  replaces the former cost/length branch and the hot loop reads and writes one
  array instead of two. The original two-array algorithm remains the 32-bit
  fallback, and the unused 64-bit length array is deliberately retained to keep
  the shared `HashIndex` layout stable for unrelated short encoders. A 64-shape
  oracle covers min-match 3/4, nonzero suffix offsets, incremental 37/131/258
  extensions, randomized costs, and all-costs-equal longest-tie selection; the
  complete optimal token oracle and x86 32-bit compile check also pass. Eleven
  fixed-CPU-2 independent-binary pairs preserved all eight Brotli ratio wires
  and checksums while improving the 32 KiB source row by `1.1263x` with 11/11
  wins. The eight row medians had a `1.0326x` geometric mean and a `0.9924x`
  floor on the 11-byte uppercase timer; a separate 15-pair, 5,000-iteration
  run measured that row at `1.0151x`. The shared Zstd consumer preserved every
  token/statistic/wire/checksum across its nine text/JSON/binary optimal-stage
  rows; seven fixed-CPU-2 pairs improved every row by `1.1889x`--`1.3422x`,
  with a `1.2490x` row-median geometric mean.
  Resuming optimal match extension after its already validated four-byte prefix
  was evaluated next and rejected. A mismatch-at-every-offset oracle proved the
  resumed matcher identical, and all optimal parser tests plus Brotli wires and
  checksums remained exact. Seven fixed-CPU-2 independent-binary pairs improved
  the 32 KiB source target by only `1.0054x`, however, while ordinary ratio JSON
  fell to `0.9559x` with 0/7 wins; dictionary and mixed were also slightly
  negative at `0.9973x` and `0.9956x`. The four-row median geometric mean was
  `0.9884x`. The special extension and its oracle were removed; the shared
  match-length routine continues to scan from byte zero.
  Loading the next optimal predecessor before prefix validation was rejected as

  Added a dedicated Brotli ratio-stage profiler instead of continuing to infer

  zero/nonzero literal lengths. Fifteen interleaved independent-binary,
  fixed-CPU-2 JSON level-1 pairs (20 iterations, 9 rounds) preserved the
  643-byte frame but measured only `1.0033x` geometrically with a `0.9953x`
  floor. The common trial loop remains because eliminating one fixed iteration
  does not justify a dedicated branch.
  The single-state beam now rejects short match transitions before computing
  their exact length/distance cost when an occupied target is already no worse
  than the format-derived minimum: eight bits for a repeat match or sixteen
  bits for a direct match. The shortcut is limited to the profiled short-match
  hot path below 68 bytes, leaving text's dominant long matches branch-free;
  equal costs preserve the earlier path and deterministic tie behavior. An exhaustive
  transition oracle covers match-length cost boundaries through 258, repeat and
  direct distances through 32 KiB, occupied/unoccupied targets, and low/high
  source and target costs. Compile-time-only profiling found that the bound
  rejects 29,050 of 29,388 failed primary JSON indexed transitions and all
  22,355 failed primary binary transitions; text remains dominated by long
  matches. Twenty-one fixed-CPU-2 stage pairs preserve all candidate bytes and
  improve JSON/binary medians by `1.0398x`/`1.0573x`, with text at `1.0006x`.
  Thirty independent complete-frame matrix pairs preserve every one of 20 frame
  sizes and checksums: JSON levels 1/3 improve by `1.0100x`/`1.0180x`, the
  row-median geometric mean is `1.0012x`, and the weakest median is text level
  3 at `0.9940x`. The stage CSV now retains literal/indexed/recent-offset empty
  insert, replacement, and rejection counts plus minimum-cost rejection counts
  so future transition work can be evidence-driven.
  Extending the same transition lower bound to exactly 258-byte matches was
  rejected at the focused stage gate. The profiler found only 189 provable
  primary-text rejections and 1,890/945 in the 4/8 KiB adaptive rows, versus
  tens of thousands of maximum-length matches that still require exact costs.
  Twenty-one independent fixed-CPU-2 pairs reduced text primary/adaptive
  throughput to `0.9821x`/`0.9893x`/`0.9914x`; JSON and binary controls also
  fell to `0.9879x`/`0.9898x`. Production retains the short-match-only branch.
  The native Zstd candidate-stage benchmark now reuses the shared compile-time-
  only optimal-search profiler for every `optimal` row. Its CSV exposes compact-
  index bytes, index/search/reconstruction time, visited chain nodes, four-byte
  prefix and prefix-cost rejections, mismatch/bound/slack histograms, full
  match-length calls, expanded length choices, and candidate-budget stops; the
  100-row gate checks every accounting identity and requires zeroed fields on
  unrelated stages. The ordinary encoder's `.text` and `.rodata` remain byte-
  identical. On the first 128 KiB of Ghostty `Terminal.zig`, 1,988,269 chain
  visits split into 1,296,473 prefix rejects, 484,550 lower-bound rejects, and
  176,096 full match-length calls; 65,058 searches stop at the eight-candidate
  budget. Search takes about 17.90 ms of the 18.47 ms profiled plan, identifying
  candidate traversal rather than index construction or token reconstruction as
  the next large-source target.
  Zstd's fastest-level exact optimal fallback now stops after seven useful
  candidates per position instead of eight; every higher search budget and all
  non-Zstd users retain eight. A 4/6/7/8 sweep over four 80--128 KiB real source
  files selected seven as the narrow Pareto point. A 32-shape generated audit
  spanning 8--64 KiB random, periodic, sparse-noise, and copied-tail inputs
  replays both token streams exactly; three candidate wires change, all three
  become smaller, and the aggregate moves from 230,784 to 230,779 bytes. On
  twelve 128 KiB Silesia prefixes, thirty fixed-CPU-2 complete-frame pairs give
  a `1.0167x` row-median geometric mean with every file at or above `1.0056x`.
  Six wires are unchanged, one shrinks by nine bytes, and five grow; aggregate
  size changes from 574,892 to 575,562 bytes (`+0.1165%`) while remaining below
  libzstd 1.5.5's 632,131 bytes. The worst ratio tradeoff is `nci`, up 109 bytes
  (`+1.033%`) but still 468 bytes smaller than libzstd. Fifteen fixed-CPU-2
  optimal-stage pairs on Ghostty `Terminal.zig`, README, the roadmap, and
  `src/zstd.zig` improve by `1.0373x`/`1.0350x`/`1.0412x`/`1.0456x`, all with
  15/15 wins. A thirty-pair complete 20-row matrix keeps every locked wire and
  checksum, reaches a `1.0025x` row-median geometric mean, and has a `0.9939x`
  floor; JSON level 1 improves by `1.0144x`. The pre-existing 128-shape
  level-1 single-beam audit changes by four bytes in aggregate (`649,782` to
  `649,786`, about `0.0006%`) while its bounded/deep-parser equivalence remains
  exact; that golden total now records the deliberate fastest-policy change.
  A fixed 23-byte non-overlapping copy for the other half of `huffman80k`'s
  match distribution was rejected. The exact 16+4+2+1-byte kernel preserved
  the caller-buffer suffix, but twenty-one fixed-CPU-2 five-row pairs improved
  the target by only `0.9977x` and reduced `large_json` to `0.9846x`. The
  generic match copier remains for this length.
  Relaxing the fastest wide double-fast direct-return threshold beyond the
  retained `4/15` ratio was rejected by a 16-file real-data size screen before
  timing. At `3/10`, the 128 KiB Silesia `mr` prefix grew from 32,676 to 37,918
  bytes (`+16.04%`) and became 1.088 times libzstd 1.5.5's 34,863-byte result.
  At `5/16`, Ghostty `Terminal.zig` and README additionally grew by 24.55% and
  22.02%, both exceeding libzstd; `1/3` also grew the roadmap prefix by 26.16%
  to 1.111 times libzstd. The existing `4/15` gate is therefore a real quality
  boundary rather than an arbitrary conservative constant.
  Lowering the fastest optimal candidate budget again from seven to six was
  rejected after the real-corpus screen. Across twelve 128 KiB Silesia prefixes,
  fifteen fixed-CPU-2 pairs improved by `1.0119x` geometrically, but six of the
  twelve row medians were below the seven-candidate baseline. The sixteen-file
  size screen grew by another `0.1569%`; the largest incremental case was `nci`
  at `+0.535%`, bringing its cumulative change from the original eight-candidate
  policy to about `+1.57%`. More decisively, thirty independent 20-row frame
  pairs fell to a `0.9957x` row-median geometric mean with a `0.9873x` floor on
  JSON level 1; that target won only 2/30 pairs. The seven-candidate Pareto point
  remains, and budgets six/four are closed absent a separately isolated layout.
  Borrowing the caller's parsed `HuffmanLiteralDecodeState` in the all-FSE/
  Huffman sequence helper was rejected at the focused decode gate. It removes
  the roughly 5.1 KiB by-value block-entry copy and shrinks the helper by three
  bytes, but makes the hot loop reach its cursor/tree/lookup through a pointer.
  Twenty-one fixed-CPU-2 pairs kept every decoded checksum while reducing
  `large_json` to `0.9944x`; `huffman80k`, `binary_mixed`, `numbered_json`, and
  `ascii64k` were noise-neutral. The local state copy remains because its better
  loop locality outweighs five copies per 512 KiB frame.
  An upstream-style 32-byte vector copy for long non-overlapping matches was
  rejected after enforcing Vort's caller-buffer boundary. A speculative
  wildcopy first improved the five-row profile, but could overwrite up to 31
  bytes beyond the logical decoded length when the caller supplied extra
  capacity, so it was not an acceptable public API implementation. The corrected
  kernel copied complete vectors plus an exact tail, with an exhaustive
  1--258-byte/distance oracle that also verified untouched suffix bytes. Inline,
  it improved `large_json`/`binary_mixed` by `1.0573x`/`1.0295x` but reduced
  `huffman80k` to `0.9857x`. Moving its 97-byte body to an independent text
  section did not fix the formal 13-row path: twenty-one fixed-CPU-2 pairs put
  `huffman80k` at `0.9704x`, `numbered_json` at `0.9867x`, and `large_json` at
  `0.9984x`, for a `0.9977x` row-median geometric mean. The compact exact
  `memcpy` match path remains.
  The pure Zstd decode-profile tool now walks every compressed block through the
  production sequence parser outside the timed decode loop and records literal/
  match bytes, zero-literal sequences, overlapping/non-overlapping match counts
  and bytes, vector-copy eligibility, coarse length/offset histograms, and exact
  32--127-byte match lengths. The five-row gate verifies sequence, byte, and
  histogram identities. The ordinary 13-row reference benchmark's `.text` and
  `.rodata` are byte-identical with and without the profiler. The 512 KiB
  `large_json` frame has 7,299 non-overlapping matches covering 515,977 bytes;
  7,295/515,907 qualify for a 32-byte copy, and 6,059 matches are exactly 71
  bytes. `binary_mixed` has 8,188 non-overlapping, vector-eligible matches
  covering 393,085 bytes, of which 8,121 are exactly 48 bytes. The all-FSE/raw
  `huffman80k` control has zero vector-eligible matches. This narrows follow-up
  work to compact fixed-71/fixed-48 kernels rather than another general loop.
  The all-FSE/Huffman sequence loop now handles its dominant 71-byte,
  non-overlapping match with two exact 32-byte vector copies and a seven-byte
  tail. The route requires an in-frame offset of at least 71 and retains the
  public caller-buffer contract: it checks the exact remaining match length and
  never writes beyond the logical decoded end. A direct module oracle compares
  the specialized and generic copies while also checking every untouched suffix
  byte. Twenty-one fixed-CPU-2 pairs against an independent `b274d982` binary
  improve the five-row decode-profile median by `1.1888x` on `large_json`;
  `huffman80k`, `binary_mixed`, `numbered_json`, and `ascii64k` stay at
  `1.0053x`/`0.9977x`/`0.9974x`/`1.0006x`. The complete 13-row reference
  benchmark confirms `large_json` at `1.1752x` with 21/21 wins, a `1.0116x`
  row-median geometric mean, and a `0.9910x` floor on `numbered_json`; every
  compressed input size and decoded checksum remains identical.
  The symmetric fixed-48-byte optimization for the FSE/FSE/RLE raw-literal
  loop was rejected. Its exact 32+16-byte vector kernel passed the same suffix-
  preserving module oracle and targets 8,121 of `binary_mixed`'s 8,188 matches.
  Twenty-one fixed-CPU-2 pairs improved that target by `1.0225x` with 21/21
  wins, but the adjacent `large_json` control fell to `0.9884x`. The 71-byte
  path remains isolated to the all-FSE/Huffman loop; adding both fixed shapes
  perturbs that profitable loop beyond the control floor.
  Expanding the retained 71-byte helper to the adjacent 68--71-byte cluster was
  rejected even though it covered another 1,228 `large_json` matches. The two
  fixed vector stores plus variable 4--7-byte tail passed the exact copy/suffix
  oracle, but twenty-one fixed-CPU-2 five-row pairs reduced `large_json` to
  `0.9379x` and `huffman80k` to `0.9725x`; only `binary_mixed` improved to
  `1.0171x`. The exact 71-byte code shape is retained.
  A temporary exact 3--31-byte match histogram identified `huffman80k`'s two
  dominant lengths: 2,575 matches at 23 bytes and 2,574 at eight bytes, out of
  5,161 total. The extra 29-counter diagnostic changed the formal reference
  binary's `.text`/`.rodata` layout, so it was removed after collecting the
  evidence rather than becoming a permanent profiler field.
  A fixed `(match_len=8, offset=7)` overlapping-copy specialization was also
  rejected. All 2,574 eight-byte `huffman80k` matches have that exact offset,
  and a direct 7-byte-load/eight-byte-store oracle preserved the full output
  tail. Twenty-one fixed-CPU-2 five-row pairs nevertheless left `huffman80k` at
  only `0.9951x` and reduced `large_json` to `0.9854x`; the generic seed-and-
  doubling copy remains.
  Prefetching long-distance match sources while the all-FSE/Huffman loop decoded
  the preceding literals was rejected. The candidate targeted the 6,420 of
  7,299 `large_json` matches whose offsets are at least 4 KiB and prefetched two
  cache lines only when both addresses were already-produced, frame-local
  history; it did not change any decoded checksum or profile statistic. It grew
  `decodeAllFseHuffmanSequences` by 49 bytes, however, and twenty-one
  fixed-CPU-2 interleaved five-row pairs reduced `large_json` to `0.9486x` with
  0/21 wins. `huffman80k`, `binary_mixed`, `numbered_json`, and `ascii64k` were
  `0.9899x`/`0.9887x`/`0.9991x`/`1.0015x`; the row-median geometric mean was
  `0.9854x`. The hardware demand load is preferable to adding branches and two
  software prefetches in this loop.
  Special-casing one-byte Huffman literal runs in that helper was rejected too.
  A temporary benchmark-only histogram showed that 6,831 of `large_json`'s
  7,299 sequences (93.6%) have `literal_len == 1`, while 5,155 of
  `huffman80k`'s 5,161 sequences have zero literals and 8,121 of
  `binary_mixed`'s 8,188 sequences have at least sixteen. Routing the one-byte
  case through a fixed-length slice nevertheless duplicated the inlined lookup
  and error paths, growing `decodeAllFseHuffmanSequences` by 485 bytes. In
  twenty-one fixed-CPU-2 interleaved five-row pairs, `large_json` fell to
  `0.9851x` with 3/21 wins and `huffman80k` to `0.9875x`; the row-median
  geometric mean was only `1.0018x`, despite an unrelated layout gain on
  `binary_mixed`. The temporary histogram was removed and the compact runtime-
  length literal loop remains.
  Hoisting the complete-Huffman lookup proof to block dispatch instead of
  checking a proof bit per literal was also rejected. Storing the proof in the
  state's tail padding shrank the specialized helper by 14 bytes, but changed
  state field placement; twenty-one fixed-CPU-2 pairs left `large_json` neutral
  at `0.9998x` and reduced `huffman80k` to `0.9828x`. Revalidating all lookup
  entries once before dispatch preserved the state layout and again shortened
  the helper by 14 bytes, but moved surrounding code: `large_json` fell to
  `0.9727x` with 0/21 wins, while unrelated `huffman80k`/`binary_mixed` rows
  rose to `1.0234x`/`1.0280x`. The checked packed-entry test remains in the
  sequence-interleaved literal loop; only the separately isolated whole-section
  decoder uses `lookupAssumeComplete`.
  Fusing the large-table FSE builder's normalized-total scan with initialization
  of its 256-entry `symbol_next` array was rejected. The table oracle and corrupt-
  input tests stayed exact, and eliminating the explicit zero fill plus second
  values pass shrank `fse_builder.build` from 1,760 to 1,257 bytes. That size
  change moved the downstream all-FSE/Huffman helper by 496 bytes, however. In
  twenty-one fixed-CPU-2 five-row pairs, `large_json`/`huffman80k` fell to
  `0.9778x`/`0.9699x`, both with 0/21 wins; `binary_mixed` and `numbered_json`
  rose to `1.0352x`/`1.0155x`, confirming a mixed layout effect rather than a
  safe aggregate win. Keep the current two-pass initialization until the builder
  can be compared in an isolated text layout.
  Moving the unchanged large-table FSE builder into its own object-format text
  section was tested as that isolation boundary and rejected. It preserved the
  1,760-byte builder and every decoded checksum, but moving the function itself
  also shifted the downstream all-FSE/Huffman helper. Twenty-one fixed-CPU-2
  five-row pairs put `large_json` at `0.9857x` with 4/21 wins, below the control
  floor; `huffman80k` was neutral at `1.0016x` and `binary_mixed` rose to
  `1.0264x`. Section isolation therefore cannot be assumed neutral in this
  executable and was removed.
  A final causality check compared the fused builder with the unchanged builder
  while both occupied that same temporary section. This kept the downstream
  `decodeAllFseHuffmanSequences` address and size identical and confirmed only
  a sub-threshold gain: thirty-one fixed-CPU-2 pairs measured `large_json`/
  `huffman80k` at `1.0033x`/`1.0052x`, a five-row geometric mean of `1.0021x`,
  and a `0.9987x` floor on `binary_mixed`. Both the fusion and temporary section
  were removed; this separates the small real builder saving from the much
  larger, unstable layout effects seen in the unisolated binaries.
  Requiring every sequence-interleaved Huffman table to pass the existing
  complete-prefix builder, then using unchecked lookup without a stored proof
  bit or rescan, was rejected on attribution grounds. Focused valid and malformed
  Huffman tests passed, and twenty-one fixed-CPU-2 five-row pairs reached a
  `1.0117x` row-median geometric mean with a `0.9953x` floor. However, the
  intended `large_json` path itself was `0.9953x` with only 7/21 wins; the
  apparent gains were `huffman80k` `1.0259x` and `binary_mixed` `1.0377x`, whose
  raw literal sections never execute the changed lookup. The result is therefore
  a code-layout artifact, not evidence for removing the defensive partial-table
  fallback.
  A Zstd-only optimal-search instance that checked the fourth byte before the
  full four-byte prefix was rejected. The compact index hashes three bytes but
  does not guarantee equality because buckets collide, so the candidate retained
  the full comparison after a fourth-byte hit and kept candidate order, budgets,
  tokens, search-profile counters, wire bytes, and checksums exact. On the first
  128 KiB of Ghostty `Terminal.zig`, 1,215,417 of 1,243,327 prefix rejects
  (97.8%) differ first at byte four. Even with the change isolated from Deflate
  and Brotli through a compile-time Zstd instance, fifteen fixed-CPU-2 optimal-
  stage pairs lost on all four real source targets: Terminal, README, roadmap,
  and `src/zstd.zig` measured `0.9792x`/`0.9784x`/`0.9809x`/`0.9788x`. The
  staged dependency costs more than the avoided wide comparisons, so the single
  u32 check remains.
  Hoisting the current-position u32 prefix load out of the optimal candidate
  chain was rejected below threshold even when isolated to a compile-time Zstd
  instance, leaving Deflate and Brotli code generation unchanged. A generated
  min-match-four oracle and the real-source profiler preserved every token,
  statistic, candidate wire, and checksum. Fifteen fixed-CPU-2 optimal-stage
  pairs were consistently positive on Ghostty `Terminal.zig`, README, roadmap,
  and `src/zstd.zig` (`1.0042x`/`1.0058x`/`1.0039x`/`1.0066x`), but the
  `1.0051x` geometric mean does not clear the 1% retention bar. LLVM already
  keeps the current address live, so eliminating the repeated memory operand is
  too small to justify another shared-parser instance.
  Caching `best_length_choices[choices_built_through]` in the optimal search
  loop was rejected. The value changes only when a newly compared match extends
  the constructed length range, so the generated bound/token oracle and real-
  source profile retained identical choices, all counters, candidate bytes, and
  checksums. The extra live scalar increased register pressure: fifteen fixed-
  CPU-2 optimal-stage pairs reduced Ghostty `Terminal.zig`, README, roadmap, and
  `src/zstd.zig` to `0.9779x`/`0.9690x`/`0.9633x`/`0.9743x`. The direct array
  load remains because its address is cheap and its shorter live range schedules
  better.
  Widening the two-state Zstd repeat beam from `u16` to `u32` positions was
  rejected after a 128 KiB real-source probe. The unchanged algorithm completed
  all nineteen beam tests and produced candidates roughly 1.8--2.4 times faster
  than the exact optimal search, but it was dominated by the existing greedy
  candidate on every input. Ghostty `Terminal.zig`, README, roadmap, and
  `src/zstd.zig` produced 35,325/22,073/37,529/25,464-byte beam candidates
  versus 34,304/21,802/37,420/23,842 bytes from greedy, and the wider beam was
  slower as well. Expanding its state/index memory therefore cannot replace or
  safely skip the much smaller 31,832/20,193/34,329/21,778-byte optimal
  candidates; the compact 65,535-byte limit remains.
  Replacing the retained 71-byte copy's exact seven-byte tail with one exact
  eight-byte vector load/store starting at byte 63 was rejected. The overlap is
  semantically safe because byte 63 was already written by the second 32-byte
  vector, and the existing full-buffer oracle confirmed that no byte beyond the
  logical match changed. The generated helper grew by two bytes, however, and
  twenty-one fixed-CPU-2 five-row pairs reduced `large_json` to `0.9876x` with
  only 4/21 wins; the row-median geometric mean was `0.9983x`. LLVM's current
  overlapping 4+4-byte implementation of the seven-byte tail remains faster.
