  Removing the fixed-71 dispatch's repeated `frame_output_start <= written`
  guard was rejected below threshold. The enclosing block decoder proves this
  invariant before parsing sequences, and `written` then grows monotonically;
  all 32 focused native-decoder tests and the match-copy suffix oracle passed.
  The generated helper nevertheless grew by two bytes, and twenty-one fixed-
  CPU-2 five-row pairs left `large_json` neutral at `0.9997x` with 9/21 wins.
  The five-row geometric mean was `1.0033x` with a `0.9969x` floor, so the
  explicit local guard remains as useful defensive documentation rather than
  retaining an unmeasurable layout change.
  An upstream-style eight-sequence lookahead queue for the long-distance all-
  FSE/Huffman decoder was rejected at the first target gate. It decoded FSE
  states and repeat offsets in original order, retained actual literal/match
  execution order, and prefetched only two cache lines already inside the
  currently initialized frame output. All 35 focused native-decoder tests
  passed, but the helper grew from 4,082 to 6,945 bytes. Nine fixed-CPU-2,
  500-iteration `large_json` pairs measured only `0.8731x` with 0/9 wins. The
  queue management and lost loop locality overwhelm any hidden memory latency,
  so production keeps the single-sequence decode/execute loop.
  Level-1 optimal parsing for 65,537--131,072-byte blocks now uses a dedicated
  four-byte hash-chain kernel in `zstd/match/optimal_four.zig`. The ordinary
  shared LZ77 parser and every shorter or higher-level Zstd block retain the
  established three-byte index. This revisits the previously profitable but
  layout-sensitive four-byte experiment with a genuinely separate object-format
  text section and a 257-byte noinline emission wrapper, rather than adding
  another generic instantiation to `lz77.zig` or inflating its old wrapper. The
  15-bit hash still verifies all four input bytes after collisions;
  candidate budget, DP cost/tie policy, 32 KiB distance window, and final exact-
  size candidate arbitration are unchanged. A 128-shape, 65--128 KiB generated
  oracle replays every plan, requires no fixed-bit-cost regression, and records
  two improvements (`30,487,549` versus `30,487,553` aggregate bits). A separate
  32-frame public encoder audit is byte-neutral in aggregate (`590,165` bytes),
  while boundary tests pin the 65,536/65,537-byte route and allocation-failure
  coverage verifies both complete failure enumeration and same-scratch recovery.
  On four 128 KiB real source prefixes, fifteen fixed-CPU-2 optimal-stage pairs
  improve by `1.4210x`/`1.4158x`/`1.6584x`/`1.3372x` (15/15 wins each), for a
  `1.4534x` row-median geometric mean; candidate sizes change from
  31,832/20,193/34,329/21,806 to 31,812/20,193/34,328/21,794 bytes. Complete
  level-1 frame medians are `1.2043x`/`1.1853x`/`1.3078x`/`1.0019x`, with a
  `1.1694x` geometric mean and aggregate size 113,545 to 113,524 bytes. Across
  all twelve 128 KiB Silesia prefixes, the complete-frame geometric mean is
  `1.1408x`, the floor is `0.9998x`, and every file wins at least 7/15 pairs;
  aggregate size falls from 575,562 to 575,231 bytes. Only `sao` grows, by four
  bytes (`97,828` to `97,832`) while remaining 14.2% smaller than libzstd 1.5.5.
  A separate 15-pair 20-row built-in matrix keeps every wire unchanged, reaches
  `1.0027x` geometrically, and has a `0.9964x` floor; a longer 31-pair JSON
  level-1 confirmation is `0.9975x`. Normalized disassembly confirms the old
  small-block optimal wrapper retains the same instruction sequence apart from
  relocated constant addresses. The final 100-row native-stage and 20-row
  libzstd 1.5.5 encode gates pass, as do the 273-case compatibility probe,
  five-row decode profile, nine-campaign/9,900-frame decodecorpus gate,
  131,072-byte large-sequence probe, 237-case native-frame probe, complete test
  suite, and all 85 compile-check targets.
  The isolated four-byte kernel now reuses the shared 259-entry compile-time
  fixed match-length cost table instead of executing its local range ladder for
  every newly constructed DP length. Exposing the existing table through a tiny
  inline LZ77 accessor avoids duplicating constants: independent binaries have
  byte-identical `.rodata`, unchanged ordinary `.text` address/size, and the
  dedicated four-byte section shrinks from `0x893` to `0x842` bytes. Twenty-one
  interleaved fixed-CPU-2 pairs preserve all candidate/frame bytes and checksums.
  Four real-source optimal-stage rows improve `1.0838x`/`1.0685x`/`1.0376x`/
  `1.1556x` (15/15 wins each), a `1.0855x` geometric mean. Their complete
  level-1 frames improve `1.0879x`/`1.0171x`/`1.0551x`/`1.0004x`, or
  `1.0396x` geometrically. Twelve 128 KiB Silesia prefixes reach `1.0129x`
  with a `0.9983x` floor and 200/252 pair wins; the 20-row level-1/3/9/22
  control matrix is `0.9999x` geometrically with a `0.9930x` floor.
  Scalar two-way unrolling (`0.9393x`), four-lane SIMD prefix-min (`0.8434x`),
  cached and on-demand distance thresholds (`0.9631x`/`0.9807x`), and a
  64K-bucket index (`0.9949x`) were rejected on the same four-source stage
  gate. Reducing the physical chain limit to 96, 112, or 120 failed the
  generated quality oracle; 124 preserved it but improved only `1.0072x`.
  Reusing one whole-block literal histogram across the unindexed large-block
  single-duplicate search was rejected despite a strong isolated result. Each
  candidate subtracted and restored exactly its matched interval, rebuilt the
  same Huffman plan, and still scanned the two retained literal spans for exact
  four-stream bit counts; a 16-shape 65,537/131,072-byte oracle matched the old
  selected positions, lengths, and payload scores exactly. Four real-source
  single-candidate rows improved `1.3005x`/`1.5402x`/`1.2455x`/`1.2254x`,
  all with 15/15 wins. Three production layouts nevertheless disturbed short
  paths: a direct selector split gave a 20-row floor of `0.9840x`; moving the
  finder, scorer, and dedicated two-span bit counter into the existing isolated
  section still reduced text levels 1/3/9/22 to roughly `0.980--0.988x`; and
  moving both old/new hashed finders behind one symmetric out-of-line wrapper
  left a `0.9885x` floor. All variants were removed rather than exchanging a
  large unused-candidate win for stable non-target regressions.
  Bounding the wide double-fast preflight to the two-state beam's 65,535-byte
  input limit was also rejected after exposing a false premise in the shortcut.
  On three 128 KiB source files where the preflight eventually discarded its
  candidate, the bound improved complete level-1 medians by
  `1.1968x`/`1.1836x`/`1.1988x`. However, a current `src/zstd.zig`
  prefix passes the pre-beam fastest-policy `4/15` threshold: disabling the
  preflight changed its 27,178-byte speed candidate to a much smaller 21,803-byte
  full-arbitration frame while slowing encoding to `0.1989x`. The preflight is
  therefore not generally dead above the beam limit; it independently implements
  the documented level-1 speed/ratio policy and remains enabled.
  Large sequence-table plans now remain borrowed throughout table scoring and
  final bitstream emission. The dynamic plan union contains a 64-byte normalized-
  count payload plus multiple slices; passing it by pointer avoids copying and
  reopening that tagged value for each of more than 512 symbols and transition
  fields. Existing compressed-transition scan-reference, 450/499/500/512 borrowed-
  emitter boundaries, large-table selection, and the 2,044-sequence libzstd probe
  preserve every state, bit field, and wire byte. Fifteen fixed-CPU-2 stage pairs
  across double-fast, greedy, and optimal on four 128 KiB source files improve all
  twelve rows by `1.0429x`--`1.1340x`, a `1.1035x` row-median geometric mean.
  Twenty-one complete-frame pairs improve the four sources by `1.0717x`
  geometrically with a `1.0391x` floor; twelve Silesia prefixes improve
  `1.0755x` geometrically with a `1.0046x` floor and 249/252 pair wins.
  The 20-row level-1/3/9/22 control matrix keeps all sizes/checksums, reaches
  `0.9998x` geometrically with a `0.9932x` floor, and the ReleaseFast binary's
  ordinary `.text` shrinks by 3,072 bytes. The 100-row stage and 20-row
  libzstd 1.5.5 encode gates, 273-case compatibility probe, five-row decode
  profile, 9,900-frame decodecorpus gate, 237-case native-frame probe, all
  1,543 tests, and all 85 compile-check targets pass.
  Extending the retained inverse FSE compression-table transition builder from
  <=512 sequences to the dynamic >512-sequence path was rejected despite a
  strong target result. A 513/1,024/2,047-sequence oracle matched the existing
  per-symbol-chain builder's initial state, next states, state widths, transition
  values, and transition widths exactly, and the 2,044-sequence libzstd probe
  retained its wire. Twelve double-fast/greedy/optimal real-source stage rows
  improved `1.1868x` geometrically, all 15/15. But moving the inverse helper to
  the FSE section changed the surrounding section placement and reduced the
  20-row complete-frame matrix to `0.9921x` geometrically with a `0.9647x`
  floor; inlining it into the original large planner reached only `0.9958x`
  with a `0.9771x` floor. Both variants were removed. A future retry needs a
  matched-layout isolation of the complete large planner, not another local
  transition substitution.
  Forcing the borrowed large-sequence symbol resolver inline was rejected as
  another layout-sensitive local win. The existing large-plan, borrowed-field,
  and 2,044-sequence interoperability tests stayed byte-exact. Fifteen fixed-
  CPU-2 pairs improved all twelve double-fast/greedy/optimal 128 KiB source
  stage rows, with a `1.0425x` geometric mean and `1.0144x` floor. The
  21-pair complete 20-row matrix instead reached only `0.9976x` geometrically:
  text levels 3/9/22 fell to `0.9837x`/`0.9823x`/`0.9832x` and binary
  level 1 to `0.9836x`. Keep the out-of-line resolver until the entire
  >512-sequence encoder can be isolated without moving shorter hot paths.
  Resuming four-byte optimal match extension after its already verified four-byte
  prefix was retested inside the independently linked large-block kernel. An
  exhaustive mismatch-position oracle, the 128-shape cost/token audit, OOM
  recovery, profile identities, and 32-bit compile check all passed, eliminating
  the former shared-parser layout confounder. Even so, all four 128 KiB source
  stage rows lost, with 0/15 wins and a `0.9837x` geometric mean. Starting the
  compact vector matcher at byte zero remains faster on this CPU.
  Hoisting the current-position prefix load was likewise retested inside the
  isolated four-byte kernel, removing the earlier shared-parser layout concern.
  The complete token/cost/profile/OOM and 32-bit checks remained exact, but
  fifteen fixed-CPU-2 pairs reduced all four 128 KiB source stages: medians were
  `0.9972x`/`0.9960x`/`0.9963x`/`0.9924x`, a `0.9955x` geometric mean.
  LLVM's existing loop placement is still preferable, so the source-level load
  stays.
  A fixed-258-byte match-extension specialization inside the isolated four-byte
  optimal kernel was rejected at the focused gate. It used eight fixed 32-byte
  vector comparisons plus an exact two-byte tail for all non-tail positions;
  an exhaustive mismatch-at-every-offset oracle, the 128-shape cost/token
  audit, allocation-failure recovery, profile identities, and 32-bit compile
  check all passed. The enlarged generated loop nevertheless reduced all four
  128 KiB source stages, with 0/15 wins and a `0.9452x` geometric mean. The
  compact shared bounded extender remains faster than fixed-loop unrolling.
  Isolating the complete >512-sequence emitter and its compressed-plan builder
  into the existing wide-sequence section was rejected as a matched-layout
  foundation for the inverse-transition experiment. The unchanged chain
  algorithm retained every wire and moved about 9.4 KiB from ordinary `.text`,
  but fifteen fixed-CPU-2 complete-matrix pairs reached only `0.9995x`
  geometrically and reduced JSON level 3 to `0.9818x`. Section isolation is
  therefore not neutral enough to rescue the otherwise fast inverse builder;
  both placement changes were removed.
  Reusing already validated canonical codes to score dynamic >512-sequence
  compressed tables was rejected despite another consistent target win. A
  default/non-default repcode oracle matched the stateful LL/OF/ML scorer's
  table bytes and total bit counts, and all twelve double-fast/greedy/optimal
  source stage rows improved with a `1.0661x` geometric mean and `1.0268x`
  floor. The inline production form narrowly missed the control floor
  (`0.9991x` geometric mean, text level 22 `0.9890x`); placing the helper
  in the wide section was worse at `0.9960x` with a `0.9873x` floor. Both
  were removed; large-table scoring keeps the authoritative stateful pass.
  Combining the five equal-length `u8` arrays in `LargeSequenceScratch` into
  one backing allocation was rejected after resource and performance validation.
  It reduced first-use allocation calls by four while preserving reuse, OOM
  recovery, and every large-sequence wire; allocator capacity rounding cost 512
  extra bytes, leaving frame-level reuse at nine fewer allocations and 75,970
  fewer bytes than the no-scratch path. Twelve real-source stage rows improved
  only `1.0077x` geometrically, and the complete 20-row matrix fell to
  `0.9976x` with multiblock level 3 at `0.9879x`. The five independently
  grown arrays remain because their end-to-end layout is measurably better.
  Passing all three complete `LargeSequenceTablePlanAlternatives` containers
  into the final selector by pointer was also rejected. This is narrower than
  the earlier caller-owned-return experiment: the established return ABI and
  per-plan borrowing remain, while only the selector's three inputs changed.
  Large-plan and 2,044-sequence wire probes passed; twelve real-source stage
  rows improved `1.0103x` geometrically with a `1.0029x` floor. The 21-pair
  complete matrix was only `0.9998x`, however, and reduced JSON level 3 to
  `0.9842x` plus text level 22 to `0.9869x`. Keep the by-value container
  call; LLVM's current return/call layout is better for short inputs.
  Removing the four-byte optimal kernel's logically redundant `nice_len`
  branch was rejected as unmeasurable. The fixed contract sets
  `nice_len == max_match == 258`, and the preceding `length == max_len`
  exit proves the branch cannot fire; the complete token/cost/profile/OOM and
  32-bit checks remained exact. Fifteen fixed-CPU-2 source-stage pairs measured
  only `1.0005x` geometrically, so the explicit generic-shaped guard remains.
  Reusing the four-byte optimal parser's existing `Token` backing allocation
  as a compact `u32` decision table was rejected. Literal and 9-bit-length /
  15-bit-distance match packing covered all field boundaries, and the 128-shape
  token/cost audit, OOM recovery, profile identities, and 32-bit compile check
  passed. The intended write-working-set reduction did not improve the target:
  fifteen fixed-CPU-2 source-stage pairs reached only `0.9995x` geometrically,
  with three of four row medians below one. The native tagged `Token` table
  remains.
  Isolating only `planLargeCompressedSequenceCodes`, while leaving the complete
  >512-sequence emitter in place, was also rejected as a matched-layout base.
  The unchanged chain builder preserved the 2,044-sequence wire and moved about
  1.6 KiB from ordinary `.text` into the FSE section, but 21 fixed-CPU-2
  complete-matrix pairs reached only `0.9973x` geometrically; text level 1
  fell to `0.9824x` and JSON level 3 to `0.9947x`. This final placement
  variant was removed, so the inverse-transition result remains evidence-only.
  Added a deterministic 32 KiB Brotli `records_q8` workload to both the
  libbrotli encode gate and ratio-stage profile. Production emits 3,459 bytes
  versus libbrotli 1.1.0 q8's 3,117 bytes; the four-byte optimal proposal is
  3,504 bytes because it leaves 1,284 literals / 31,484 matched bytes versus
  lazy's 1,258 / 31,510, emits 1,293 versus 1,253 commands, and has a worse
  fixed proxy at 38,520 versus 38,188 bits. It has more recent-distance/code-0
  hits (413/284 versus 374/269), so distance reuse alone does not explain the
  loss. Exact-wire arbitration correctly retains the 3,459-byte lazy plan.
  This locks a concrete Brotli command-fragmentation gap that the existing
  source-only profile did not expose. A three-byte optimal sweep at
  16/32/64/128 candidates produced 3,982/3,835/3,637/3,503 bytes and was
  removed: low budgets created up to 1,754 commands, while the full budget
  converged to the four-byte result. An upstream-style q8 parser
  prototype reduced the row to 2,674 bytes and improved 17 of 96 Silesia
  16/32 KiB slices without a size regression, but equivalent-harness controls
  missed the 0.99 speed floor (down to 0.9587 at row median). Multiple helper,
  wrapper, compile-time, and text-section isolation layouts failed to make the
  complete matrix neutral, so production code was removed and only the
  reproducible workload/profile evidence remains.
  Follow-up cost-model probes showed that a fixed per-command tax is not the
  missing variable: 1...12 bits did not change the record path, 16...32 bits
  removed one command but enlarged the proposal to 3,507 bytes, and larger
  penalties degraded sharply. `NDIRECT=15` reduced the internal proposal to
  3,491 bytes but gave no public source-size win and a dual-layout wire trial
  missed the throughput floor. An alphabet-width literal proxy was materially
  better: seven-bit printable-record literals changed recent/code-zero hits
  from 413/284 to 464/308 and reduced `records_q8` from 3,459 to 3,442 bytes
  (six/four-bit diagnostic constants reached 3,387/3,362 bytes). It cannot be
  enabled globally: a 12-row 64 KiB Silesia audit enlarged five rows, with
  Dickens +57 bytes and Samba +54 bytes. A strict fixed-width ASCII-record gate
  restored those 12 rows bit-exact, but shared-loop and isolated/copied parser
  integration layouts still missed the 0.99 control floor (best full-matrix
  row median 0.9802; isolated `nci` probes about 0.82...0.97). Those prototypes
  were removed. The successful follow-up moved the record-aware parser into an
  independently compiled Zig object with caller-owned scratch and token
  buffers, leaving the generic LZ77 hot loop unchanged. A strict 4...64 KiB
  fixed-width printable-record classifier gates the path; explicit non-default
  Brotli windows stay generic. This first stage moved `records_q8` to 3,442
  bytes (`-17`, `-0.49%`) and fixed-CPU-2 independent-binary A/B measured `1.0372x`
  median throughput (11/11 wins, about 4.12 versus 3.97 MiB/s). A 480-case
  record family audit improved 134 cases, rejected 301 losing record proposals
  through exact-wire arbitration, and found zero cases where skipping generic
  optimal lost a smaller wire. All Vort/libbrotli round trips passed. The 12-row
  64 KiB Silesia control remained byte-exact with a `1.0051x` row-median floor
  and `1.0143x` matrix geomean.
  Added a dedicated record-plan shape gate. Record and generic optimal both
  emit 1,293 commands on `records_q8`; the 62-byte proposal win comes from
  distance-history rearrangement instead: explicit distances fall 880 -> 829,
  recent hits rise 413 -> 464, code-zero rises 284 -> 308, and distance 128
  appears 514 versus 461 times. An isolated row-distance cost sweep demonstrated
  substantial remaining ratio headroom: costs 1...9 produced 2,779/3,110/
  3,320/3,340/3,347/3,349/3,361/3,368/3,387 bytes, with cost 2 beating
  libbrotli q8 by seven bytes on this single fixture. All variants were removed
  because fixed-CPU-2 target screening stayed around 0.94...0.96x; a length-16
  gate saved only four bytes and measured about 0.87x. Do not repeat scalar
  row-distance discounts. Continue with bounded distance-history state or
  two-pass command-cost refinement while preserving the isolated object ABI.
  Post-parse replacement with an equivalent row-distance copy and zero-to-four
  bit row-distance near-tie preferences were all wire-neutral at 3,442 bytes,
  confirming that the remaining gain requires path-level history state rather
  than a local tie-break.
  A width-two forward beam tracking only the newest distance then reached
  2,630 bytes and improved 465 of 480 fixed-record variants with zero
  arbitration hazards, but emitted 1,794 commands, shifted the dominant
  distance from 128 to 896, and measured only `0.9149x` median throughput over
  five fixed-CPU-2 target pairs. The prototype was removed. Any next beam must
  explicitly limit command growth or be admitted as a selective second pass.
  A row-distance-cost plus match-penalty grid did constrain commands: penalties
  2/4/6/8/10 yielded 3,110/3,320/3,340/3,347/3,347 bytes and
  1,511/1,332/1,303/1,295/1,295 commands. The penalty-eight point saved 95
  bytes with only two extra commands, but measured `0.9491x` over five target
  pairs. Penalizing only non-row distances retained 3,347 bytes and fell to
  `0.8525x`. Both were removed; avoid adding scalar branches to the object
  search loop without a separately proven hot-kernel design.
  Retained a sparse, allocation-free `rep0` refinement after the record DP: it
  keeps all 2,630 token / 1,293 command boundaries fixed and substitutes the
  current last distance only when it reproduces the full copy. On `records_q8`
  recent/code-zero hits rise 464/308 -> 542/504, explicit distances fall
  829 -> 751, and production shrinks 3,442 -> 3,209 bytes (`-6.77%`, only
  2.95% above libbrotli q8). Eleven fixed-CPU-2 pairs measured `1.0096x` median
  throughput (4.14 versus 4.12 MiB/s) with 10/11 wins. The 480-case audit improved 448 cases, rejected
  28 losing proposals, and found zero hazards; the 12-row Silesia control was
  byte-exact with a `0.9919x` row-median floor and `1.0016x` geomean. Future
  distance-only refinements may test older cache slots only with a hot-path
  design that avoids multiple full-copy validations per match.
  Compared the retained stream structure with libbrotli q8 and removed UTF-8
  literal contexts only from classifier-approved record candidates: libbrotli
  uses one literal tree on the target while Vort previously emitted two. This
  leaves token/command/distance choices unchanged and moves `records_q8`
  3,209 -> 3,187 bytes (`-0.69%`, 70 bytes / 2.25% above libbrotli q8). The
  single-tree form beat the prior two-tree wire in all 480 audited record rows
  by 1...32 bytes (9,901 bytes total). Eleven fixed-CPU-2 target pairs measured
  `1.0041x` median / `1.0039x` geomean throughput with 9/11 wins; the 12-row
  Silesia control retained bit-exact sizes/checksums with a `0.9995x` floor and
  `1.0001x` geomean. Existing entropy-split proposals were wire-neutral. A
  `rep1`-only distance probe reached merely 3,207 bytes and was rejected as too
  little ratio gain for another per-match branch.
  Retained a gated reconstruction refinement that extends each DP-selected
  match only beyond its already-proven endpoint at the same distance. The
  alternate path is used only when it adds at least four token/literal
  boundaries, a cheap structural signal that avoided every exact-wire
  regression in both the original 480-row grid and an independent 2,592-row
  grid. The target falls 3,187 -> 3,134 bytes (`-1.66%`), only 17 bytes / 0.55%
  above libbrotli q8. Eleven fixed-CPU-2 target pairs measured `0.9997x` median
  and geomean throughput; a 12-row Silesia control retained bit-exact output
  sizes/checksums with a `0.9909x` floor and `0.9932x` geomean. The original
  grid has 215 improvements / 265 unchanged / zero regressions, while the new
  grid has 969 / 1,623 / zero. Wire accounting attributes the prior 70-byte
  gap to +110 header, +249 command, +43 length-extra, and +626 distance bits,
  offset by -463 literal bits. Fixed NDIRECT=4, unconditional literal-count RLE
  smoothing, and a libbrotli-like leading-boundary rewrite were rejected after
  reaching 3,182 / 3,184 / 3,191 bytes respectively without robust enough
  tradeoffs.
  Retained a narrower form of upstream Huffman-count smoothing for the one-tree
  record literal alphabet. It constructs original and smoothed code lengths,
  selects by exact tree-header plus original-frequency payload bit cost, and
  emits only the winner instead of performing the previously rejected second
  full wire encode. `records_q8` moves 3,134 -> 3,132 bytes (15 bytes / 0.48%
  above libbrotli q8); the 480-row grid has 397 improvements, 83 unchanged, and
  zero regressions. Eleven fixed-CPU-2 pairs measured `1.0076x` median /
  `1.0090x` geomean with 11/11 wins, while the Silesia control remained
  bit-exact with a `0.9972x` floor and `1.0001x` geomean.
  Generalizing the selector to the record command and distance trees was
  wire-neutral at 3,132 bytes: their 15/18 active symbols are below the
  upstream smoother's 28-symbol floor. Keep the production option scoped to
  the literal tree until a small-alphabet header optimizer proves a win. A
  final equal-length `rep1` probe after match-tail extension reached 3,129
  bytes but regressed target throughput to `0.9907x` median / `0.9899x`
  geomean with 0/11 wins, so it was removed.
  A width-two beam with one shared ordinary match per position still reached
  2,648 bytes and improved 465/480 record variants with zero hazards, but the
  full-position/state walk measured only `0.6025x` over five fixed-CPU-2 target
  pairs. It was removed without testing wider ordinary candidate sets. Future
  stateful work should reuse the reverse DP output and refine sparse command
  boundaries instead of rescanning every input position in a forward beam.
  Retained a Zstd ratio-level proof inside the existing mixed-cancellation
  scheduler. An absolute-decisive repeat beam is encoded first; greedy and lazy
  still parse, but their entropy emission is skipped if unmatched-literal
  Huffman cost plus unavoidable LL/ML/OF extra bits already exceed the beam.
  The bound minimizes extra widths across direct, repeat-aware, and predefined
  representations and omits every positive tree/FSE/header cost. Locked JSON
  bounds are 714/831 bytes versus a 633-byte beam. A 48-shape oracle checks 44
  exact emitted wires (20 prunable), and fast/disabled-bound tests preserve the
  target plus 24 generated structured frames byte-for-byte. Twenty-one
  fixed-CPU-2 level-9 pairs improve `1.1175x` median / `1.1182x` geomean, all
  wins, at the same 640 bytes. The 20-row level matrix keeps all wire sizes and
  checksums; non-target floor/geomean are `0.9931x`/`1.0036x`. All Zstd gates,
  1,560 tests, and 93 compile checks pass. Keep this out of the ordinary
  selector: an in-body prototype had a `0.9835x` floor. Literal-cost hoisting
  (`0.9651x`) and 16-to-12-byte beam-state packing (`0.9791x`) were rejected.
  Removed the lower-bound helper's per-sequence scans over predefined LL/ML/OF
  states. Exhaustive format-range tests prove direct LL/ML/OF extra-bit widths
  never exceed the minimum predefined width, so direct widths (and the smaller
  repeat-aware OF width) are equally conservative. This removes about 4.1% of
  the profiled complete encoder. Relative to the first beam-first version, 21
  fixed-CPU-2 JSON level-9 pairs improve `1.0671x` median / `1.0663x` geomean,
  all wins, at the same 640 bytes. The 20-row control stays bit-exact with a
  `0.9973x` non-target floor and `1.0016x` geomean; all 1,561 tests, 93 compile
  checks, and four Zstd gates pass.
  Replaced the dedicated beam-first helper's full duplicate-index build with
  the existing bounded build. This path only needs paired candidates for the
  single-duplicate dominance proof and never reads the full cursor hash chain.
  The 16-seed full/bounded index oracle plus target and 24 generated full-wire
  tests preserve every relevant row and output. Twenty-one fixed-CPU-2 JSON
  level-9 pairs improve `1.0558x` median / `1.0567x` geomean, all wins, at
  640 bytes. The 20-row matrix is size/checksum exact with a `0.9918x`
  non-target floor and `1.0007x` geomean; the formal row reaches about
  35.21 MiB/s versus libzstd 1.5.5's 224.98 MiB/s. All four Zstd gates, 1,561
  tests, and 93 compile checks pass.
  Replaced that proof-only bounded index with a direct one-pass pairing scan on
  the successful dominance path. It computes the same maximum verified match
  length and byte frequencies without writing and rereading dense candidate
  rows; failed proofs still construct the bounded index and run exact
  single-match selection. A 24-seed, six-threshold oracle over 4,097--64,288
  bytes matches the old indexed decision on both sides, while all target and
  generated full-wire checks remain exact. The new helper lives in an isolated
  text section to protect unrelated hot-code layout. Twenty-one fixed-CPU-2
  complete-matrix pairs improve JSON level 9 by `1.0351x` median / `1.0312x`
  geomean and level 22 by `1.0294x` / `1.0333x`; all 20 sizes, input hashes,
  reference sizes, and checksums remain identical. The 16 non-JSON row medians
  have a `0.9926x` floor and `1.0001x` geomean. The formal level-9 row reaches
  about 37.56 MiB/s at 640 bytes versus libzstd 1.5.5's 233.29 MiB/s at 677
  bytes. All four Zstd gates, 1,562 tests, 93 compile checks, and the 328/237-case
  native/frame probes pass. Rejected follow-ups include a shared-index pending
  bitset, which regressed unrelated rows to about `0.985x`, and retained index
  byte frequencies, whose focused A/B produced only `0.9989x` geomean.
  Added interoperable ID-less raw-content dictionaries for Zstd.
  `NativeDictionary.initRawContent` represents caller-supplied history whose
  frames omit `Dictionary_ID`; explicit one-shot, caller-buffer, chunked,
  incremental, and reusable encoder/decoder paths now retain that
  history instead of treating ID zero as an instruction to discard it.
  Dictionary sets still reject zero IDs because an ID-less frame cannot select
  among multiple entries. A deterministic raw dictionary produces a 19-byte
  libzstd 1.5.5 frame for a 16 KiB payload: both libraries reject it without
  history and decode it byte-exactly with the explicit raw dictionary. Vort's
  one-shot and incremental ID-less output also decodes through libzstd. The
  compatibility probe now reports 276 cases, including three raw-dictionary
  cases; the 25-case dictionary probe and four upstream dictionary campaigns
  (4,200 frames, 2,118 block-stream cases, all 64 LL/OF/ML mode tuples) pass.
  Seekable streams now complete the same explicit-dictionary contract. Four new
  public scan/index × into/alloc range APIs carry one caller-selected dictionary
  across every intersecting frame, allowing ID-less raw dictionaries without
  weakening set-based routing. A two-frame range crossing the frame boundary
  checks every API, every frame header remains ID zero, no-dictionary decode
  fails, and a wrong dictionary is detected by the seek-entry checksum.
  Retained a Zstd ratio-level lower bound that lets a decisive repeat beam prove
  the first single-duplicate family at least 24 times larger without exact
  entropy scoring. The proof scans the existing paired index for the maximum
  removable interval, subtracts that maximum independently from the whole-block
  byte frequencies, and computes the optimal 11-bit Huffman cost of the bytes
  that must remain. Omitting tree, stream, sequence, and block overhead keeps
  the result conservative. It is compile-time-specialized only into callers
  requesting mixed-dominance proof; runtime-only placement variants were
  rejected after producing stable short-text layout regressions. The 32,797-byte
  JSON level-9 frame stays bit-exact at 640 bytes and improves by `1.2930x`
  median / `1.2943x` geomean over eleven fixed-CPU-2 independent-binary pairs,
  all wins. Twenty-four generated structured streams match the forced exact
  path byte-for-byte, and a 32-shape oracle rejects every false dominance
  proof. Sixteen non-target level-1/3/9/22 rows retain exact sizes/checksums with
  a `0.9911x` row-median floor and `0.9967x` geomean. The 20-row libzstd 1.5.5
  encode gate, 256-case runtime compatibility probe, comparison/block-sweep
  gates, all 1,558 tests, and all 93 compile checks pass.
  Reused exact sub-258-byte indexed match lengths across adjacent single-state
  beam positions when their selected distance is unchanged. The previous match
  proves both the shifted `L-1` prefix and its terminating mismatch; capped
  258-byte matches retain vector extension to protect the text-heavy control. A
  64-shape optimized/reference oracle compares tokens and statistics and requires
  a real reuse hit. The stage CSV adds `single_shifted_matches`; primary JSON
  hits 28,448 times out of 31,661 indexed matches and binary hits 22,356/23,063,
  versus only 253/37,300 on max-length-heavy text. Twenty-one fixed-CPU-2
  independent-binary JSON level-3 pairs improve `1.0254x` median / `1.0282x`
  geomean with 21/21 wins and identical 643-byte output. A 15-pair, 20-row
  matrix preserves every size/checksum, reaches a `1.0012x` row-median geomean,
  and keeps a `0.9926x` floor. The formal libzstd 1.5.5 gate reports about
  100.05 MiB/s versus 1445.50 MiB/s, so the broader standard-encoder throughput
  gap remains open.
  Added conservative encoded bounds and caller-owned output APIs for native
  Zstd seekable streams, including explicit dictionaries and dictionary-set
  selection. The into variants accept the exact encoded length or any larger
  buffer and produce byte-exact output matching the existing allocating path
  for empty, checksum/plain,
  identified-dictionary, and ID-less raw-dictionary streams.
  Added `NativeSeekableStreamEncoder` for repeated workloads. It retains the
  per-frame encoder, final output buffer, and seek-entry array while exposing
  alloc/scratch/append/into variants for plain, explicit-dictionary, and
  dictionary-set streams. A counting-allocator regression now proves that a
  second same-shape encode removes five allocation calls while preserving exact
  bytes, and an injected OOM followed by successful reuse covers rollback and
  teardown.
  The native allocation report separately locked one-shot caller-buffer encoding
  at 174 calls / 911,692 bytes and warmed reusable encoding at 172 calls /
  911,334 bytes; positive, negative-drift, schema, and aggregate dashboard gates
  validate the relationship. The reusable native frame context now also retains
  the two outer block-candidate arbitration buffers. Across the same four-frame
  seekable workload this reduces one-shot encoding to 168 calls / 910,486 bytes
  and warmed encoding to 164 calls / 909,726 bytes, while preserving the exact
  305-byte stream. The stricter gate now requires the full four-call / 760-byte
  warmed advantage. Thirty-one alternating independent-binary warmed A/B pairs
  (100 encodes per side) measured `1.0046x` paired median / `1.0030x` geomean
  with 21/31 wins. A 21-pair complete 129 KiB multi-block level-3 control kept
  the 27,517-byte wire and checksum exact while measuring `0.9983x` median /
  `0.9982x` geomean, so the retained claim is allocation reuse rather than a
  broad one-shot throughput gain.
  Extended the reusable block context to retain the nested greedy/lazy token
  lists, optimal-parser DP and compact hash-index storage, and inner match
  candidate buffers. Allocation-stack profiling attributed 40 of the remaining
  warmed calls and about 0.89 MiB to rebuilding those parser workspaces once per
  frame. The formal four-frame report now drops one-shot encoding to 132 calls /
  245,440 bytes and warmed encoding to 116 calls / 18,094 bytes, preserving the
  305-byte stream; the gate requires the full 16-call / 227,346-byte warmed
  advantage. Thirty-one alternating independent-binary warmed A/B pairs (100
  encodes per side) measured `1.0034x` median / `1.0096x` geomean with 18/31
  wins. A 21-pair complete 129 KiB multi-block level-3 control preserved the
  27,517-byte wire and checksum and measured `1.0028x` median / `1.0035x`
  geomean with 13/21 wins. Relative to the preceding reusable implementation,
  the warmed allocation count falls another 29.3% and transient requested bytes
  fall 98.0%; retained capacity is released by encoder teardown.
  Added a bounded stack path for hash-token sequence candidates up to 1 KiB. It
  uses an isolated 4 KiB arena for the five short-lived emission buffers and
  transparently retries through the existing allocator if that bound is too
  small; other candidate families and larger blocks keep their prior code path.
  The formal report falls from 132/116 calls and 245,440/18,094 bytes to 72/56
  calls and 236,098/8,752 bytes for one-shot/warmed encoding, with the same
  305-byte stream. A first
  retained-buffer prototype achieved 101/80 calls but was rejected because the
  complete 129 KiB level-3 control regressed to `0.9805x` median / `0.9784x`
  geomean. A broader wrapper that also routed non-hash sequence emitters through
  the stack path reached zero warmed allocations but remained about 0.5--0.8%
  slower on repeated multi-block controls and was rejected. The final compact
  call-site-only version measured a `1.0032x` row-median geomean across 15 paired
  runs of the complete 20-row encode matrix, with 13/20 positive rows and a
  `0.9960x` floor; all input hashes, frame sizes, and checksums remain exact. A
  31-pair multi-block confirmation measured `0.9952x`, while the warmed seekable
  target measured `1.0015x`. The retained claim is therefore a 51.7%
  allocation-call reduction and 51.6% transient-byte reduction, not a direct
  latency win.
  Removed the remaining redundant small-block single-duplicate emission when
  its exact precomputed payload length plus the block header cannot strictly
  beat the already selected candidate. The existing tie order keeps the earlier
  winner, so a 32-shape × four-budget × beam on/off oracle can force the old
  path and require byte-identical output while recording real prune hits. The
  four-frame allocation report drops again from 72/56 calls and 236,098/8,752
  bytes to 44/28 calls and 231,722/4,376 bytes for one-shot/warmed encoding.
  Fifteen paired runs of the complete 20-row encode matrix preserve every input
  hash, frame size, and checksum while measuring a `1.0060x` row-median
  geomean, 16/20 positive rows, and a `0.9955x` floor. Sixty-one warmed seekable
  pairs measured `1.0028x` median with 43/61 wins and `0.9997x` geomean.
  Added exact winner-only emission for single-sequence blocks without adding a
  new helper or changing the multi-sequence path. The shared literals section
  is built once, the existing RLE and predefined length models select one
  emitter, and equal lengths retain the original RLE-first wire. The selected
  block length is reserved before emission so allocator failure cannot leave a
  partial caller output. A forced-generic oracle over 64 deterministic valid
  shapes records real optimized-path hits, covers predefined wins and RLE ties,
  and requires byte-identical output; an allocation-failure sweep also checks
  output atomicity. The four-frame allocation report falls from 44/28 calls and
  231,722/4,376 bytes to 28/12 calls and 229,122/1,776 bytes for
  one-shot/warmed encoding, preserving the 305-byte stream. Fifteen paired
  runs of the complete 20-row encode matrix preserved every input hash, frame
  size, and checksum with a `1.0037x` row-median geomean; two sub-`0.99x` rows
  observed under a system load above 30 were retested independently for 61
  pairs and measured `1.0215x` (text level 3) and `0.9960x` (binary level 1)
  medians. Sixty-one warmed seekable pairs measured `1.0016x` median,
  `0.9990x` geomean, and 36/61 wins, so the retained claim is a 57.1% warmed
  allocation-call reduction and 59.4% transient-byte reduction with neutral
  end-to-end throughput.
  Extended the existing reusable block scratch to retain the single-sequence
  literals, selected payload, and reverse-bitstream buffers used by the
  repeated-pattern candidate. Non-reusable call sites keep locally owned
  buffers, and multi-sequence selection is unchanged. The four-frame report
  falls from 28/12 calls and 229,122/1,776 bytes to 19/0 calls and
  227,790/0 bytes for one-shot/warmed encoding, while retaining the exact
  305-byte stream. The reusable encoder test locks all three capacities across
  calls and requires a zero-allocation warm pass. Fifteen paired runs of the
  complete 20-row encode matrix measured a `1.0012x` row-median geomean; three
  noisy sub-`0.99x` rows were each retested for 61 pairs and measured
  `1.0000x` (multiblock level 9), `0.9938x` (JSON level 22), and `0.9903x`
  (text level 9) medians. Sixty-one warmed seekable pairs measured `0.9995x`
  median, `1.0029x` geomean, and 30/61 wins. The retained claim is zero
  transient allocations after warm-up, with neutral end-to-end throughput.
  Added a bounded 64-token initial reserve for the reusable greedy, lazy, and
  optimal parser outputs. On the locked 1 KiB frame shape each parser finishes
  with 35 tokens; reserving once replaces three identical 22-to-55 capacity
  growth sequences without applying the allocating planner's much larger
  4,096-token policy. The one-shot allocation report falls from 19 calls /
  227,790 bytes to 16 calls / 227,556 bytes, while the warm pass remains at
  zero allocations and the 305-byte stream is unchanged. Fifteen paired runs
  of the complete 20-row matrix measured a `0.9999x` row-median geomean; the
  lone `0.9574x` outlier (multiblock level 9) recovered to `1.0010x` median /
  `0.9956x` geomean over 61 independent pairs. Sixty-one warmed seekable pairs
  measured `0.9992x` median / `0.9991x` geomean, confirming neutral throughput.
  Batched complete Zstd Huffman lookup construction around the table's packed
  two-byte entry. Canonical ranges of one and two entries retain direct stores,
  four-entry ranges use one 64-bit vector store, and every larger power-of-two
  range is filled eight entries at a time with 16-byte stores. This mirrors the
  width-specialized fill strategy in upstream zstd while preserving the existing
  adjacency, coverage, and bounds proof; an attempted `@memset` spelling was
  rejected because Zig 0.16 still emitted a scalar 16-bit loop. A deterministic
  oracle generates 256 complete canonical trees and compares every lookup byte
  against the original reference builder, in addition to the existing malformed
  tree tests. Fifteen alternating independent-binary pairs at 100,000 decodes
  each improve the 1,290-byte `numbered_json` target by `1.1422x` median with
  15/15 wins. A separate 15-pair five-row profile at 10,000 decodes per run
  measures `1.1481x` on `numbered_json`, `1.0043x` on `huffman80k`, `1.0105x`
  on `ascii64k`, `1.0209x` on `large_json`, and `0.9995x` on `binary_mixed`.
  The 21-pair complete 13-row reference matrix improves `1.0202x` by the
  geometric mean of row medians; its lone noisy sub-`0.99x` short-sample row,
  `repetitive` at `0.9880x`, recovers to `1.0115x` median over 31 independent
  100,000-decode pairs. The full 9,900-frame upstream decodecorpus suite covers
  all 64 LL/OF/ML mode tuples, and the 276-case libzstd 1.5.7 compatibility
  matrix reports zero unsupported frames.
  Rejected two follow-up representations for the adjacent-match reuse state in
  Zstd's single-state beam. Splitting the optional match into two `u16` values
  improved the isolated JSON parser by about `1.028x`, but moved following hot
  helpers and reduced the full text level-1 path to about `0.980x`; restoring
  the old helper addresses left only about `1.004x` on full JSON. Packing the
  pair into one `u32` with the same fixed layout measured about `0.998x` on
  JSON and `0.990x` on text. Both prototypes were removed; future retries must
  improve the complete encoder rather than only the isolated parser.
  Added an out-of-line sequence-table workspace to `NativeFrameDecoder` for
  repeated caller-buffer decode. Four bounded cache slots retain resolved
  LL/OF/ML tables behind exact self-delimiting table-description bytes;
  Repeat_Mode remains frame-local, and execution still copies the resolved spec
  into the established `SequenceDecodeState` layout. The workspace is allocated
  only on the first compressed block, allocation failure transparently falls
  back to the one-shot decoder, and raw/RLE frames use the existing zero-
  allocation raw fast path. The public decoder handle stays at most 64 bytes and
  the complete workspace at most 64 KiB. A cache oracle covers exact hits and
  changed descriptions; integration tests cover a warm all-FSE hit, workspace
  OOM fallback, teardown, and raw zero-allocation behavior. The reusable modes
  added to both Zstd decode harnesses leave their default one-shot measurements
  unchanged. Against an independent `0287d427` binary driven through the same
  warmed `NativeFrameDecoder` API, eleven alternating 13-row pairs at 1,000
  decodes per row improve `numbered_json` by `1.3026x`, 512 KiB JSON by
  `1.1239x`, `huffman80k` by `1.0550x`, and mixed binary by `1.0554x`; every row
  median is at least `1.0073x`. A separate strict same-harness one-shot matrix
  has a `0.9996x` row-median geometric mean and a `0.9917x` median floor, so the
  warmed gain does not trade away the existing stateless API. The final 577
  Zstd tests, 1,571 repository tests, 93 compile checks, 328-case native probe,
  237-case frame probe, 25-case dictionary probe, large-sequence probe, 26-case
  CLI diff, 276-case compatibility matrix, and all 9,900 upstream decodecorpus
  frames across 64/64 sequence-mode tuples pass.
  Tightened that reusable sequence cache's hit contract from a by-value result
  to caller-owned `lookupInto`. The previous optional return first copied the
  roughly 12 KiB `SequenceModeSpec` out of its cache slot and then copied it
  again into the decode cursor; the cache now verifies the same exact
  self-delimiting description and writes once into the caller's final local
  spec, preserving the established by-value hot-loop layout. Twenty-one
  alternating independent-binary pairs at 100,000 decodes improve warmed
  `numbered_json` by `1.0973x` median with 20/21 wins. Fifteen five-row pairs
  improve `numbered_json` by `1.1147x`; `huffman80k`, mixed binary, large JSON,
  and zero-sequence ASCII stay at or above `0.9999x` at their medians. The
  15-pair warmed 13-row matrix has a `1.0107x` row-median geometric mean and a
  `0.9924x` floor after a noisy tiny row recovered to `1.0137x` over 31 pairs at
  100,000 decodes. A separate 15-pair one-shot matrix has a `1.0028x`
  row-median geometric mean and a `0.9902x` floor, while key decoder symbol
  addresses remain identical. All 577 Zstd tests, 1,571 repository tests, 93
  compile checks, the native/frame/dictionary/large-sequence probes, the
  26-case CLI diff, the 276-case compatibility matrix, and all 9,900 upstream
  decodecorpus frames across 64/64 sequence-mode tuples pass. A follow-up
  reusable Huffman tree/lookup cache was rejected despite up to `1.50x` on
  warmed `numbered_json`: adding a second decoder allocation reduced one-shot
  `huffman80k` to `0.9839x`, while folding tree-only entries into the existing
  workspace still reduced one-shot `numbered_json` to `0.9869x`; making the
  full reusable block wrapper noinline cut warmed throughput nearly in half.
  Future Huffman reuse needs a separately compiled decoder unit that can keep
  the ordinary decode text layout fixed, not another root-module cache field.
  Made warmed cache hits mode-aware after `lookupInto` exposed that mixed-mode
  blocks still materialized all three 4 KiB FSE tables. The cache now returns a
  borrowed entry plus its self-delimiting description length; the decoder keeps
  the same complete local `SequenceModeSpec`, but copies only tables whose
  resolved mode is `compressed` and initializes inactive-table metadata to
  zero. A dirty-destination oracle locks the mixed
  LL=Predefined/OF=Compressed/ML=RLE case, active OF entries, RLE metadata, and
  relocated bitstream offset. Against independent `26ae0cee` binaries,
  twenty-one alternating 100,000-decode pairs improve warmed `numbered_json` by
  `1.0318x` median with 21/21 wins. Fifteen five-row pairs keep every control
  median at or above `0.9966x`; the 15-pair warmed 13-row matrix improves
  `numbered_json` by `1.0315x` with a `1.00095x` row-median geometric mean and
  a `0.99135x` non-tiny floor. The noisy tiny control recovers to `1.0022x`
  warmed and `0.9988x` one-shot over separate 31-pair, 100,000-decode runs. The
  complete one-shot 13-row matrix has a `1.0021x` row-median geometric mean and
  a `0.9906x` non-tiny floor. All 578 Zstd tests, 1,572 repository tests, 93
  compile checks, the native/frame/dictionary/large-sequence probes, the
  26-case CLI diff, the 276-case compatibility matrix, and all 9,900 upstream
  decodecorpus frames across 64/64 sequence-mode tuples pass.
  Removed the empty literal-copy call from the reusable decoder's generic
  compressed-sequence loop. The `huffman80k` profile has 5,155 zero-literal
  sequences among 5,161 total, so preserving the existing Huffman-state branch
  while skipping `copyLiteralsFromSection` only when the raw literal length is
  zero avoids repeated no-op slice setup without changing the ordinary one-shot
  decoder's code layout. Against independent `eff21c1e` binaries, twenty-one
  alternating warmed pairs at 10,000 decodes improve `huffman80k` by `1.0790x`
  median with 21/21 wins. Fifteen warmed five-row pairs measure `1.0797x` on
  `huffman80k`, `1.0037x` on mixed binary, `0.9985x` on large JSON, `1.0094x`
  on numbered JSON, and `0.9974x` on zero-sequence ASCII. The warmed 13-row
  matrix has a `1.0095x` row-median geometric mean; its noisy short structured
  row recovers to `1.0030x` over 31 independent 100,000-decode pairs. In the
  one-shot matrix, noisy numbered JSON, tiny, and large-text controls recover
  respectively to `0.9960x`, `0.9970x`, and `0.9994x` medians in long reruns.
  Ordinary decoder symbols remain byte-identical between binaries. All 578
  Zstd tests, 1,572 repository tests, 93 compile checks, the 328-case native,
  237-case frame, 25-case dictionary, lib-generated, handcrafted, and
  large-sequence probes, the 26-case CLI diff, the 276-case compatibility
  matrix, and all 9,900 upstream decodecorpus frames across 64/64 sequence-mode
  tuples pass.

  Audited reusable Zstd decoder validation on macOS/Apple M1 Pro. The upstream
  corpus probe previously validated allocating and incremental APIs without
  exercising the recent sequence-table cache. It now reuses one decoder across
  every dictionary-free campaign and decodes each frame twice with independently
  poisoned output. The gate requires all eligible cases plus actual table hits
  in compressed campaigns; missing counters, short/excess counts, negative or
  absent hits, and incorrectly attributed dictionary coverage are rejected.
  The diagnostic hit accessor is public with explicit lifetime/error semantics.
  Warm-cache unit coverage now compares every nonempty truncation and every
  sequence-bitstream bit flip with the stateless API, checks OutputTooSmall,
  and verifies recovery on the original frame. The gate smoke also resolves
  reference-library paths before comparison on macOS, where /var resolves to
  /private/var.
  The final nine-campaign run passes all 9,900 upstream frames and all 64 mode
  tuples, including 5,700 dictionary-free frames decoded twice and 2,240 exact
  table hits. Dictionary campaigns retain their allocating/incremental checks
  without falsely claiming cache coverage. Use
  zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast run-zstd-decodecorpus-gate -j1 -- --libzstd
  /opt/homebrew/opt/zstd/lib/libzstd.dylib on this host; the generator identifies
  itself as v1.4.7-3063-gee650ef2 and the loaded library as 1.5.7.
  An active-prefix FSE table-copy prototype was evaluated and removed. Against
  independent 47fa6b01 baseline/candidate ReleaseFast binaries, eleven alternating
  20,000-decode pairs measured numbered JSON at 1.00835x median with 10/11 wins.
  The eleven-pair 13-row matrix at 1,000 decodes had a 0.97263x repetitive
  median; an eleven-pair 100,000-decode repeat recovered to 0.99418x median and
  1.00004x geometric mean. Input SHA-256, encoded sizes, and checksums matched.
  macOS 26.4.1, Zig 0.16.0, Apple M1 Pro, and Homebrew libzstd 1.5.7 were used,
  with one benchmark thread, no CPU affinity, five in-process timing samples,
  and alternating process order. Significant unrelated background load prevents
  treating these sub-percent changes as stable improvements; no production
  table-copy change or performance-win claim is retained. Local raw CSVs,
  independent binaries, and the reproduction driver are under
  zig-out/zstd-active-prefix-20260916. Next work should use an idle host for
  allocation/layout profiling before another cache-layout optimization.
  Made the Zstd reference benchmark, pure-Vort decode profiler, and encode
  benchmark accept `--libzstd PATH`, matching the compatibility and
  decodecorpus tools. This is required on macOS hosts where the Homebrew dylib
  is not on the process loader path, and keeps the exact reference
  implementation in benchmark provenance. The encode path smoke exercises an
  available explicit library and rejects missing arguments and nonexistent
  paths.
  A 20,000-iteration Apple M1 Pro survey against explicit libzstd 1.5.7 shows
  that the old single-predefined-sequence priority is stale: text, structured,
  repetitive, and RLE rows are already 2.88x--15.48x the reference throughput.
  The remaining large gaps are multi-sequence entropy paths: `numbered_json`
  0.435x, raw-literal all-FSE `huffman80k` 0.400x, `large_json` 0.620x, and
  mixed binary 0.477x. The host load was elevated, so these figures establish
  priority and order of magnitude rather than a fine-grained performance claim.
  Next work should profile the 5,161-sequence raw-literal all-FSE loop first.
  Added that dedicated raw-literal all-FSE decode loop for dictionary-free
  blocks with at least 1,024 sequences. It borrows the already parsed literal
  slice, decodes LL/OF/ML directly from their resolved FSE tables, copies only
  nonempty literal runs, and executes proven in-frame matches without reentering
  the generic literal-kind and dictionary dispatch. All smaller, mixed-mode,
  dictionary, Huffman, and RLE paths retain the generic decoder. A fixed
  libzstd 1.5.7 frame locks the exact 80,000-byte/754-byte shape: raw literals,
  5,161 sequences, and three compressed FSE tables. It covers allocating,
  caller-owned, cold/warm reusable, OutputTooSmall, 24 bitstream mutations
  against the stateless decoder, and recovery after errors. Against independent
  ReleaseFast binaries, the final 15-pair warmed five-row matrix improves
  `huffman80k` by 1.3558x with 15/15 wins; the control medians are 1.0113x
  numbered JSON, 0.9980x zero-sequence Huffman, 0.9965x large JSON, and
  1.0101x mixed binary. A separate 21-pair target run measured 1.3567x with
  21/21 wins, while the 15-pair one-shot matrix measured 1.4272x on the target
  with a 0.9977x floor. The same-process libzstd 1.5.7 comparison moves this
  row from about 0.40x to 0.60x reference throughput, materially closing but
  not eliminating the gap. All 404 Zstd tests, the compile gate, the 237-case
  frame probe, 276-case compatibility matrix, and all 9,900 upstream corpus
  frames across 64/64 sequence modes pass.
  Specialized the two dominant exact match shapes inside the isolated
  raw-literal all-FSE loop. A `(length=8, offset=7)` kernel performs two exact
  four-byte copies, with the second load observing the first newly written byte
  to preserve LZ overlap semantics. A non-overlapping 23-byte kernel performs
  one 16-byte vector copy and an exact seven-byte tail. Both have direct oracles
  that compare the entire output buffer, including untouched suffix bytes, with
  the generic copier. Keeping the parent helper in its own object-format text
  section isolates unrelated Huffman and mixed-mode loops from its code-size
  changes. Against independent ReleaseFast binaries, the final 21-pair warmed
  five-row matrix improves `huffman80k` by 2.0473x with 21/21 wins; all control
  medians are at least 0.9973x. The 15-pair one-shot matrix improves the target
  by 1.8825x with a 0.9987x control floor. Eleven same-process comparisons
  against Homebrew libzstd 1.5.7 put Vort ahead on this fixed shape by 1.2631x
  median, 11/11 wins, and a 1.2326x--1.2969x range. This is a shape-specific
  lead, not a claim of broad Zstd decoder superiority. All 406 Zstd tests, the
  compile gate, the 237-case frame probe, 276-case compatibility matrix, and
  9,900-frame/64-mode upstream corpus pass.
  Revisited the remaining 512 KiB `binary_mixed` decode gap with explicit code
  layout boundaries. Its first raw-literal block uses FSE/FSE/RLE tables and
  the following three use FSE/RLE/RLE; 8,121 of 8,188 matches are exact
  non-overlapping 48-byte copies, and the latter blocks predominantly carry
  16-byte literal runs. The FSE/FSE/RLE helper and a new FSE/RLE/RLE raw helper
  now live in separate object-format text sections. Both use an exact 32+16-byte
  match kernel, while the latter removes unused OF/ML state dispatch and uses
  an exact 16-byte literal copy. The 48-byte copy oracle checks the entire
  destination, including untouched suffix bytes; a 1,024-sequence direct oracle
  compares the specialized FSE/RLE/RLE loop with the generic decoder and covers
  retained table/repcode state, OutputTooSmall, and an invalid initial match.
  Relative to independent `3cd5ae91` binaries, fifteen five-row pairs improve
  `binary_mixed` by 2.2600x warmed and 2.1749x one-shot, both 15/15 wins; control
  medians stay at or above 0.9939x warmed and 0.9967x one-shot. Eleven direct
  warmed comparisons against Homebrew libzstd 1.5.7 measure 1.1696x median,
  11/11 wins, with a 1.0782x--1.1881x range. Three 20,000-iteration one-shot
  full-matrix samples put the same row at 1.0154x--1.0272x. All 408 Zstd tests,
  the compile gate, 237-case frame probe, 276-case compatibility matrix, and
  9,900-frame/64-mode corpus pass. The formal 13-row absolute reference gate
  remained red only on the unrelated zero-sequence `ascii64k` row at
  0.5970x--0.5994x versus its 0.60 floor under high system load; independent
  candidate/baseline matrices place that untouched row at 0.9977x--1.0027x,
  and the threshold was not weakened.
  Replaced that row's repeated five-prefix gathers with a persistent 64-bit
  reverse reservoir per Huffman stream. The next bit remains at the register's
  high end; after five symbols, trailing-zero state advances the input window
  by at most seven bytes. The helper never reads outside an individual stream
  and reconstructs the existing checked reader exactly before the irregular
  tail. The fast dispatch moved to the already-zero-sequence block boundary so
  `numbered_json` and other sequence paths do not acquire a new condition or
  code-layout dependency. Relative to a fresh `29734b27` ReleaseFast binary,
  fifteen independent pairs improve `ascii64k` by 1.5707x warmed and 1.5732x
  one-shot, both 15/15 wins. Five-row control medians stay at or above 0.9945x;
  a separate 15-pair, 100,000-decode `numbered_json` confirmation is 1.0023x.
  Against Homebrew libzstd 1.5.7, a 50,000-iteration caller-owned run measures
  982.52 versus 1042.21 MiB/s (`0.9427x`), materially closing the previous
  roughly `0.598x` gap without claiming parity. Exhaustive reservoir tests
  cover widths 1...11, byte alignments, repeated reloads and tail equivalence;
  the large four-stream fixture also pins untouched caller-output suffix bytes.
  Added an isolated caller-owned fast path for small, single-block, known-size
  Zstd frames whose sequence mode is exactly LL=predefined, OF=compressed FSE,
  ML=predefined. This is the locked 1,290-byte `numbered_json` shape: the path
  builds only the dynamic offset table and reads the other symbols from the
  static predefined tables, avoiding generic three-table state materialization.
  A cheap `frame.len <= 4096` guard keeps large-frame hot paths out of the
  recognizer, and every miss falls back before mutating caller output. Final
  independent binaries improve `numbered_json` by 1.5524x--1.5594x across
  15/15 one-shot pairs; the five-row one-shot control floor is 0.9943x and the
  reusable floor is 0.9963x. A 100,000-iteration run against Homebrew libzstd
  1.5.7 reaches 449.80 versus 662.35 MiB/s (`0.6791x`), up from roughly
  `0.439x`. The fixed 183-byte reference frame pins byte-exact generic/fast
  equivalence, terminal state, OutputTooSmall, content-size error precedence,
  zero-write misses, and all bit flips across the OF table plus sequence stream.
  Added a bounded split-literal decoder for the remaining large structured-JSON
  gap. Eligible dictionary-free all-FSE blocks have at least 1,024 sequences,
  four-stream Huffman literals, and at most 4 KiB of regenerated literals. The
  existing bulk four-stream decoder materializes that small literal set once on
  the stack, after which sequence execution uses exact literal slices instead of
  interleaving thousands of Huffman cursor reads. The helper lives in its own
  object-format text section; raw-literal controls miss at the caller boundary.
  Against an independent `548623fe` binary, final 21 serial interleaved target
  pairs improve `large_json` by 1.0963x one-shot and 1.1235x reusable with
  21/21 wins in both modes. Fifteen-pair five-row matrices measure
  1.1039x/1.1353x on the target and retain median control floors of 0.9965x
  one-shot and 0.9972x reusable; separate 100,000-decode numbered-JSON
  controls measure 0.9935x and 0.9971x. Homebrew libzstd 1.5.7 at 5,000
  iterations measures 4429.53 versus 6639.97 MiB/s (`0.6671x`) on the exact
  524,307-byte input (`b0d873df...69fd27c95`). A fixed 2,874-byte, 128 KiB
  single-block fixture directly compares fast and generic output, checks a
  64-byte poison suffix and OutputTooSmall, and matches success bytes or errors
  for 64 evenly spaced Huffman-payload mutations plus 64 sequence-bit mutations.
  The predecoded-literal executor now handles its dominant one-byte runs with
  one exact byte load/store rather than entering the dynamic `memmove` path;
  the fixed fixture requires more than 1,000 direct-copy hits. Against an
  independent `867a46aa` binary, 21 serial one-shot target pairs improve
  `large_json` by another 1.0977x with 21/21 wins. Fifteen-pair five-row
  matrices measure 1.0919x one-shot and 1.1039x reusable on the target, with
  control median floors of 0.9898x and 1.0010x; a separate 31-pair, 5,000-run
  `binary_mixed` control recovers to 0.9950x. The final Homebrew libzstd 1.5.7
  comparison reaches 4900.73 versus 6640.37 MiB/s (`0.7380x`) over 5,000
  iterations, and the gate raises the `large_json` floor from 0.55x to 0.65x.
  Multi-sequence entropy arbitration now uses the existing exact RLE,
  predefined, and mixed-table payload estimators to select the old winner and
  tie order before serialization, then emits only that representation. A
  test-only copy of the former three-emitter selector proves byte-identical
  output on the built-in text/JSON/binary token streams, generated valid
  sequences, and fixtures covering all three winner families; injected
  allocation failures preserve the caller prefix. Independent `f95aadac` and
  candidate binaries improve JSON level 1 by 1.0455x median / 1.0458x geometric
  mean over 31 pairs with 31/31 wins and the same 643-byte frame. Fifteen paired
  complete 20-row matrices preserve every input hash, output/reference size,
  and checksum, improve by 1.0182x across row medians, and retain a 0.9982x
  weakest median; binary level 1 improves by 1.0608x. A 31-pair longer
  multi-block level-3 confirmation measures 0.9969x median / 0.9974x geometric
  mean. The 100-row stage gate also now accepts zero timer resolution only for
  unavailable stages and still requires positive timing for every available
  result.
  The winner-only multi-sequence writer now reserves its exact final size and
  writes transactionally into caller output instead of allocating and copying a
  temporary block. The predefined-winner allocation oracle falls from 6 calls /
  882 requested bytes to 4 / 580, preserves byte-identical output, and retains
  rollback under every injected allocation failure. A 21-pair independent-binary
  20-row matrix preserves every input hash, output/reference size, and checksum,
  with 1.0033x row-median geometric throughput and a 0.9987x weakest median.
  Longer level-1 controls measure 0.9994x JSON, 1.0019x text, and 1.0077x binary;
  this is retained as an allocation/copy reduction rather than a latency claim.
  Reverse sequence-bitstream emission now iterates the existing read-order
  fields backwards, removing a copy into a second array of up to 3,072
  `BitField` records (roughly 48 KiB on 64-bit targets). The reference oracle
  covers empty through maximum-length lists, mixed zero-to-15-bit widths,
  invalid zero/oversized widths, and one-over-limit input. Against independent
  `49cc7607` and candidate binaries, 31 JSON level-1 pairs improve by 1.0401x
  median / 1.0405x geometric mean with 31/31 wins and the same 643-byte frame.
  A separate 21-pair 20-row matrix preserves all hashes, sizes, and checksums,
  reaches 1.0149x across row medians, and keeps a 0.9965x weakest median; binary
  level 1 and multi-block level 3 improve by 1.0299x and 1.0260x.
  Directly emitting the 450--512-sequence borrowed table plan without its
  remaining read-order `BitField` array was then tested and rejected. The

  mixed Repeat_Mode, and best-plan cases at both sequence-count boundaries; it
  also rejected malformed lengths and preserved caller output on allocation
  failure. Independent 31-pair level-1 runs measured 0.9989x on JSON and
  0.9929x on binary. The 21-pair complete 20-row matrix preserved every input
  hash, size, and checksum but reached only 0.9997x across row medians and
  regressed text level 1 to 0.9874x, so the production field materialization
  remains.
  Reusing capped 258-byte single-state beam matches at the following position
  was also rejected. The previous match proves the first 257 bytes, so the
  prototype compared only the newly exposed tail byte; a boundary oracle and
  the existing 64-shape reference comparison kept tokens and wires exact. On
  the synthetic repetitive-text stage this expanded shifted-match reuse from
  253 to 37,299 hits and improved 2.8275x across 31/31 pairs. Real 32 KiB
  README/source prefixes gained only 1.004x--1.019x at the isolated stage with
  no additional capped reuse, while the complete JSON level-1 encoder fell to
  0.9913x; a narrower caller-local form fell to 0.9883x. The optimization and
  layout-padding variants were removed because the large synthetic win does
  not represent production corpus coverage.
  Level 1 now serializes an already-computed absolute-decisive beam before its
  unchanged greedy parse, then applies the existing conservative token lower
  bound to avoid serializing a provably larger greedy entropy block. The proof
  is enabled only for the compile-time precomputed-beam/fastest-policy path and
  requires a strict lower-bound loss, so equal sizes retain the original
  greedy-first tie. A 32-shape forced-old/new oracle covers both pruned and
  fallback paths byte-for-byte, exhaustive allocation failure keeps caller
  prefixes intact, and the locked
  JSON case removes 16 allocations plus 8,741 cumulatively requested bytes.
  Against independent `46198919`/`ca8c7785` ReleaseFast binaries, 31
  interleaved 100-encode JSON level-1 pairs improve by 1.1586x median /
  1.1614x geometric mean with 31/31 wins at the same 643 bytes. A separate
  21-pair 20-row matrix preserves every input hash, frame/reference size, and
  checksum, reaches a 1.0100x row-median geometric mean, and has a 0.9895x
  short-sample floor. The two weakest rows recover in longer 31-pair runs:
  JSON level 3 reaches 0.9912x and tradeoff level 9 reaches 1.0042x.
  A follow-up integer Shannon precheck for the greedy lower bound was rejected

  The simpler exact Huffman proof remains.
  Precomputed level-1 beams now defer construction of the roughly 384 KiB
  paired duplicate index until a direct capped-prefix scan fails to prove the
  single-match candidate irrelevant. The proof mirrors the existing indexed

  `max(beam_len, block_len / 256) + 1`, preserving both equal-length tie order

  blocks build the unchanged index. A 32-shape indexed/direct oracle across six
  limits plus complete old/new selector tests cover hits, ordinary/high-byte
