  checksum at 1.0043x across row medians; its 0.9877x short-row floor recovers
  to 1.0019x on tradeoff level 3 and 1.0049x on text level 9 in longer runs.
  An exact-Huffman direct proof was rejected first because its complete match
  extension and tree construction reduced the target to 0.9329x with 0/15
  wins.
  Absolute-beam selection now also prunes the repeated-pattern entropy candidate
  with a conservative literal lower bound. The preceding direct single-match
  proof retains the exact whole-block maximum byte frequency in reusable
  scratch; once greedy is independently proven worse, repeated-pattern
  discovery finds the minimum regenerated-literal count across its single- and
  multi-sequence forms. If that count exceeds the maximum frequency, at least
  two symbols remain, so one bit per literal plus the block header cannot beat
  the current winner. Equal sizes preserve the earlier winner, and mixed-family
  24x cancellation still requires exact repeated scoring. Generated exact-wire
  checks cover 32 shapes and six limits; selector hit/fallback, old/new wire,
  and OOM oracles pass. The locked JSON path drops from 44 allocations /
  1,519,048 requested bytes to 26 / 1,283,956. Independent
  `7100fb34`/`c2b18207` binaries improve JSON level 1 by 1.1951x median /
  1.2005x geometric mean over 31 pairs with 31/31 wins and the same 643-byte
  frame. The 15-pair 20-row matrix preserves every hash, size, and checksum,
  reaches 1.0134x across row medians, and keeps a 0.9920x floor; long JSON
  level-3 and tradeoff level-1 controls measure 0.9933x and 0.9938x. Reusing a
  failed multi-pattern scan's first segment improved its isolated stage 1.0426x
  but reduced the full target to 0.9863x; a 32/8-byte periodic extender reduced
  the isolated stage to 0.9877x. Two proof placements that changed shared
  selector layout were likewise rejected at 0.9787x/0.9797x on tradeoff level 1
  and 0.9730x on JSON level 3. The retained scratch-marker layout avoids those
  non-target regressions.
  A 10-second, 1 ms macOS sample of the retained `c2b18207` JSON level-1
  encoder collected 7,978 stacks: 3,675 (about 46%) attribute to
  `single_beam.planReuse`, about 1,816 (23%) to beam entropy work, 834 (10%)
  to the direct single proof, about 837 (10%) to greedy parsing/emission, and
  110 (1.4%) to the repeated-pattern proof. Prioritize single-beam planning and
  entropy scoring over more repeated-pattern micro-optimization. A fused
  single-beam `ByteSummary` was rejected after complete JSON level 1 measured
  0.9895x with 3/31 wins. A vectorized alphabet-preservation proof was also
  removed: although JSON level 1 improved 1.0794x with 31/31 wins, the long
  tradeoff level-1 control regressed to 0.9833x with 0/31 wins.
  The single-state beam now returns an exact shifted match before its generic
  chain traversal when the newest hash entry is the preceding match source plus
  one and the prior uncapped match proves the current `L-1` length. This keeps
  the existing chain, cost, and tie semantics while avoiding repeated optional
  and candidate handling on the common adjacent-match path. A 64-shape oracle
  requires a real fast-path hit and matches every reference token and
  `PlanStats` field. Independent `c2b18207`/`b71f0ad0` binaries improve JSON
  level 1 by 1.0113x median / 1.0112x geometric mean over 31 pairs with 31/31
  wins and the same 643-byte frame. The 15-pair 20-row matrix preserves every
  hash, size, and checksum at a 1.0036x row-median geometric mean; longer
  31-pair text level-1/9 controls recover the noisy short-sample floor to
  0.9960x/0.9917x.
  Multi-sequence winner selection now obtains the all-predefined payload length
  from the mixed-table planner's already-built LL/OF/ML predefined alternatives
  instead of immediately running the same three DPs a second time. Candidate
  availability and RLE/predefined/mixed tie order are unchanged, and predefined
  winners still use the existing emitter. An exact-cost oracle matches the old
  independent scorer, while the generated winner-only oracle preserves every
  reference byte. Independent `b71f0ad0`/`7405d1b6` binaries improve JSON level
  1 by 1.0584x median / 1.0581x geometric mean across 15 pairs with 15/15 wins
  and the same 643-byte frame. A separate 15-pair 20-row matrix preserves every
  hash, size, and checksum, reaches a 1.0220x row-median geometric mean, and
  keeps a 0.9957x floor; the weakest multi-block level-1 row measures 1.0011x
  over 31 longer pairs. A same-duration 10-second post-change sample reduces
  `planPredefinedSequenceValues` self samples from 371 to 203.
  The direct single-dominance proof now collects the same exact 256-symbol
  histogram through four interleaved `u16` lanes and folds them afterward. The
  existing 65,535-byte input ceiling bounds each lane below `u16` overflow, and
  direct/indexed plus selector/repeated-prune oracles preserve every decision,
  wire, and tie. Independent `7405d1b6`/`f8d4d069` binaries improve JSON level
  1 by 1.0320x median / 1.0307x geometric mean over 15 pairs with 15/15 wins
  and the same 643-byte frame. A 15-pair 20-row matrix preserves every hash,
  size, and checksum, reaches a 1.0030x row-median geometric mean, and keeps a
  0.9953x floor; the weakest tradeoff level-3 row recovers to 1.0100x over 31
  longer pairs. Rejected follow-ups include a known-valid direct-offset scorer
  at only 1.0023x JSON, inverse-FSE-derived decode entries at 0.9992x across the
  matrix with a 0.9732x text floor despite a 1.0149x JSON target, and a 32-bin
  frequency precheck that reduced JSON to 0.9922x.
  A 1 kHz `samply` profile with per-PC leaf addresses localized remaining
  `single_beam.planReuse` time to literal target insertion and indexed/rep0
  short-match arbitration, not allocator growth or backtracking. A likely-empty
  literal branch based on the measured 30,619/32,797 empty JSON targets reduced
  complete JSON level 1 to 0.9900x with 0/15 wins. Deferring the literal state
  until the following position kept all 17 single-state token/profile/tie/OOM
  tests exact but reduced complete JSON level 1 to 0.9754x. Both layouts were
  removed; future beam work should reduce successful match-state work rather
  than extend live state or override LLVM's current literal insertion layout.
  An eight-lane variant of the retained exact dominance histogram was rejected
  too: JSON level 1 measured 0.9986x with 6/15 wins, so four lanes retain the
  better update-dependency versus final-fold balance.
  A fresh 10-second post-change sample attributes 3,973 of roughly 7,900 stacks
  to `single_beam.planReuse`, 619 to the direct proof, 514 to offset resolution,
  284 to greedy parsing, and 263 to the separate match extender. The per-PC map
  confirms literal arbitration, hash-head updates, and indexed/rep0 short-match
  insertion as the beam core. Moving the shifted-match lower-bound check into
  the finder retained all 17 token/profile/tie/OOM tests but reduced complete
  JSON level 1 to 0.9938x, so the extra out-state and live values were removed.
  Reverse sequence-bitstream emission now consumes the existing read-order
  `BitField` slice backwards, removing the former copy into a second array of up
  to 3,072 fields (roughly 48 KiB on 64-bit targets). The reference oracle
  covers empty through maximum-length field lists, mixed zero-to-15-bit widths,
  invalid values/widths, and one-over-limit input. Thirty-one interleaved
  independent-binary JSON level-1 pairs improve by 1.0401x median / 1.0405x
  geometric mean with 31/31 wins and the same 643-byte frame. A separate
  21-pair 20-row matrix preserves every input hash, frame/reference size, and
  checksum, reaches 1.0149x across row medians, and keeps a 0.9965x weakest
  median; binary level 1 and multi-block level 3 improve by 1.0299x and 1.0260x.
  Added an explicit Zstd `.fast_compressed` native-frame selection between
  raw/RLE-only operation and the full level-1 candidate arbitration. Its
  bounded per-block policy selects RLE immediately, accepts a decisive
  prefix-tail match, otherwise emits the double-fast match candidate directly,
  and tries Huffman-only/raw only when no match candidate exists. The one-shot,
  reusable scratch, append, caller-buffer, incremental, raw-content dictionary,
  dictionary-set, root facade, and CLI surfaces all expose the same policy;
  incremental encoding is pinned byte-for-byte to one-shot output with 1 KiB
  blocks and tiny output slices. `.auto` and numeric levels 0/1/3 remain
  unchanged. The generated native differential expands from 328 to 364 cases,
  the 594-test Zstd root suite passes, the 276-case libzstd 1.5.7 compatibility
  probe reports zero unsupported frames, and the large-sequence probe covers
  2,044-sequence blocks plus 64-block Repeat_Mode and dictionary state.
  A 1,000-iteration/seven-round Apple M1 comparison against libzstd 1.5.7 level
  1 measured 80/694/8,607/2,038/34,228 Vort bytes for text/JSON/binary/tradeoff/
  multiblock at 4,979.04/385.27/217.37/105.30/110.26 MiB/s. The matching
  libzstd rows were 80/838/8,609/1,967/25,606 bytes at 6,866.33/1,877.73/
  1,490.92/2,291.87/2,119.27 MiB/s. This is a useful Vort-internal low-latency
  Pareto point, especially the roughly 3.5x level-1 JSON and 2.5x multiblock
  speedups, but it is not a libzstd throughput-parity claim. The shared encode
  benchmark accepts `--native-selection fast_compressed`, and
  `run-zstd-fast-compressed-bench-gate` retains and validates a dedicated
  five-row CSV artifact.
  A frozen default-policy A/B across 15 paired runs of the complete 20-row
  matrix preserved all hashes, sizes, and checksums at 1.0081x row-median
  geometric throughput; its 0.9900x
  short JSON level-1 floor recovered to 1.0117x median / 1.0106x geometric mean
  over 31 longer pairs with 31/31 wins.
  Follow-up profiling of the explicit fast selection attributes roughly 16.7%
  of JSON samples to `double_fast.planReuse`, 17.5% to repeated-offset extra
  encoding, and another roughly 43% to compressed/predefined sequence-table
  planning and reverse-bitstream construction. Three plausible optimizations
  were measured and rejected. A fast-only RLE/compressed-FSE policy kept all
  five wires and improved JSON/binary/tradeoff/multiblock by about
  1.245x/1.116x/1.112x/1.120x, but its added code layout reduced the untouched
  default multiblock level-3 control to 0.98925x over 31 paired runs, below the
  0.99 retention floor. A strict compressed-over-predefined lower-bound proof
  preserved every wire but its extra scans reduced the complete default matrix
  to 0.9508x geometrically, with a 0.8665x floor. Finally, reusing the current
  position's already-computed short/long hashes in the double-fast table update
  improved binary/multiblock only about 1.015x/1.012x while reducing the long
  text control to 0.9800x. All three production experiments were removed. The
  next fast-mode work should avoid adding shared planner code or changing the
  surrounding hot-section layout; a dedicated direct sequence emitter with no
  fallback into the generic planner is the remaining high-leverage direction.
  A lower-cost follow-up keeps exact arbitration while avoiding that rejected
  scan: compile-time tables map each LL/OF/ML code to the minimum possible
  predefined state cost for terminal and non-terminal positions. Once a
  compressed-FSE plan already exists, one linear pass over its codes can prove
  that the compressed table's full header-plus-bit cost is strictly below even
  this optimistic predefined lower bound; only then is the predefined DP
  skipped. Equal byte costs and inconclusive codes retain the historical
  candidate and tie order. Randomized 12/31/127/256/512-sequence LL/ML cases
  plus repcode-aware OF cases compare every proof hit against the exact
  predefined planner, while the sparse-alternative oracle now requires the
  optimized and full candidate sets to retain the same minimum byte cost. The
  explicit fast prefix-tail path also reuses its existing single-sequence
  scratch and appends a <=1/8 decisive candidate directly, avoiding an
  allocation and redundant copy without changing its wire. Against frozen
  independent binaries, a 15-pair default 20-row matrix preserves every input
  hash, Vort/reference size, and checksum at 1.0161x row-median geometric
  throughput with a 1.0021x floor. The explicit fast selection improves
  JSON/binary/tradeoff/multiblock medians by
  1.1171x/1.0529x/1.0377x/1.0019x over 15 pairs, with a 1.0019x five-row
  floor. All compared wires and checksums remain exact. The final offset proof
  deliberately indexes the predefined lower-bound LUT by the original match
  distance rather than the compressed plan's repcode, and the OF oracle covers
  that distinction. The finalized tree passes all 597 Zstd tests, the 100-row
  stage gate, 364-case native probe, 276-case libzstd 1.5.7 compatibility
  matrix, large-sequence/Repeat_Mode probe, and the full compile check.
  The next profile still attributed about 17.3% of fast JSON samples to
  encoding repeated-offset extras. The canonical OF code-0/code-1 cases now
  map directly to rep0/rep1/rep2/rep0-minus-one updates instead of trying each
  extra through the decoder-side resolver; direct-offset symbols retain the
  checked generic path. A reference-loop oracle covers positive/zero literal
  lengths, duplicate and zero repcode histories, offsets 0...16, and both
  successful state rotations and exact errors. Relative to the committed LUT
  baseline, a 15-pair explicit-fast matrix preserves every hash, size, and
  checksum while improving JSON/binary/tradeoff/multiblock by
  1.1319x/1.0698x/1.0277x/1.0620x; its row-median geometric mean is 1.0586x
  with a 1.0058x floor. The complete default 20-row matrix reaches 1.0161x
  row-median geometric throughput; its 0.9757x short text level-3 sample
  recovers to 0.9954x over 31 pairs with 10,000 iterations and three rounds.
  The finalized candidate passes all 598 Zstd tests, the 100-row stage gate,
  364-case native probe, 276-case libzstd 1.5.7 compatibility matrix, the
  large-sequence/Repeat_Mode probe, and the full compile check.
  Post-change sampling reduced repeated-offset extra encoding from about 17.3%
  to the next optimization target. Canonical OF code-0/code-1 emission now maps
  rep0/rep1/rep2 and zero-literal rep0-minus-one directly instead of invoking
  the decoder-side resolver for each possible extra bit. Direct offsets retain
  the existing checked generic path. A loop-reference oracle covers positive
  and zero literal lengths, duplicate and zero repcode histories, offsets
  0...16, successful rotations, and exact error behavior. Relative to the
  committed LUT baseline, 15 independent explicit-fast pairs preserve every
  hash, size, and checksum while improving JSON/binary/tradeoff/multiblock by
  1.1319x/1.0698x/1.0277x/1.0620x; the five-row median geomean is 1.0586x
  with a 1.0058x floor. The default 20-row matrix reaches 1.0161x row-median
  geomean; its noisy 0.9757x text level-3 row recovers to 0.9954x over 31
  pairs with 10,000 iterations and three rounds. The finalized path passes all
  598 Zstd tests, the 100-row stage gate, 364-case native probe, 276-case
  libzstd 1.5.7 matrix, large-sequence/Repeat_Mode probe, and compile check.
  A dedicated trusted compressed-FSE transition builder was then evaluated
  and removed. Its oracle compared the initial state, every next state, state
  width, transition value, and transition width against both the checked
  inverse builder and the scan reference, with exact agreement. Relative to
  the frozen repeated-offset binary, the 15-pair explicit-fast matrix retained
  every input hash, frame/reference size, and checksum, but reached only a
  1.00345x row-median geometric mean; the weakest multiblock row measured
  0.998864x. That near-neutral result does not justify maintaining a second
  transition implementation with stronger internal preconditions, so the
  production path remains on the checked builder.
  Three source-equivalent follow-ups were also rejected by complete fast-mode
  measurements. Upstream-style 64-entry LL and 128-entry ML code tables matched
  the existing full-range scan oracle, but their 15-pair five-row matrix reached
  only 1.00086x geometrically, with binary at 0.99494x and multiblock at
  0.99900x. The ML-only and LL-only forms failed their five-pair screens at
  0.98961x and 0.99100x respectively on the tradeoff row. In double-fast,
  skipping a redundant four-byte extension when a shared short/long hash
  candidate had already passed eight bytes preserved every wire field and
  improved JSON by 1.01280x, but the 15-pair matrix was 0.99966x overall with
  binary at 0.99397x. A 31-pair text control recovered to 0.99757x but did not
  rescue the cross-corpus result. Finally, checking rep0's encoding rank before
  its full match scan was oracle-equivalent but reduced binary to 0.98090x in
  the five-pair screen. All production variants were removed; the existing
  arithmetic code mapping and double-fast control flow remain.
  The explicit fast encoder now commits a winning double-fast sequence block
  directly from its candidate scratch. Once that candidate is ready and beats
  the optional prefix-tail block, no later candidate is evaluated; the former
  copy into `best` and subsequent copy into caller output were therefore dead
  arbitration work. A test-only old-path comparison keeps the complete frame
  byte-identical and verifies that the direct path removes one allocation and
  at least one encoded-frame length of requested bytes; the existing exhaustive
  allocation-failure test retains caller/state rollback coverage. Against the
  frozen repeated-offset binary, 15 independent five-row fast pairs preserve
  every input hash, Vort/reference size, and checksum while improving the
  row-median geometric mean by 1.00775x with a 1.00181x floor. Binary, JSON,
  tradeoff, multiblock, and text medians are respectively 1.01177x, 1.00181x,
  1.00362x, 1.01212x, and 1.00947x. The untouched default 20-row short matrix
  measured 0.99743x geometrically; its noisy binary level-22 and multiblock
  level-3 rows recovered to 0.99705x and 0.99913x over separate 31-pair long
  controls, both above the 0.99 retention floor. The final tree passes all 598
  Zstd tests, the fast gate, 100-row stage gate, 364-case native probe, 276-case
  libzstd 1.5.7 matrix, 2,044-sequence/64-repeat-block probe, and compile check.
  A fresh 10-second/1 kHz profile of the retained direct-commit fast JSON
  encoder attributes 19.69% of 9,258 leaf samples to `double_fast.planReuse`,
  8.03% to compressed-FSE transition construction, 6.78% to sequence-code
  conversion, 6.17% to predefined dominance, 5.20% to borrowed read-field
  construction, and 5.09% to compressed-table planning. LL and ML table
  alternatives now compute their canonical code stream once and reuse it for
  RLE, predefined, compressed-FSE, and dominance planning instead of converting
  the same value column repeatedly. Offset alternatives deliberately retain the
  existing repcode-aware path: code 0/1 semantics depend on literal length and
  recent-offset history, not only on absolute distance. Exact old/new
  alternative oracles compare candidate tags, RLE codes, predefined states,
  compressed table payloads, initial states, code/state vectors, and every used
  transition; a separate canonical-value/code oracle covers LL/ML/OF through
  512 values and explicit offset code-0/code-1 streams. Against frozen final
  direct-commit and shared-code binaries, 15 independent explicit-fast pairs
  preserve every input hash, Vort/reference size, and checksum while improving
  binary/JSON/tradeoff/multiblock/text medians by
  1.03488x/1.04184x/1.02103x/1.00018x/1.00548x, a 1.02055x row-median
  geometric mean. The default 20-row matrix improves 1.00772x geometrically
  with a 1.00035x floor. The final path passes all 599 Zstd tests, the five-row
  fast gate, 100-row stage gate, 364-case native probe, 276-case libzstd 1.5.7
  matrix, 2,044-sequence/64-repeat-block probe, and compile check.
  Folding the subsequent all-equal/RLE-code check into the shared conversion
  loop was rejected despite preserving both alternatives oracles and all wire
  identities. Relative to the retained shared-code binary, its five-row fast
  screen measured 0.99501x geometrically with binary at 0.99080x and tradeoff
  at 0.98993x. The separate compact `rleSequenceCode` scan remains because its
  generated dependency structure is faster on this target.
  Small compressed sequence plans now omit their redundant per-sequence
  `next_states` and `state_bits` arrays from production builds. Final emission
  derives base/additional-bit metadata from the retained canonical codes and
  writes state transitions from the separate value/width arrays; frame
  continuation reconstructs the serialized FSE table, so the removed 1 KiB per
  plan was not part of the wire or state contract. Test builds retain both arrays
  and the existing scan/chain/inverse transition oracle still compares the full
  internal state trace. The ReleaseFast encode benchmark shrinks from 1,623,352
  to 1,606,936 bytes. Against frozen independent binaries, 15 explicit-fast
  pairs preserve every input hash, size, and checksum while improving
  binary/JSON/tradeoff/multiblock/text medians by
  1.01155x/1.01390x/1.41495x/1.00597x/1.00512x, a 1.07970x row-median
  geometric mean. The default 20-row matrix improves 1.06575x geometrically
  with a 0.99396x floor; tradeoff levels 1/3/9/22 improve
  1.36672x/1.36833x/1.15877x/1.16432x and multiblock levels improve
  1.02371x--1.09264x. The final tree passes all 599 Zstd tests, the fast gate,
  100-row stage gate, 364-case native probe, 276-case libzstd 1.5.7 matrix,
  2,044-sequence/64-repeat-block probe, and compile check.
  The remaining small-plan canonical-code and transition value/width arrays are
  now one packed production `u16` per sequence. The exact 6-bit code, 7-bit
  transition value, and 3-bit transition width layout reduces each production
  plan by another 512 bytes (1,536 bytes across the three LL/OF/ML plans), while
  test builds retain all five expanded arrays and the complete three-way state
  transition oracle. Against frozen independent compact-plan and packed-step
  binaries, 15 explicit-fast pairs preserve every input hash, Vort/reference
  size, and checksum while improving binary/JSON/tradeoff/multiblock/text
  medians by 1.00606x/1.01126x/1.25475x/1.00443x/1.00194x, a 1.05138x
  row-median geometric mean. The short default 20-row matrix improves 1.04367x
  geometrically with a 0.99928x floor; tradeoff levels 1/3/9/22 improve
  1.21528x/1.21154x/1.09727x/1.10288x, and multiblock levels improve
  1.01849x--1.05809x. A 31-pair, 10,000-iteration text control measures
  1.00629x. A clean final rebuild has identical executable code, constants, and
  data sections to the frozen candidate; only Mach-O UUID/link metadata differ.
  The final source passes all 599 Zstd tests, the five-row fast gate, 100-row
  stage gate, 364-case native probe, 276-case libzstd 1.5.7 matrix, and the
  2,044-sequence/64-repeat-block probe. A subsequent `zig build check -j1` did
  not complete: after more than 11 minutes the Zig build-server process was
  sleeping with no active compiler child and was interrupted, so this change
  does not claim a fresh full compile-check result.
  A post-pack 10-second/1 kHz fast-JSON profile attributes 20.49% of 9,083
  samples to `double_fast.planReuse`, 9.25% to compressed-FSE transition
  construction, 5.58% to borrowed sequence-field construction, and 4.84% to
  compressed-table planning. Wide borrowed emission now recognizes the
  all-compressed LL/OF/ML case and loads each packed `u16` step once per table
  and sequence, reusing its code and transition components while constructing
  the read-order fields. Other mode combinations retain the generic path. The
  existing borrowed/by-value oracle now explicitly exercises the specialized
  all-compressed loop and compares every `BitField`. Against frozen independent
  packed-plan and fused-borrowed binaries, 15 explicit-fast pairs preserve every
  input hash, Vort/reference size, and checksum while improving JSON by
  1.03105x with 15/15 wins. Binary/tradeoff/multiblock medians are
  1.00530x/1.00527x/1.00061x; the five-row median geometric mean is 1.00767x
  with a 0.99649x text floor. A separate 15-pair default 20-row matrix measures
  1.00191x geometrically; its noisy 0.98284x short text level-22 floor recovers
  across a 31-pair, 10,000-iteration all-level text control to 0.99653x, with
  the four text medians spanning 0.99653x--1.00099x. An attempted direct packed
  transition write was rejected before this change: despite exact wires, its
  five-row screen measured 0.98717x geometrically with a 0.97509x floor. The
  final source passes all 599 Zstd tests, the five-row fast gate, 100-row stage
  gate, 276-case libzstd 1.5.7 compatibility matrix, the
  2,044-sequence/64-repeat-block probe, and the Python-driven 364-case native
  probe. The latter's ReleaseFast CLI build remained silent for several minutes
  but continued consuming CPU and eventually completed, distinguishing a long
  compile from the earlier sleeping build-server failure.
  Production small compressed-FSE plans now derive transition bits directly
  from the upstream `FSE_encodeSymbol` state: the low `nbBitsOut` bits of the
  current encoder state are serialized before advancing through the compression
  table. This removes the production decode-table build and its entry lookup;
  test builds retain that table and compare the direct path's initial state and
  every used transition value/width against both the inverse checked builder and
  the independent scan reference over more than 250 generated table shapes. The
  ReleaseFast benchmark binary shrinks from 1,607,048 to 1,606,920 bytes. After
  terminating two orphaned same-repository Zig jobs and confirming an idle host,
  15 interleaved explicit-fast pairs preserve every input hash, frame/reference
  size, and checksum while improving binary/JSON/tradeoff/multiblock/text medians
  by 1.02011x/1.07119x/1.02553x/0.99990x/1.01127x, a 1.02532x row-median
  geometric mean. The matching clean-host default 20-row matrix improves
  1.00735x geometrically with a 0.99377x floor. A post-change 100,000-encode
  profile reduces transition construction from 9.19% to 5.75% of sampled leaf
  time and removes `buildFseTable` from the visible top-level hotspots. The final
  source passes all 599 Zstd tests, the five-row fast gate, 100-row stage gate,
  364-case native probe, 276-case libzstd 1.5.7 compatibility matrix, and the
  2,044-sequence/64-repeat-block probe.
  Compressed sequence plans now cache their exact canonical-value and FSE
  transition bit totals in two `u16` fields that fit existing production
  padding. Static bounds cover 512 maximum sequences, 31 offset extra bits,
  and seven transition bits. The canonical histogram fold and each of the three
  transition builders populate the totals while already visiting those values;
  LL/ML candidate scoring, known-valid offset scoring, and compressed-vs-
  predefined dominance then avoid rescanning up to 512 packed steps. The
  original stateful scorer remains an independent oracle and agrees exactly on
  randomized LL/ML/OF cases, while alternatives comparisons include both cached
  fields. Against frozen independent direct-transition and cached-cost binaries,
  15 explicit-fast pairs preserve every input hash, Vort/reference size, and
  checksum while improving binary/JSON/tradeoff/multiblock/text medians by
  1.01869x/1.04960x/1.00257x/0.99917x/1.00575x, a 1.01499x row-median
  geometric mean. The default 20-row matrix measures 1.00447x geometrically;
  its noisy 0.98771x short text level-1 row recovers in a 31-pair,
  10,000-iteration all-level text control whose medians span
  1.00125x--1.00492x. The executable remains 1,606,920 bytes, and a final
  rebuild has identical code, constant, and data sections to the measured
  candidate. Post-change profiling reduces the two dominance helpers from a
  combined 5.09% to 3.03% of sampled leaf time. The final source passes all 599
  Zstd tests, the five-row fast gate, 100-row stage gate, 364-case native probe,
  276-case libzstd 1.5.7 compatibility matrix, and the
  2,044-sequence/64-repeat-block probe.
  Two follow-up compressed-plan layout experiments were rejected. Specializing
  the generic 512-state FSE compression table to the small sequence planner's
  actual 128-state maximum reduced `planCompressedSequenceCodes`' stack frame
  from `0xbf0` to `0x8f0`, but added a second generic builder instance and 144
  bytes to the ReleaseFast executable. After exact FSE-table and transition
  oracles passed, a clean-host 15-pair explicit-fast matrix measured only
  1.00160x geometrically; JSON/tradeoff medians were 0.99934x/0.99914x, so the
  unified 512-state private table remains. Building no-previous-table LL/ML
  compressed plans directly into their alternatives slot removed the visible
  1,112-byte return copy, and the alternatives/transition oracles plus every
  benchmark wire field remained exact. Its promising five-pair screen did not
  survive the clean-host 15-pair run: the matrix fell to 0.99572x, tradeoff was
  0.98843x with 0/15 wins, and the executable grew 112 bytes. The return-value
  planner remains until a broader ownership redesign can avoid perturbing the
  surrounding entropy-planner layout.
  Shrinking only `buildFseCompressionTable`'s production symbol-spread scratch
  from 512 bytes to the current writers' 128-state maximum was rejected too.
  The existing table and transition oracles remained exact and the executable
  size was unchanged, but a clean-host five-pair explicit-fast screen measured
  0.99180x geometrically: JSON/tradeoff fell to 0.98494x/0.98643x and tradeoff
  lost all five pairs. The shared 512-byte local retains the better generated
  layout; test builds continue to exercise tableLog 5--9.
  Removing the checked bounds and signed-state branches from the production
  compressed-sequence transition loop was rejected after comparison with
  upstream `FSE_encodeSymbol`. A fourth oracle matched the scan, inverse-table,
  and checked-direct builders across more than 250 generated table shapes, and
  all 599 Zstd tests plus the fast gate passed. Frozen independent binaries
  preserved every input hash, encoded/reference size, and checksum, but the
  15-pair explicit-fast matrix improved only 1.00204x geometrically with a
  0.99097x tradeoff median. A 31-pair, 10,000-iteration tradeoff control
  confirmed a 0.99342x median, 0.99213x geometric mean, and only 5/31 wins.
  Production therefore retains the checked direct builder; removing apparently
  redundant branches perturbs this hot loop enough to cause a stable regression.
  Reserving the complete reverse sequence bitstream before emission was rejected
  as well. The candidate first validated and counted every read-order field, then
  used capacity-assuming byte appends; its copied-field oracle stayed exact, all
  599 Zstd tests and the fast gate passed, and the measured greedy fallback
  removed three allocations plus 997 requested bytes. Against frozen independent
  binaries, however, the five-pair explicit-fast screen measured only 0.99220x
  geometrically: JSON fell to 0.97364x with 0/5 wins, tradeoff to 0.98771x, and
  multiblock to 0.99173x. The extra validation/count pass costs more than the
  removed per-byte capacity checks, so the single-pass checked writer remains.
  Sharing `min(max_match, input.len - position)` between double-fast's same-
  position long/short hash candidates was rejected. A focused mismatch oracle
  covered both prefix widths plus invalid, same-position, window, and short-
  maximum boundaries, and the fast gate preserved every wire. Passing the
  precomputed maximum and window as separate live arguments nevertheless
  reduced the five-row explicit-fast screen to 0.98518x geometrically: JSON,
  binary, and tradeoff fell to 0.97630x/0.98572x/0.98318x with 0/5 wins. The
  compact options-based helper remains.
  Encoding double-fast hash positions as `position + 1` so zero can replace the
  all-ones sentinel was rejected too. It changed the two per-block 1 KiB/8 KiB
  `memset(0xff)` calls into `bzero`, retained exact sentinel/current-position
  boundaries, passed all focused parser tests and the fast gate, and kept the
  executable at 1,606,920 bytes. The five-pair complete fast matrix was only
  1.00054x geometrically, however: binary fell to 0.98639x with 0/5 wins and
  multiblock to 0.99376x with 0/5 wins. Decoding every live table position
  costs more than the cheaper initialization, so the all-ones sentinel remains.
  Hoisting canonical LL/ML kind dispatch out of the shared no-previous-table
  conversion loop was rejected after a wider control. The existing complete
  alternatives oracle and all 599 Zstd tests stayed exact, and 15 explicit-fast
  pairs improved 1.00801x geometrically, led by JSON at 1.02694x with 15/15
  wins and binary at 1.01539x. A 31-pair text control remained above the floor
  at 0.99393x. The default 20-row matrix exposed a multiblock level-22 median
  of 0.98811x, however, and its 31-pair, 200-iteration control confirmed
  0.98583x with only 5/31 wins. The combined LL/ML specialization was removed;
  follow-up work must isolate the two kinds rather than accepting a fast-policy
  win that regresses a default high level.
  The split follow-up retains only match-length specialization in the shared
  no-previous-table alternatives path. It dispatches once per ML column and
  calls the existing arithmetic `matchLengthCode` mapping directly; LL keeps
  the generic canonical-table dispatch, and offset planning remains repcode-
  aware. The complete alternatives oracle preserves every candidate tag, RLE
  code, predefined state, compressed-table payload, initial state, and used
  transition. Against frozen independent cached-cost and match-only binaries,
  15 explicit-fast pairs preserve every input hash, Vort/reference size, and
  checksum while improving binary/JSON/tradeoff/multiblock/text medians by
  1.00511x/1.02570x/1.00411x/0.99742x/1.01231x, a 1.00889x row-median
  geometric mean. A 15-pair default 20-row matrix measures 1.00139x
  geometrically. Its short tradeoff level-1/3 medians recover across separate
  31-pair, 1,000-iteration controls to 1.00863x/1.00774x, while a 15-pair,
  200-iteration multiblock level-22 control measures 1.00899x. The executable
  remains 1,606,920 bytes. The retained source passes all 599 Zstd tests, the
  five-row fast gate, 100-row stage gate, 364-case native probe, 276-case
  libzstd 1.5.7 compatibility matrix, and the 2,044-sequence/64-repeat-block
  probe.
  A canonical-offset helper limited to the packed all-compressed field emitter
  was rejected. It consumed the already validated OF code directly, retained
  the existing code-0/code-1 repcode transitions, and used `of_base`/`of_bits`
  directly for codes 2--31. A new full-code oracle covered every boundary,
  duplicate and zero histories, successor states, and exact errors against the
  generic resolver; all 600 Zstd tests and the fast gate passed. The five-pair
  screen looked positive outside noisy text, but the 15-pair independent-binary
  matrix measured only 0.99697x geometrically: text fell to 0.98386x and JSON
  to 0.99694x. The generic symbol-based emitter remains.
  Replacing all-compressed sequence field emission's per-field capacity checks
  with one exact upfront bound was rejected. Its dedicated borrowed/by-value
  oracle covered both 450- and 512-sequence plans, exact fields, one-short
  `OutputTooSmall`, and no partial mutation; all 599 Zstd tests and the fast
  gate passed. Disassembly confirmed that roughly 2,700--3,069 loop-local bound
  branches collapsed to one entry check, but the independent 15-pair fast
  matrix measured only 0.99594x geometrically: text fell to 0.98242x, binary
  was 0.99839x, and JSON improved only 1.00292x. The compact checked appends
  remain because they produce the better complete-encoder layout.
  Delaying packed canonical-code writes until a compressed sequence plan passed
  its distribution, normalized-header, and amortization gates was rejected. It
  removed up to 512 unused writes from failed candidates and changed successful
  candidates into a separate contiguous u8-to-u16 loop; alternatives and
  transition oracles plus all 599 Zstd tests remained exact. The five-pair fast
  matrix nevertheless measured 0.99342x geometrically: text was 0.98517x and
  binary/JSON/tradeoff were 0.99279x/0.99474x/0.99297x, each with only 1/5
  wins. Fusing the packed store with histogram collection remains faster.
  Fusing each packed canonical-code store into the existing reverse FSE
  transition pass was rejected as a separate attempt to avoid a second code
  scan. Production histogram collection stopped writing the plan, the direct
  builder read caller codes and wrote each complete code/value/width `u16` once,
  and its test plan was pre-poisoned to prove every code was overwritten. The
  scan/inverse/direct transition oracles and all 599 Zstd tests stayed exact,
  but the five-pair fast matrix was 0.99558x geometrically; binary/JSON/tradeoff
  medians were 0.99589x/0.99354x/0.99218x. The original fused histogram store
  plus transition update remains.
  Reusing winner-only's exact payload length to append the reverse sequence
  bitstream directly into the payload was rejected. Unlike the earlier reserve
  experiment, this path added no field-count scan: it derived bitstream bytes
  from the already selected payload length, allocated the exact destination
  slice once, validated each field while writing, and rolled back on any error.
  Wire/length/error oracles and all 599 Zstd tests passed, and the allocation
  audit removed four calls plus 2,116 requested bytes from the measured
  unpruned path. The five-pair complete fast matrix nevertheless fell to
  0.98885x geometrically, with text at 0.95378x and binary at 0.99179x. The
  existing temporary bitstream and copy remain because their generated layout
  is substantially faster on this target.
  Splitting `sequenceOffsetExtraForEncodedOffset`'s noncanonical exhaustive
  resolver into a cold noinline fallback was rejected. A synthetic noncanonical
  symbol extended the existing reference-loop oracle, all 599 Zstd tests and the
  fast gate passed, and the canonical helper shrank from roughly `0x838` to
  `0x490` bytes. The independent five-pair fast matrix still measured only
  0.99810x geometrically: text fell to 0.98281x, tradeoff lost all five pairs at
  0.99442x, and the executable grew 128 bytes. The unified helper remains.
  Zstd's specialized two-state repeat-beam matcher now rejects 12-bit hash
  collisions with one full 32-bit prefix comparison and starts match extension
  after those four proven bytes. The same skip applies to recent-offset probes.
  An old scalar compact-index oracle compares every position across eight
  generated 8 KiB inputs, while the generic/specialized beam and recent-offset
  oracles preserve exact plans. On the locked 32 KiB binary level-3 workload,
  the focused stage median fell from 633.07 to 611.50 microseconds per block.
  Five alternating independent-binary comparisons against the previous commit
  preserve the input hash, 8,607-byte frame, and checksum in every run; median
  throughput rises from 40.69 to 42.54 MiB/s (`1.0452x`, 5/5 wins). The 20-row
  encode gate passes on three consecutive runs, restoring its strict binary
  level-3/level-1 latency bound without weakening the threshold.
  The explicit fast encoder now uses a direct FSE compression-table transition
  kernel only when double-fast emits more than 512 sequences. The kernel lives
  in `zstd/sequence/large/transition.zig`; a policy bit at the end of the
  existing reusable scratch selects it without cloning or moving the general
  large-sequence encoder. Default levels retain the inverse decode-table builder
  and extensible RLE/predefined/compressed/repeat arbitration. Direct/inverse
  oracles compare table payload, initial state, and every transition field at
  513/1,024/2,047 sequences; a whole-block oracle, OOM rollback sweep,
  incremental/one-shot equality test, and libzstd large-sequence probe preserve
  wire behavior. Five alternating independent-binary fast matrices preserve
  every hash, size, and checksum while improving multiblock from 125.29 to
  232.75 MiB/s (`1.8577x`); all five row medians win, with `1.1551x` geometric
  mean and `1.0000x` floor. A separate default 20-row matrix reaches `1.0183x`
  geometric mean; eleven longer controls recover binary level 1 to `0.9915x`
  and improve JSON level 3 by `1.0100x` with 11/11 wins.
  Large LL/ML planning now generates canonical codes once and reuses them for
  RLE, predefined, compressed, and repeat candidates; predefined reachability
  intersects compile-time per-code state masks rather than scanning the full
  table at each position. A scalar oracle covers 513/1,024/2,047-code LL/OF/ML
  paths. Eleven alternating 1,000-encode pairs improve explicit fast multiblock
  by `1.0792x` median with 11/11 wins, while default text levels 3/9 and JSON
  level 9 remain at `1.0091x`/`1.0052x`/`1.0015x`. The final nine-pair
  five-row fast matrix preserves every wire/hash/checksum and reaches `1.0225x`
  row-median geometric throughput with multiblock at `1.0794x`.
  A subsequent cached-cost pass now lives in the isolated
  `zstd/sequence/large/plan.zig` module. It totals value/transition
  bits from the already-built code/state arrays and returns table-plan indexes;
  the default large planner remains a separate comptime instance without a
  runtime policy branch. A 4,096-case randomized cost/selection oracle and
  four-way 128 KiB wire test preserve exact output. Eleven alternating
  1,500-encode pairs improve fast multiblock by another `1.0756x` with 11/11
  wins, while default tradeoff
  levels 1/3 remain at `1.0068x`/`1.0054x` medians.
  Double-fast now gives only blocks above 64 KiB a bounded 64-token cold-start
  capacity before parsing. This targets the measured wide-block `storeMatch`
  growth path without applying the previously rejected input-proportional
  reservation to ordinary blocks; retained caller capacity remains reusable. An
  allocation-failure test covers the new initial reservation and verifies that
  the caller-visible token length is cleared while owned storage remains
  balanced. Against the frozen `732039c2` executable, fifteen alternating
  1,500-encode five-row fast matrices preserve every input hash, frame size, and
  checksum. The 132,096-byte multiblock row improves by `1.0057x` median with
  13/15 wins; the row-median geometric mean is `1.0022x`. Twenty-one longer
  default-policy multiblock controls retain level 1/3 at `1.0021x`/`1.0006x`
  median, with identical 27,363/27,517-byte frames. Three nearby experiments
  were removed. Folding the all-ones sentinel check into the position check won
  only 3/11 target pairs at roughly `0.995x` median. Upstream-style dummy-prefix
  loads passed an adversarial invalid-candidate oracle but lost all 11 target
  pairs at roughly `0.983x`, because address selection and post-hit validation
  outweighed Vort's predictable range branches. Applying the 64-token reserve
  to all inputs reduced the nine-pair JSON median to roughly `0.983x`; raising
  the wide-only reserve from 64 to 128 tokens was only `1.0017x` median with
  6/11 wins, so the smaller bounded policy remains.
  A post-reservation profile kept double-fast as the largest leaf and moved the
  next large hotspot to predefined sequence-state planning. Large predefined
  planning now lives in `zstd/sequence/large/predefined.zig`: compile-time LL,
  OF, and ML successor masks replace repeated runtime construction of each
  state's bounded transition range during both reverse viability and forward
  reconstruction. The existing scalar DP remains the independent oracle and
  compares every state and viability mask at 513, 1,024, and 2,047 sequences
  for all three alphabets; the module also tests malformed lengths and invalid
  codes directly. Both large-alternative helpers live in the existing wide-
  sequence text section, and removing the old planner shrinks `src/zstd.zig` by
  28 net lines while the cohesive new module remains 118 lines. Against the
  frozen `c1535ec1` executable, fifteen alternating 1,500-encode fast
  multiblock pairs improve by `1.0632x` median with 15/15 wins and identical
  hashes, 34,228-byte frames, and checksums. A matching five-row fast matrix
  reaches `1.0107x` across row medians; its noisy JSON median of `0.9889x`
  recovers to `1.0013x` with 18/31 wins in a 10,000-encode control. The full
  default 20-row matrix reaches `1.0028x` across row medians with a `0.9911x`
  floor and preserves every Vort/reference size and checksum. A first shared-
  text implementation was rejected despite the same target gain because code
  movement reduced binary/multiblock level 22 below the 0.99 floor.
  An eight-second 1 kHz post-change sample moves the old predefined planner's
  612 leaf samples to 295 in the isolated module, while `double_fast.planReuse`
  remains the next dominant encoder hotspot.
  Nearby double-fast experiments were also removed. Replacing the impossible
  forward-candidate guard with a debug invariant reduced the focused wide stage
  to `0.9866x` median; pointer-based match extension reached `0.9960x`; checking
  the short candidate before the long candidate reached `0.9857x`; a likely
  no-match branch hint lost all 15 pairs at roughly `0.978x`; and removing three
  provably redundant complementary-insertion guards reduced the stage to about
  `0.984x`. Caching literal length improved the focused stage by `1.0085x` but
  reduced the complete five-row median aggregate to `0.9975x`. Narrowing
  `storeMatch` parameters reduced its AArch64 stack frame from 128 to 112 bytes
  and improved the focused stage by `1.0046x`, but binary/multiblock complete
  medians fell to `0.9938x`/`0.9945x`. None are retained.
  The 32-state predefined offset planner now specializes the same isolated DP
  over `u32` viability masks. It reuses the low half of the existing aligned
  caller-owned `u64` scratch, so no allocation, capacity, or scratch-structure
  change is required; LL and ML retain their 64-state `u64` path. The scalar
  oracle compares every compact mask with the low 32 bits of its reference mask
  and preserves the complete state path at 513, 1,024, and 2,047 offsets.
  Against frozen `ff7869e3` and final `a3cdaeb4` ReleaseFast binaries, fifteen
  1,500-encode fast matrices preserve every hash, frame/reference size, and
  checksum. Multiblock improves by `1.0174x` median with 14/15 wins; the five
  row-median geometric mean is `1.0042x` with a `0.9953x` floor. A matching
  default 20-row matrix reaches `1.0023x` across row medians. Its noisy text
  level-1 median of `0.9823x` recovers to `1.0042x` with 19/31 wins in a
  10,000-encode control. A final 31-pair, 5,000-encode multiblock control narrows
  the target claim to `1.0026x` median / `1.0007x` geometric mean with 20/31
  wins. Two follow-ups were removed: peeling the terminal row
  from the reverse DP was only `1.0007x` median with 8/15 target wins, and
  replacing the forward non-empty check with a debug invariant was `0.9996x`
  with 7/15 wins.
  Wide double-fast blocks now emit one compact `u64` record per match instead
  of first materializing every literal as an LZ77 token and then rescanning the
  token stream into four large-sequence arrays. Record packing and validation
  live in `zstd/match/double_fast/sequence_plan.zig`, the wide-only parser lives
  in `zstd/match/double_fast/sequence_parser.zig`, and the SoA adapter lives in
  `zstd/sequence/large/record_values.zig`; the established token parser remains
  source-identical and blocks at or below 64 KiB retain that path. Wide parses
  with at most 512 matches materialize the old token representation before
  entering its bounded encoder, while denser parses feed the reusable large
  encoder directly. Compact/token differential tests, malformed-record and OOM
  checks, plus a whole-frame switch compare both routes byte-for-byte. A shared
  generic sink was rejected because it reduced the level-3 tradeoff row to
  `0.9826x`; forcing that shared parser inline was worse at `0.9214x`. Keeping
  the state machines in separate modules and isolating candidate emission in a
  noinline helper preserves the ordinary hot path. Against frozen `a3cdaeb4`
  and final `08a8dce0` ReleaseFast executables, fifteen alternating
  1,500-encode fast matrices preserve every hash, Vort/reference size, and
  checksum. The 132,096-byte multiblock row improves by `1.0746x` median with
  15/15 wins; the five row-median geometric mean is `1.0167x` with a
  `0.9938x` floor. The default 20-row nine-pair matrix is `0.9964x` overall;
  31-pair, 1,000-encode controls recover every sub-0.99 short row to
  `0.9916x`--`1.0016x`. The retained source passes the five-row fast gate,
  2,044-sequence large probe, 276-case libzstd compatibility matrix, 237-case
  frame probe, 25-case dictionary probe, 26-case CLI differential probe, all
  1,613 tests, and all 94 `check` build steps.
  A follow-up profile found compact-record growth under `storeMatch` as the
  remaining parser-local allocation hotspot. The wide parser now reserves one
  8-byte record per 64 input bytes, so the representative 128 KiB parse starts
  with exactly 2,048 records of caller-owned reusable capacity. Its oracle pins
  one allocation, zero resize operations, exact token-plan equivalence, and
  balanced release; the former 64-record seed would geometrically grow through
  eight capacities to 2,096 records. A smaller 1,024-record seed was rejected:
  it required three allocations and was `0.9984x` as fast as the retained
  2,048-record policy over 21 alternating 5,000-encode pairs. Against frozen
  `08a8dce0` and candidate `b9d62561` binaries, the retained policy improves
  multiblock by `1.0050x` median / `1.0048x` geometric mean with 16/21 wins.
  The 15-pair fast matrix is neutral overall at `0.99996x`, with a `0.9945x`
  floor; the default 20-row matrix is `1.00007x`. Its lone short-test outlier,
  text level 1, recovers to `1.0044x` over 31 alternating 10,000-encode pairs.
  Post-change sampling removes realloc/memmove descendants from compact
  `storeMatch`, and all hashes, sizes, checksums, 1,613 tests, and 94 `check`
  steps remain exact.
  The wide-only compact parser now computes each current short/long hash once,
  reads the previous candidate, and updates the corresponding table slot
  directly. This is deliberately not applied to the established token parser:
  an earlier shared implementation improved wide blocks but reduced a long text
  control to `0.9800x`. Two record-only encoder helpers now live in a separate
  `fast_sequence_record` text section, keeping the shared dispatcher and
  ordinary small-block hot functions at their baseline addresses. Without that

  Added `run-zstd-sequence-decode-stage-bench` as a separate ReleaseFast
  executable for the unresolved source-frame bottleneck. Its prepared API
  parses frame/literal sections, builds and resolves sequence tables, validates

  iterations then execute only reverse-bit/FSE sequence decode and checksum the
  decoded lengths, offsets, and final repcode state; no literal or match bytes
  are copied. Routing mirrors the production bounded/wide all-FSE split. Every
  benchmark row first verifies full decoded bytes and compares its prepared
  sequence count with the independent sequence profile; every timed iteration
  also checks the prepared checksum. Two idle-host 1,000-iteration, seven-round measurements give
  README `7.816`/`8.112`, `build.zig` `10.580`/`10.512`, roadmap `9.002`/
  `9.007`, and `src/zstd.zig` `10.092`/`10.108` ns/sequence. Roadmap and the
  decoder source differ by only 0.06%/0.16% between runs and contain zero

  was immediately rejected by this gate after moving those rows backward to
  `9.207`/`10.284` ns/sequence. The stage oracle now hashes every sequence in
  order and compares each prepared fast block with the generic decoder. This
  exposes a benchmark-only Zig aggregate-assignment alias bug that collapsed
  repcodes under ReleaseFast and invalidates the apparent packed-symbol win
  recorded in `e692ffa1`.

  3/15 wins against frozen `19ff5365`: packed loads help the isolated entropy
  loop but raise pressure when copy state is also live. Earlier absolute packed

  Known-size caller-owned and reusable decoding now use a bounded short-match

  exact copies. A full-buffer oracle checks generic output and the untouched
  physical suffix. Twenty-one reverse-order 5,000-decode README pairs improve
  `1.0122x` median / `1.0118x` geometrically with 15/21 wins; separate one-shot
  and reusable controls reach `1.0207x` and `1.0156x`. An 11-pair four-source

  The existing 512 randomized malformed-input comparison against Zig std plus

  reader progress, and error classification. Against frozen independent

  `numbered_json` pairs improve by `1.0318x` median / `1.0267x` geometric
  throughput with 20/21 wins. The warmed target improves `1.0260x`; a 21-pair

  measures `numbered_json` at 516.09 MiB/s one-shot and 426.72 MiB/s reusable

  The source-like all-FSE/Huffman executor now follows libzstd's AArch64 hot

  end, and all other paths retain exact checked copies. Against frozen

  `1.0001x` over 21 pairs; `large_json` is `0.9893x` median / `0.9974x`
  geometric and remains layout-sensitive. All 645 focused tests, 276
  compatibility cases, and 9,900 decodecorpus frames with all 64 sequence-mode
  combinations pass. Rejected follow-ups include state localization/reordering,
  a borrowed-table cursor, explicit repcode swaps, and unconditional match
  prefetch; each caused a measurable README regression and was removed.
  A follow-up localizes only the sequence counter, avoiding one hot large-offset
  state load/store without localizing the other live state. Against the frozen
  `933fd71e` binary this improves README by `1.0098x` median / `1.0123x`
  geometric throughput (13/15 wins), roadmap by `1.0122x`, and `src/zstd.zig`

  The common dense/wide sequence now shares one bounds preflight across its
  short-literal and offset-at-least-16 match wildcopies; failed preconditions
  enter an out-of-line checked executor. Against frozen `e23e8269`, README
  improves by `1.0377x` median (14/15 wins), with `1.0118x`, `1.0153x`, and

  9,900 decodecorpus frames pass.
  Added a libzstd-inspired two-symbol Huffman decoder for selected large, dense
  four-stream literal sections. Its separate Zig object keeps the 8-KiB X2
  decode table and refill loop from perturbing main-module X1/sequence code
  layout. Each 2,048-entry table slot stores one or two decoded bytes, consumed
  bits, and symbol count; four persistent reverse-bit reservoirs perform up to
  five lookups per stream before refill. The bounded production route requires
  at least 12 KiB of regenerated literals and compressed/regenerated literal
  size no greater than 0.66, falls back to X1 for unsupported trees, and maps
  malformed input to the existing errors. A dedicated 64-KiB 16-symbol test
  proves the selector hit and X1 byte parity, then checks direct-ABI truncation,
  every stream end marker, OutputTooSmall, and untouched caller suffix bytes.
  Against the frozen clean pre-change executable, 15 alternating pairs improve
  README by `1.0299x` median / `1.0314x` geometric throughput (15/15 wins),
  `build.zig` by `1.0023x` / `1.0036x` (11/15), this roadmap by `1.0243x` /
  `1.0248x` (15/15), and `src/zstd.zig` by `1.0045x` / `1.0049x` (14/15). A
  final high-load 11-pair README control records `1.0339x` median / `1.0301x`
  geometric gain with 10/11 wins. Eleven independent absolute runs under that
  load measure 1,251.43 versus 1,400.87 MiB/s for libzstd 1.5.7 (`0.8926x`),
  leaving about 10.7%; this is a real gain, not a parity claim. All 645 focused
  ReleaseFast tests, 276 compatibility cases, all 9,900 upstream decodecorpus
  frames across 64/64 sequence-mode combinations, and the complete compile
  check pass.
  The dense/wide all-FSE sequence loop now loads up to 56 bits for an entire
  sequence through one bounded 64-bit input load. The field reader lives in
  `zstd/sequence/field_group.zig`; larger groups and the last bytes use the
  checked reader. Tests compare bit-exact output for zero-width fields, every
  alignment, rejected groups without cursor progress, and directly forced
  grouped decoding of mutated upstream sequences. The prepared stage shares
  this reader and retains its ordered generic oracle. Eleven alternating
  independent-binary pairs against `ad167131` improve frozen README, build,
  roadmap, and source inputs by `1.1118x`, `1.0196x`, `1.0512x`, and `1.0709x`
  medians, with all 44 file pairs ahead. README reaches 1,388.05 MiB/s versus
  1,393.93 MiB/s for libzstd 1.5.7 (`0.9974x` median same-process ratio), while
  the other three files remain at `0.6417x`, `0.6696x`, and `0.7888x`. Controls
  remain near neutral by median, with retained host jitter on binary_mixed.
  See [protocol, results, and outstanding goal coverage](performance/zstd-sequence-fields.md).
  A Linux private-corpus profile then exposed 234 small-literal blocks that still
  used per-field checked state reads. Blocks with at least 2,048 sequences now
  reuse the existing grouped executor; the 128 KiB long-match specialization
  remains selected below that threshold. Seven fixed-CPU-5 level-1 pairs
  improve private-json by 1.6880x with 7/7 wins, while two
  PDFs and the 63 MiB log remain within 0.4% of baseline. The trace's prepared
  stage changes from 6 generic / 234 bounded / 2 wide blocks to 6 / 12 / 224
  and from 22.510 to 11.456 ns/sequence; end-to-end throughput reaches 2711.30
  MiB/s, or 0.7166x system libzstd 1.5.5. A 1,536-sequence threshold was
  rejected because it displaced the validated 1,834-sequence long-match path
  and was slower on the target smoke run.
  The grouped field reader now leaves its loaded 64-bit word immutable and
  advances a small consumed-bit cursor, removing one loop-carried reservoir
  shift per field. Against `3b81b575`, seven more fixed-CPU-5 pairs improve the
  two private PDFs by 1.0042x/1.0019x, the log by 1.0182x, and the trace by
  1.0070x; all four medians are positive and the latter two win 7/7. Final
  throughputs are 4689.27, 5411.59, 3021.75, and 2730.78 MiB/s respectively.
  The same grouped executor now selects a bounded 32-byte vector wildcopy when
  both the match distance and rounded destination span permit it, retaining
  the 16-byte path for smaller overlaps and tight output tails. Direct oracles
  cover distances 32/47/64, lengths 3...128, adaptive selection, and untouched
  suffix bytes. Against `f9e9c02c`, seven fixed-CPU-5 private-corpus pairs improve
  the first PDF, log, and trace by 1.0111x, 1.0558x, and 1.0436x; the second PDF
  is neutral at 0.9976x. Final log/trace throughput reaches 3182.47/2833.50
  MiB/s, or 0.7716x/0.7472x system libzstd 1.5.5.
  A second bounded tier copies two 32-byte vectors per iteration when distance
  and frame-tail space both cover 64 bytes, retaining the 32/16-byte fallbacks.
  Against `b401f6dc`, seven more fixed-CPU-5 private-corpus pairs improve the log and

  system libzstd 1.5.5; broad decode leadership remains unproven.
  The raw/all-FSE executor now selects the same adaptive 64/32/16-byte match
  copy only for raw literal sections of at least 4 KiB. Smaller sections keep

  Seven fixed-CPU-5 pairs against `1e8e7620` improve the two private PDFs by
  1.0485x and 1.0083x with 7/7 wins; log, trace, and `huffman80k` stay within
  0.4% of baseline. The PDFs reach 4901.08/5439.05 MiB/s, or 0.6962x/0.7353x
  system libzstd 1.5.5.
  Grouped sequence-field reads are now independent of the wide-copy policy.
  The below-2,048-sequence executor consumes one bounded field group but keeps
  its single-literal, rep0, and 68--71-byte match kernels; denser blocks retain

  trace 1.4236x, all with 7/7 wins. PDF medians and other level-1 rows remain

  The compact copy policy now uses bounded 64/32/16-byte wildcopies only for

  or 0.6578x/0.6265x libzstd 1.5.5, so further sequence/copy work remains.
  Brotli external-literal lookup executors now consume their parsed context-map

  Against `646a48bb`, seven fixed-CPU-5 quality-5 private-corpus pairs improve the

  External-literal meta-blocks now detect whether every literal block type maps
  all 64 contexts to one Huffman tree. Each command in that case uses a compact
  context-free literal loop; non-independent maps and the high-tree wide loop

  quality-5 private-corpus medians improve the PDFs by 1.3648x/1.2110x. Fifteen-pair
  log/trace controls stay within 0.3% at 0.9975x/0.9981x. Quality-1 improves all

  1.3395x/1.1929x while log/trace remain at 1.0025x/0.9980x. Absolute q5
  throughput is 248.52/221.36/1484.90/1729.88 MiB/s, or
  0.6646x/0.6414x/0.7197x/0.7134x libbrotli 1.1.0. The broad leadership goal
  therefore remains open.
  External-lookup literal decoding now batches each contiguous literal-block
  run. Block-switch checks and remaining-count updates move out of the
  per-byte loop; context-independent runs additionally hoist their tree lookup,
  while context-dependent runs retain per-byte context selection. Against
  `6843f8c4`, fixed-CPU-5 quality-5 medians improve the two private PDFs by
  1.0303x/1.0263x with 7/7 wins. Fifteen-pair log/JSON controls are neutral at
  0.9998x/1.0001x median and 1.0003x/0.9995x geometric mean. Quality-1 improves

  1.0374x/1.0257x while its controls stay within 0.2%. Quality-5 throughput is
  257.57/226.89/1482.47/1705.92 MiB/s, or
  0.6865x/0.6594x/0.7190x/0.7237x libbrotli 1.1.0.
  The external literal table now calls a fixed 10-bit bit-reservoir peek rather
  than the dynamic-width entry point. The refill, staged-bit checks, fallback,
  and cursor semantics remain shared, with a direct equivalence oracle over
  every starting bit offset and short input tail. Against `524e0716`, q5 PDF
  medians improve by 1.0593x/1.0486x with 7/7 wins, JSON improves by 1.0043x,

  1.0658x/1.0687x and quality-9 PDF gains 1.0603x/1.0475x. The weakest extended
  controls are q1 JSON at 0.9966x and q9 log at 0.9940x median. Quality-5
  throughput reaches 272.57/236.79/1479.33/1720.64 MiB/s, or
  0.7308x/0.6939x/0.7243x/0.7255x libbrotli 1.1.0. A 7-byte refill variant was
  rejected after regressing both PDF targets by about 1.8%.
  The fast Brotli reservoir no longer stores a separately updated absolute bit
  cursor. It derives that cursor at synchronization and query boundaries from
  the clipped staged-input end minus the unread staged bits, removing a
  loop-carried write from every decoded symbol. Existing scalar-equivalence,
  short-tail, cursor, and truncation tests cover the invariant. Against
  `890a53e5`, q5 fixed-CPU medians improve the two private PDFs by
  1.0149x/1.0103x, the log by 1.0291x, and JSON by 1.0206x; all 44 pairs win.
  Quality-1 medians improve by 1.0023x--1.0158x and quality-9 by
  1.0097x--1.0354x. Quality-5 throughput reaches
  277.09/240.56/1523.51/1775.89 MiB/s, or
  0.7376x/0.6966x/0.7432x/0.7476x libbrotli 1.1.0.
  The high-tree tail-lookup executor now keeps its output cursor local across
  each meta-block and writes it back on every exit, removing pointer-backed
  cursor traffic from its literal loop without changing bounds or partial
  progress. Against `546a5721`, fixed-CPU-5 q5 medians are neutral on the two
  anonymous PDFs, improve the log by 1.0160x (7/7 wins), and improve JSON by
  1.0013x. Quality-9 log/JSON improve by 1.0093x/1.0068x with 5/5 wins; all
  quality-1 controls remain within 0.2%. Brotli remains below libbrotli on the
  current corpus, so the broader leadership objective remains open.
  The high-tree tail executor now directly indexes its prepared inline literal
  trees. Context-map parsing proves each index is below the declared tree count,
  and tail preparation proves the whole set fits the 64-tree inline tier, so
  the general resolver's repeated bounds branches are redundant on this path.
  Against `1f63d49b`, the q5 anonymous log wins 11/11 fixed-CPU pairs at
  1.0054x median / 1.0052x geometric mean; q5 JSON improves 1.0032x and both
  PDFs remain neutral. Quality-1 and quality-9 controls stay within 0.1% of
  baseline except positive q1 JSON and q9 PDF-A rows.
  Prepared auxiliary command lookup is now forced into each payload executor,
  removing its error-union call boundary and exposing the following length
  decode to the same optimization scope. Against `775368c6`, q1 log/JSON
  improve by 1.0496x/1.0524x, q5 by 1.0160x/1.0297x, and q9 by
  1.0204x/1.0280x; every one of those pairs wins. PDF medians range from
  0.9980x to 1.0059x, an explicit sub-0.2% tradeoff on the two negative rows.
  The prepared auxiliary distance decoder now follows the same upstream-style
  forced-inlining strategy while retaining its output-parameter ABI and all
  malformed-distance checks. Against `b14cb65f`, q5 log/JSON improve by
  1.0218x/1.0237x and q9 by 1.0144x/1.0244x. The confirmed costs are q1 JSON
  at 0.9940x and q5 PDF-B at 0.9967x; the other measured rows range from
  0.9978x to 1.0035x.
  Standard Brotli meta-block headers now prepare the distance extra-bit widths
  and offsets used by the payload loop, following upstream Brotli's
  `CalculateDistanceLut` invariant while retaining Vort's separately bounded
  Large Window path. Against `ef4d4a86`, fixed-CPU-5 medians improve anonymous
  Log/JSON inputs by 1.0134x/1.0154x at q1, 1.0059x/1.0116x at q5, and
  1.0046x/1.0132x at q9. PDF controls range from 0.9997x to 1.0037x; the sole
  sub-baseline median has a positive 1.0006x geometric mean over 15 pairs.
  Exhaustive parameter/symbol oracles, the full test/check graph, the upstream
  7,056-case one-shot and progressive matrices, and the four-category real

  The compact all-FSE Zstd executor now extends libzstd-style bounded wildcopy
  to 3--67-byte matches with offsets of at least 16, while preserving the
  measured 68--71-byte exact kernels and the existing >=72-byte route. Against
  `d0b7486d`, fixed-CPU-5 Log/JSON medians improve by 1.1984x/1.0201x at level
  5 and 1.1647x/1.1265x at level 9; level-1 and PDF controls remain within
  0.1% after extended confirmation. A q9 Log hardware-counter run reduces
  cycles by about 9.2%, branches by 3.6%, and branch misses by 32.5%. Current
  q9 Log/JSON throughput reaches 4,071.26/3,897.95 MiB/s, or
  0.7630x/0.7056x system libzstd 1.5.5, so sequence execution remains the main
  gap rather than an industry-leadership result.
  Compact matches through 16 bytes now bypass the adaptive width selection and
  issue exactly one bounded 16-byte copy. Against `437377b9`, this adds

  eight controls stay within 0.4%. A 17--32-byte extension was neutral and

  0.7755x/0.7262x system libzstd 1.5.5; all compatibility and full-build gates
  pass, leaving the broader leadership target open.
  The compact <=16-byte match path now uses a dedicated single-vector copy
  rather than entering the general 16-byte loop. Against `3d27921e`, q9
  Log/JSON improve another 1.0029x/1.0090x and q5 by 1.0037x/1.0067x; the
  remaining controls stay within 0.6%, with the weakest extended control at
  0.9981x median / 0.9993x geometric mean. A 3--16-byte by three-distance
  full-buffer oracle and all compatibility/full-build gates pass. Zstd still
  measures about 0.73x--0.76x libzstd on these q9 inputs.
  Brotli's 9-bit in-table Huffman miss path now preserves its already-peeked
  prefix and continues out of line from bit 10, instead of restarting the
  compact decoder at bit 1. Against `d4246691`, fixed-CPU-5 Log/JSON medians
  improve by 1.0519x/1.0213x at q5 and 1.0563x/1.0149x at q9; both PDF controls
  improve 1.0163x--1.0320x at those qualities, while all q1 rows stay within
  0.2%. Current q9 Log/JSON throughput reaches 1,771.61/2,148.04 MiB/s, or
  0.8302x/0.8190x libbrotli 1.1.0. Full upstream, real-corpus, test, check, and
  reference gates pass; broad Brotli leadership remains open.
  The out-of-line Brotli tail-lookup fallback now scans two adjacent canonical
  entries per iteration while retaining its sequential per-width layout.
  Against `edd58f51`, fixed-CPU-5 Log/JSON medians improve 1.0083x/1.0112x at
  q5 and 1.0133x/1.0090x at q9; both PDFs are positive at q5/q9 and q1 remains
  within 0.1%. Current q9 Log/JSON throughput reaches 1,802.29/2,139.19 MiB/s,
  or 0.8424x/0.8374x libbrotli 1.1.0. All upstream, real-corpus, test, check,
  and reference gates pass; the remaining gap is explicit.
  The x86-64 ReleaseFast all-FSE split executors now apply libzstd's deliberate
  sequence-loop instruction alignment after Huffman setup. Against `7b246260`,
  fixed-CPU-5 q9 Log/JSON medians improve by 1.0083x/1.0079x, q5 by
  1.0090x/1.0026x, and q1 remains neutral; PDF controls range from 0.9986x to
