  0.7965x/0.7345x system libzstd 1.5.5. Compatibility, decodecorpus, full-build,
  and reference gates pass, while the broader leadership objective remains
  open.
  Prepared Brotli command/distance tail tables now use a fixed 9-bit fast-reader
  peek in the tail, small-external, and >128-tree external executors, while the
  layout-sensitive 65--128-tree tier keeps the generic reader. The wide
  external executor is 64-byte aligned to isolate its unchanged middle-tier
  specialization. Against `f9815650`, fixed-CPU-5 Log/JSON medians improve by
  1.0280x/1.0394x at q1, 1.0249x/1.0242x at q5, and 1.0229x/1.0202x at q9;
  extended PDF controls remain within 0.2%. Current q9 throughput reaches
  1,831.89/2,184.38 MiB/s, or 0.8620x/0.8491x libbrotli 1.1.0. Full upstream,
  real-corpus, test/check, and reference gates pass, but industry leadership is
  not yet established.
  Brotli command and distance extra-bit reads now take an inline staged fast
  path immediately after their fixed 9-bit Huffman lookup, while reservoir
  refill and truncation remain in the original out-of-line reader. Against
  `6ec3a13e`, all 12 fixed-CPU-5 matrix rows improve: Log/JSON medians are
  1.0286x/1.0409x at q1, 1.0201x/1.0295x at q5, and 1.0199x/1.0250x at q9;
  PDF gains range from 1.0030x to 1.0075x. Current q9 throughput reaches
  1,879.24/2,260.71 MiB/s, or 0.8783x/0.8674x libbrotli 1.1.0. Reader,
  command/distance, upstream, real-corpus, full-build, and reference gates pass;
  the overall leadership target remains open.
  Brotli short-distance resolution now uses upstream's compact ring-index and
  packed-delta invariant while preserving Vort's invalid-symbol, underflow, and
  overflow errors. The ReleaseFast helper shrinks from `0x199` to `0x80` bytes
  and loses its indirect jump table. Against `e7a87933`, fixed-CPU-5 q5
  Log/JSON medians improve by 1.0117x/1.0175x and q9 by 1.0078x/1.0092x;
  PDF controls are neutral to slightly positive. The explicit tradeoff is q1
  Log at 0.9972x median / 0.9979x geometric mean over 17 pairs. Short-distance,
  tail-distance, upstream, real-corpus, full-build, and reference gates pass;
  broad Brotli decode leadership remains unproven.
  Complete four-stream Zstd X1 tables now use a dedicated two-byte symbol plus
  full-byte bit-count entry, following libzstd's invariant that a proven-full
  table needs no validity tag. Tagged entries remain authoritative for
  incomplete and malformed trees. The ReleaseFast reservoir helper shrinks
  from `0x624` to `0x5cc` bytes and removes 28 mask instructions. Against
  `1011e1d8`, fixed-CPU-5 Log/JSON medians improve by 1.0096x/1.0054x at level
  1, 1.0084x/1.0041x at level 5, and 1.0074x/1.0082x at level 9. PDF-B is
  positive at all levels; PDF-A is neutral except for a measured 0.9980x q1
  control. Current q9 Log/JSON throughput is 4,232.21/4,073.28 MiB/s, or
  0.7827x/0.7386x system libzstd 1.5.5. Randomized table equivalence, malformed
  tree, native, compatibility, 9,900-frame decodecorpus, full-build, and
  reference gates pass; broad Zstd decode leadership remains open.
- Standard-window Brotli meta-blocks with 16--64 eligible literal trees now
  build a libbrotli-inspired compact 8-bit root plane in an isolated noinline
  wrapper. Each tree uses 256 two-byte entries; single-symbol trees consume no
  bits, and long codes continue through the existing pairwise canonical oracle.
  Against `3234bcc7`, fixed-CPU-5 Log/JSON medians improve by
  1.0050x/1.0035x at q1 and 1.0094x/1.0072x at q5; q9 Log improves 1.0076x,
  while extended q9 JSON and PDF-A controls are neutral by median and positive
  by geometric mean. Final q9 Log/JSON throughput is 1905.82/2258.91 MiB/s,
  or 0.8937x/0.8810x libbrotli 1.1.0. The full upstream, progress, real-corpus,
  test/check, and 13-row reference gates pass. The remaining gap means Brotli
  decode leadership is still open.
- The 16--64-tree compact Brotli tail tier now uses a compile-time packed
  eight-byte command metadata table derived from the authoritative 704-entry
  table, following libbrotli's cache-dense command-LUT invariant while keeping
  other decoder tiers unchanged. Fixed-CPU-5 q5/q9 Log improves by
  1.0055x/1.0058x median with 5/5 wins; the twelve-row matrix geometric mean is
  1.0009x and the largest control cost is 0.15%. Final q9 Log/JSON throughput
  is 1903.04/2250.20 MiB/s, or 0.8946x/0.8819x libbrotli 1.1.0. Exhaustive
  table equivalence, high-extra-bit decode, compatibility, full-build, and
  reference gates pass; overall Brotli leadership remains open.
- Brotli's compact, external, and wide-external payload executors now follow
  libbrotli's zero-insert command transition and skip literal-context setup
  when there are no literals to decode. Against `53e16bd4`, fixed-CPU-5
  Log medians improve by 1.0033x/1.0144x/1.0128x at q1/q5/q9; JSON improves
  by 1.0014x/1.0083x/1.0061x. Two PDF controls remain neutral across all
  qualities, and the equal-weight geometric mean of the twelve row means is
  1.0047x. Focused decoder tests, upstream differential, real-corpus
  differential, reference benchmark, and compile-check gates pass; Brotli
  decode is improved but still below libbrotli on the measured large inputs.
- Brotli short non-overlapping matches now use a meta-block-bounded fixed
  16-byte move when the logical length is at most 16 and the distance is at
  least 16, following libbrotli's first-copy strategy without assuming padding
  beyond caller-owned output. Against `7c89e5df`, 15 alternating-order
  `clustered_q8` pairs improve median throughput from 1136.18 to 1201.12 MiB/s,
  a 1.0551x paired median and 1.0568x geometric-mean gain with 15/15 wins. The
  13-row reference gate and the 7,056-case one-shot/progressive upstream
  matrices pass. This workload still trails local libbrotli 1.2.0, so broad
  Brotli decode leadership remains open.
- Brotli static-dictionary transform zero now borrows its immutable embedded
  base-word slice instead of copying into a 64-byte scratch buffer before the
  decoder copies it again. All non-identity transforms retain the existing
  materialization path. Against `d1ffc878`, 15 alternating-order
  `clustered_q8` pairs improve median throughput from 1203.25 to 1244.89 MiB/s,
  a 1.0355x paired median and 1.0366x geometric-mean gain with 15/15 wins. The
  median Vort/libbrotli 1.2.0 ratio rises from 0.7551x to 0.7834x. Six focused
  dictionary tests, the 13-row reference gate, and the 7,056-case one-shot and
  progressive upstream matrices pass; broad Brotli leadership remains open.
- Sparse Brotli command trees in the flat 16--64 literal-tree tier now build a
  capacity-checked 10-bit lookup in their existing unused entry storage while
  distance trees retain the established 9-bit lookup. Dense command trees fall
  back atomically to the prior 9-bit route. Against `206f18ee`, 15
  alternating-order `clustered_q8` pairs improve median throughput from
  1234.51 to 1241.19 MiB/s, a 1.0076x paired median and 1.0084x geometric-mean
  gain with 13/15 wins. Five-second sampling reduces observed 704-symbol
  long-code fallback from 2.77% to 1.44%. Lookup equivalence, atomic fallback,
  the 13-row reference gate, and the 7,056-case one-shot/progressive upstream
  matrices pass; broad Brotli leadership remains open.
- Follow-up probes kept the command-10/distance-9 split unchanged. Widening
  distance tables too removed the sampled distance fallback but regressed to
  0.9950x median / 0.9940x geometric mean with 2/15 wins. A fixed eight-bit
  literal peek reached only 1.0006x / 1.0016x with 9/15 wins; explicit window
  bound hoisting reached 1.0013x / 1.0043x with 9/15 wins; and 64-byte executor
  alignment regressed to 0.9956x with 2/15 wins. The 256-byte alignment,
  zero-extra command branch, trusted symbol/index paths, compile-time UTF-8
  split, and inlined dictionary-transform screens were also neutral or
  negative and were removed. Reusing the second spare command-slot bit for
  copy-extra-zero hints likewise measured only 0.9990x median / 1.0012x
  geometric mean with 7/15 wins, so fusion remains restricted to commands with
  both extra widths zero. Future work should reduce payload-loop work without
  multiplying executor instances or shifting small checks across hot call
  boundaries.
- The sparse 10-bit command lookup now fuses complete zero-extra-bit command
  metadata into the same 16-bit slots by using the otherwise unreachable high
  bit as a tag. Root hits recover Huffman width, insert/copy bases, and implicit
  distance state without a second access to the 704-entry command table;
  extra-bit commands and >10-bit codes retain their existing paths. Against
  `cf9b124c`, 15 alternating-order `clustered_q8` pairs improve median
  throughput from 1518.06 to 1577.54 MiB/s, a 1.0414x paired median and 1.0387x
  geometric-mean gain with 15/15 wins. The median Vort/libbrotli 1.2.0 ratio
  rises from 0.7923x to 0.8195x. Exhaustive 704-command slot checks, root-hit /
  extra-bit / long-code decoder tests, the 13-row reference gate, and the
  7,056-case one-shot/progressive upstream matrices pass.
- Zstd's grouped sequence-field reader now branches once for a zero-width field
  and extracts every nonzero field with one `64 - consumed` shift instead of
  two dependent shifts. The left-aligned reservoir and cursor contract are
  unchanged, and the implementation remains isolated in
  `zstd/sequence/field_group.zig`. Against `62563067`, 15 alternating-order
  complete 13-row pairs improve `huffman80k` by 1.3016x and `large_json` by
  1.1048x, both with 15/15 wins; `binary_mixed` improves 1.0036x and the row-
  median geometric mean is 1.0273x. Candidate/reference medians reach 0.9474x,
  0.8744x, and 1.1984x respectively. All 14 reader tests, the fixed raw/all-FSE
  frame, 13-row reference gate, 276-case compatibility matrix, and 9,900-frame
  decodecorpus pass. Moving the sequence decrement and aligning the executor to
  16/64 bytes were independently rejected by 21-pair or focused measurements.
- Restored the documented direct bitset/complement implementation behind the
  validated 256-state no-low-probability FSE builder after an unrelated later
  change had replaced it with a 264-byte symbol scratch, scatter pass, and
  symbol-indexed transition pass. The restored builder enumerates final states
  directly and visits the complement for dense 226/208/255 probabilities.
  Against `e15013d1`, 15 alternating-order complete 13-row pairs improve
  `large_json` by 1.0422x (15/15), `binary_mixed` by 1.0284x (15/15), and keep
  `huffman80k` neutral-positive at 1.0025x. The row-median geometric mean is
  1.0046x; longer noisy-control reruns recover `tiny`/`text` to 0.9967x/0.9926x.
  Sampling reduces direct builder attribution from 8.80% to 4.46%,
  while all major decode helper addresses remain identical. The table oracle,
  five-row profile gate, 13-row reference gate, 276-case compatibility matrix,
  and 9,900-frame decodecorpus pass.
- The restored 256-state builder now computes transition widths and baseline
  strides once per symbol instead of calling `log2(next_state)` and shifting
  for every final state. Each symbol's contiguous `[p, 2p)` next-state range
  crosses at most one power-of-two boundary; absent symbols are skipped before
  the calculation. Against `fa050e76`, 15 alternating pairs improve
  `large_json` by 1.0151x median / 1.0164x geometric throughput with 14/15 wins;
  `binary_mixed` improves 1.0035x and `huffman80k` remains neutral. The same
  table oracle, profile/reference gates, compatibility matrix, and decodecorpus
  validate the finalized implementation.
- Follow-up `large_json` probes retained the `13f323a3` implementation. A
  six-symbol width-at-most-nine Huffman batch improved the target by only
  1.0097x in five pairs while reducing `huffman80k` to 0.9306x. Grouped-reader
  fallback isolation improved the target by 1.0191x over 15 pairs but reduced
  `binary_mixed` to 0.9840x; a tighter hot/cold split around the 68--71-byte
  match clusters reduced the target to 0.9208x. Rep0 branch reordering, a likely
  hint on the 6,059-hit fused branch, a 4 KiB stack bound, and parser-carried
  low-probability metadata were neutral or negative. Register-local FSE bitset
  enumeration failed the complete 15-pair matrix (`large_json` 0.9967x), and a
  separate 128-entry width-seven X1 path was neutral at 1.0018x while moving a
  control to 0.9752x. All candidates were removed; detailed evidence and the
  resulting size-stable next-step constraint are recorded in
  `docs/performance/zstd-sequence-fields.md`.
- Caller-owned multi-block Zstd decode now skips the roughly 12 KiB LL/OF/ML
  state copy after a split-Huffman block only when a bounded lookahead proves
  that the immediately following compressed block defines all three tables
  independently. Truncation, raw/RLE or zero-sequence successors, reserved
  bits, and any Repeat_Mode field retain the established copy; repcodes always
  advance on nonterminal blocks. The hot split helper no longer contains the
  table assignment, while its caller and reusable workspace restore it when
  required. Fifteen alternating 20,000-decode pairs improve `large_json` by
  1.0254x median / 1.0236x geometric throughput; a separate complete 13-row
  matrix measures 1.0213x / 1.0262x with 15/15 target wins and a 1.0020x
  row-median geometric mean. The final libzstd 1.5.7 gate reaches 6,102.34
  versus 6,509.45 MiB/s (`0.9375x`), while `binary_mixed` remains ahead at
  `1.2343x`. All 659 tests, profile/reference gates, 276 compatibility cases,
  9,900 decodecorpus frames with 64/64 modes, and `zig build check -j1` pass.
- The compact split-Huffman loop now recognizes its dominant LL=one-literal and
  OF=rep0 shape from the already loaded entries. It skips the two zero-width
  field reads and general offset dispatch while still decoding ML extra bits;
  the existing exact 71-byte copy remains the output oracle and fast executor.
  The helper shrinks by 68 bytes. Against frozen `f131da21`, 15 alternating
  20,000-decode pairs improve `large_json` by 1.0158x at the median with 13/15
  wins; a complete 13-row matrix measures 1.0064x median on the target and
  1.0050x across row medians. A noisy `large_text` result recovers to 1.0076x
  over 21 longer pairs. The formal libzstd 1.5.7 ratio reaches 0.9559x.
- Zstd decode now has an explicit per-row performance target of at least 1.20x
  libzstd, not merely aggregate leadership. The current formal rows still below
  that floor are `huffman80k` 0.9193x, `large_json` 0.9559x, `raw256k` 0.9822x,
  `numbered_json` 1.0566x, and `ascii64k` 1.0612x; the required additional
  speedups are respectively 1.3053x, 1.2554x, 1.2217x, 1.1357x, and 1.1308x.
  `binary_mixed` already clears the new floor at 1.2273x. All 659 tests, formal
  gates, compatibility/decodecorpus coverage, and the full check pass.
- Large AArch64 Zstd raw blocks now bypass runtime-sized libc `memcpy` dispatch
  with an isolated, 256-byte-aligned 128-byte vector loop; small blocks and
  non-AArch64 targets keep `@memcpy`, exact tails are preserved, and the frame
  is still fully validated before output mutation. Against frozen `c715ffc2`,
  15 alternating 20,000-decode `raw256k` pairs improve by 1.0891x median /
  1.0675x geometric throughput with 13/15 wins. The candidate/libzstd 1.5.7
  median is 1.1716x (4/15 runs reach 1.20x), while a loaded-host complete matrix
  records 1.1304x; this is retained progress, not completion of the 1.20x row
  target. All 660 tests, decode-profile/reference gates, 276 compatibility
  cases, 9,900 decodecorpus frames, x86-64 cross compilation, and
  `zig build check -j1` pass.
- Dense raw-literal all-FSE Zstd blocks now route once into a dedicated
  short-pair executor when at most 64 literals feed at least 4,096 sequences.
  Its steady loop recognizes zero-field LL/OF symbols plus one-bit ML
  transitions directly from packed table words, rotates rep1 exactly, and
  handles the dominant 8-byte/distance-7 and 23-byte match pair without the
  general field group or match dispatcher. Against frozen `002b0980`, a
  15-pair five-row matrix improves `huffman80k` by 1.4897x median / 1.4917x
  geometric throughput with 15/15 wins; all four controls are neutral by
  median, and a 21-pair `binary_mixed` control is 0.9961x median / 0.9973x
  geometric with byte-identical hot instructions. Fifteen libzstd 1.5.7 runs
  measure 1.4217x median, 1.4199x geometric, and 1.3864x minimum, so this row
  now clears the 1.20x floor on every recorded run. The reference gate now uses
  5,000 rather than 100 iterations per row after the old raw micro-sample
  repeatedly false-failed under sustained system load; no floor was lowered.
  All 660 tests, profile/reference gates, 276 compatibility cases, 9,900
  decodecorpus frames, and the full check pass.
- FSE-compressed Huffman weights now retain a reverse reservoir across three
  even/odd state pairs before refilling, and the small mixed-FSE decoder groups
  each fully bounded sequence's extra and transition fields into one load.
  Against frozen `b55f2111`, a 15-pair five-row matrix improves
  `numbered_json` by 1.0822x median / 1.0853x geometric throughput with 14/15
  wins and a 1.0156x row-median geometric mean; control medians remain between
  0.9950x and 1.0035x. Fifteen libzstd 1.5.7 runs reach only 1.1375x median, so
  the row still needs about 5.5% and remains below the 1.20x acceptance floor.
  All 660 tests, profile/reference gates, 276 compatibility cases, 9,900
  decodecorpus frames, and the full check pass.
- Seven-bit, sequence-free four-stream Huffman sections of at least 64 KiB now
  use a 16,384-entry, 14-bit X2 table when their literal ratio is at most 0.90.
  Every lookup emits exactly two symbols, so four persistent reservoirs produce
  32 bytes from 16 dependent table lookups instead of the X1 loop's 32. Against
  frozen X1 `e92e5b70`, 15 focused alternating pairs improve `ascii64k` by
  1.3054x median / 1.3088x geometric throughput with 15/15 wins; all four
  controls remain within one percent. Fifteen independent libzstd 1.5.7 runs
  reach 1.5182x median / 1.5205x geometric throughput with a 1.4979x minimum,
  so every run clears the per-row 1.20x floor. All 664 ReleaseFast Zstd tests,
  profile/reference gates, 276 compatibility cases, 9,900 decodecorpus frames,
  and the full check pass. The remaining below-floor rows are `raw256k`,
  `numbered_json`, and `large_json`.
- The small `numbered_json` path now prepares its complete 128-entry Huffman
  lookup while assigning canonical tree prefixes, decodes 33 non-tail
  one-byte literal runs directly, and keeps a persistent reservoir across at
  least 48 bytes of its initial single-stream literal run. Against frozen
  `13bb21a4`, 15 focused pairs improve the target by 1.1604x median / 1.1601x
  geometric throughput with 15/15 wins; a five-row matrix keeps all controls
  within 1.4%. Fifteen 50,000-iteration comparisons against libzstd 1.5.7
  reach 1.3195x median / 1.3204x geometric throughput with a 1.2935x minimum,
  so every run clears the 1.20x floor. All 664 tests, profile/reference gates,
  276 compatibility cases, 9,900 decodecorpus frames, and the full check pass.
  The remaining below-floor rows are `raw256k` and `large_json`.
- The `large_json` split-Huffman path now pairs adjacent one-literal rep0
  sequences, directly handles the remaining 2--4-byte rep0 runs, commits pair
  bounds once on known-size output, and specializes its dominant 70-byte
  copies. The exact 71-byte kernel preloads its initialized tail once before
  bounded stores. A 21-pair comparison against the frozen direct-offset
  candidate improves the target by 1.0469x median / 1.0460x geometric with
  21/21 wins. Fifteen long libzstd 1.5.7 comparisons reach 1.1979x median /
  1.1990x geometric and a 1.1881x minimum, so the strict every-run 1.20x
  requirement remains open. The AArch64 raw loop also issues four independent
  32-byte loads before stores, while the reference benchmark alternates
  Vort/libzstd samples to reduce heterogeneous-core ordering bias; `raw256k`
  remains open under the same hard floor.
- An AArch64-only dense FSE-table fill now enumerates the sparse gaps for a
  symbol with probability at least 192/256 and writes each contiguous run as
  four packed entries. The existing randomized table oracle remains exact.
  Relative to committed candidate `5247b6e2`, 21/21 alternating pairs improve
  `large_json` by 1.0197x median / 1.0202x geometric throughput. Fifteen long
  libzstd 1.5.7 runs reach 1.2269x median / 1.2266x geometric and 1.2121x
  minimum, closing `large_json`; `raw256k` is the remaining locked row below
  the every-run 1.20x target.
- The 16--64-literal-tree Brotli executor now materializes its eligible
  10-bit command and 9-bit distance root planes contiguously instead of
  revisiting tail tables separated by full canonical-tree strides. Command
  metadata fusion happens while the external plane is built, and root misses
  retain the canonical decoder. A focused dictionary-copy module uses exact
  first/last 4-, 8-, and 16-byte moves for 4--31-byte transformed words.
  Against clean pre-change `ef85a56d`, 15 alternating Apple M1 Pro pairs
  improve `clustered_q8` by 1.0563x median / 1.0584x geometric throughput with
  15/15 wins and identical output; a separate 13-row run measures 0.8613x
  local libbrotli 1.2.0. The reference gate, 7,056
  one-shot plus 7,056 progressive upstream cases, 1,401 fragmentation runs,
  64 high-tree truncation cases, and real-corpus driver smoke pass. Brotli
  leadership remains open, and vector-copy, circular-ring, literal-width,
  alignment, countdown, and outlining follow-ups were measured and removed.
- The same Brotli high-tree executor now keeps its active command root/tree and
  distance context-map base in local state, refreshing them only after their
  respective block switches. Against `1124aafc`, 21 alternating Apple M1 Pro
  pairs improve `clustered_q8` by another 1.0160x median / 1.0136x geometric
  throughput with 20/21 wins; after one 0.9780x scheduling outlier, all 20
  remaining pairs are at least 1.0085x. A separate 13-row run reaches 0.8810x
  libbrotli 1.2.0. Longer tiny/text/structured-q11 controls are neutral, and
  the reference, upstream differential, and real-corpus smoke gates pass.
  Wider prepared-distance slots, context-bearing literal slots, and four-way
  distance pointer caches all regressed and were removed.
- Large standard-window Brotli meta-blocks with exactly one literal block/type,
  command block/type, and distance block/type now use a dedicated single-tree
  executor. It decodes directly from one 10-bit literal root, one fused 10-bit
  command root, and one 9-bit distance root without per-symbol block-switch or
  context-map work. Against `51d5c13f`, 15 alternating Apple M1 Pro pairs
  improve a repository source q1 stream by 1.2029x median / 1.2028x geometric
  throughput and a documentation q1 stream by 1.2478x / 1.2483x, both with
  15/15 wins. Fifteen candidate/libbrotli 1.2.0 runs reach 0.9203x and 0.9050x
  median respectively, so the remaining parity gap is explicit. The focused
  route test, 13-row reference gate, upstream 7,056 one-shot plus 7,056
  progressive cases, 1,401 fragmentation runs, 64 high-tree truncation cases,
  and real-corpus driver smoke pass.
- Packed 65--256-tree Brotli decoding now batches each insert across the
  current literal-block run, hoisting its context mode and 64-entry context-map
  base out of the per-byte loop. Against `db1eb637`, 15 alternating Apple M1
  Pro pairs improve repository documentation/source q5/q9 streams by
  1.0144x--1.0234x median with 12--14/15 wins; `clustered_q8` remains neutral
  at 1.0000x median. Absolute candidate/libbrotli 1.2.0 medians remain
  0.6378x--0.6573x, so the literal-rich wide path is still the largest Brotli
  decode gap. The reference gate, upstream differential, and real-corpus
  driver smoke pass.
- The large single-tree Brotli executor now uses a private 32-bit command root
  that embeds copy metadata for zero-insert commands. This expands complete
  root fusion from commands with two zero-width fields to the 75.2% zero-insert
  share observed in the source q1 stream. Against `bb6e2dfa`, 15 alternating
  pairs improve source q1 by 1.0403x median / 1.0412x geometric throughput with
  15/15 wins, and documentation q1 by 1.0078x / 1.0121x with 14/15 wins.
  Absolute candidate/libbrotli 1.2.0 medians reach 0.9496x and 0.9062x;
  `clustered_q8` remains neutral. The focused lookup/route tests, reference
  gate, upstream differential, and real-corpus smoke pass.
- Two additional M1 `raw256k` copy shapes were rejected. Recognizing the exact
  two-full-128-KiB-block frame and copying through fixed-boundary loops measured
  0.9423x median / 0.9575x geometric throughput with 7/21 wins; replacing the
  remaining-byte loop with an end-pointer comparison measured 0.9603x /
  0.9649x with 6/21 wins. Both were removed, leaving the committed 128-byte
  load-first loop as the measured best path while the 1.20x target remains
  open.
- A complete libbrotli-style 8-bit literal root plus per-prefix secondary table
  was tested for the 65--256-tree wide decoder. It eliminated canonical long
  misses and reduced the per-tree working set, with atomic fallback to the
  established 10-bit route on capacity failure, but 15 alternating pairs
  regressed documentation q5/q9 to 0.9831x/0.9807x and source q5/q9 to
  0.9779x/0.9819x median. The 15-bit peek and second-level dependency cost more
  than the cache reduction on M1 Pro, so the implementation was removed.

- Apple M1 raw-frame copying now uses a dedicated `zstd/frame/raw_copy.zig`
  module. Encoded frames of at least 256 KiB may use non-temporal NEON copies
  for raw blocks of at least 64 KiB; smaller working sets retain the existing
  cached kernel. Twenty-one complete-frame pairs improve `raw256k` by 1.0309x
  median with 21/21 wins, and four additional size controls stay within 0.8%.
  The oracle covers 70,656 alignment/tail/guard combinations; all 670 Zstd
  tests and the 9,900-frame/64-mode upstream decodecorpus pass. The measured
  1.0659x median versus libzstd still misses the 1.20x floor. Exact paired
  observations, rejected copy shapes, and remaining comparison work are in
  `docs/performance/zstd-raw-copy.md` and its JSON companion.

- Reusable Zstd performance evidence now compares warmed Vort contexts with
  `ZSTD_decompressDCtx`, identifies both APIs in every CSV row, and has a
  dedicated `run-zstd-reusable-reference-bench-gate`. The corrected baseline
  exposed a 1.0423x `numbered_json` gap. Reusable terminal blocks with 2--256
  predefined-LL/compressed-OF/predefined-ML sequences now share the small
  Huffman executor and borrow the cached offset table. Fifteen alternating
  pairs improve the row by 1.8151x median, reaching 1.8870x DCtx with a 1.8632x
  minimum; one-shot small JSON and large reusable JSON remain neutral. A
  first placement inside the generic executor was rejected for a 1.8% large
  JSON regression. See `docs/performance/zstd-reusable-decode.md`; the raw
  bandwidth gap and wider corpus/platform leadership remain open.

- The strict synthetic `raw256k >= 1.20x` condition is no longer a prerequisite
  for real-file evaluation. Raw decoding is already dominated by caller-buffer
  copy bandwidth, and the user accepted its smaller libzstd lead. The next
  evidence stage uses representative files from `~/Downloads`, reports
  one-shot and warmed reusable APIs separately, and retains input hashes and
  benchmark provenance.

- The first eight-file Downloads decode matrix exposed a real compressed-frame
  gap that the synthetic suite did not show: Vort initially measured 0.42x on
  a 171 MiB SVG and 0.72--0.82x on log, JSON, ELF, and executable inputs, while
  video/ZIP raw-style frames remained near parity. Production sampling found
  512--1023-sequence all-FSE Huffman blocks falling into `readModeSequence`.
  Moving that threshold from 1,024 to 512 and aligning the noinline executor
  improves the SVG by 1.3063x median / 1.3072x geometric with 15/15 wins in a
  matched-layout A/B. Five real-file controls are positive or neutral; a 256
  threshold is rejected at 0.9984x median. The current SVG still reaches only
  0.5573x of warmed libzstd, so generic/incomplete-Huffman fallback, literal
  decode, table rebuilds, and copy traffic remain the next measured targets.
  See `docs/performance/zstd-downloads-corpus.md` and its JSON record.

- The medium all-FSE Huffman executor now applies bounded adaptive match
  wildcopy only to highly compressed blocks of at most 4 KiB with 512--1023
  sequences. The caller proves output padding, a current-frame source, and
  match length/offset of at least 16 bytes; dictionary and tail cases retain
  exact copying. Against the aligned 512-threshold baseline, 15 alternating
  large-SVG pairs improve by 1.0972x median / 1.0932x geometric with 15/15 wins.
  Five real-file controls are neutral or positive by geometric mean within
  noise. Unrestricted all-FSE wildcopy, an ungated medium executor, and a
  32-byte minimum were rejected because they regressed JSON/header controls or
  lost SVG throughput. The combined retained SVG gain from `4c98febd` is about
  1.433x, but it still reaches only 0.6122x of warmed libzstd.

- Reusable decode profiling now records its API mode plus timed sequence-table
  and Huffman-tree cache hits. All six large compressed Downloads files showed
  zero hits after warmup, while the small `numbered_json` case retained one hit
  per cache per decode. Known-size frames above 512 KiB therefore bypass the
  four-slot cache and hoist workspace selection out of the block loop while
  preserving lazy allocation for raw/RLE-only frames. Fifteen alternating SVG
  pairs improve by 1.0139x median / 1.0160x geometric with 13/15 wins; five
  real-file controls remain within loaded-host noise. The
  generated large-frame oracle, 671 direct Zstd tests, reusable reference gate,
  profile gate/path smoke, and 9,900-frame decodecorpus pass.

- Zstd decode profiling now records sequence blocks, explicit/repeat/RLE/
  predefined table modes, low-probability use, and FSE accuracy-log
  histograms through a diagnostic-only parser pass. The six compressed
  Downloads inputs contain 8,143 no-low tables out of 11,646 explicit tables,
  but the distribution is workload-specific: 100% for the SVG and 20.1% for
  trace JSON. Real-file A/B rejected 128- and 512-state generalizations of the
  no-low builder. Removing the 256-state verification scan by retaining a
  parse-time count was also neutral on the robot log at 0.9977x median /
  1.0002x geometric with 10/21 wins, so no decoder hot-path change remains.
  The isolated profiler, 671 direct tests, reference/profile/compatibility
  gates, and the 9,900-frame/64-mode decodecorpus pass.

- Byte-aligned LL/OF/ML normalized-count headers now decode through an isolated
  64-bit little-endian reservoir in `zstd/sequence/normalized_counts.zig`.
  Adjacent 1--9-bit fields reuse the loaded word, and final byte consumption is
  derived from loaded minus remaining bits rather than updated after every
  field. The original forward-bit parser remains an independent differential
  oracle and continues to serve non-byte-aligned callers. Against frozen
  `b7ca21c9`, fifteen alternating pairs across all six compressed Downloads
  files are positive at the median: reusable SVG/log/JSON improve
  1.0167x/1.0118x/1.0114x and one-shot improve 1.0176x/1.0155x/1.0111x.
  Reusable and one-shot row-geometric means improve 1.0101x and 1.0120x.
  A separate 256-byte-aligned attribution pair keeps the parser gain at
  1.0205x median on SVG and 1.0190x on the robot log. All 672 direct tests,
  both reference gates, profile/path gates, 276 compatibility cases, and the
  9,900-frame/64-mode decodecorpus pass.

- Follow-up real-file profiling now records literal-section modes separately
  from sequence-table modes. The SVG contains 846 new-tree and 531 treeless
  compressed blocks; the log, JSON, shared library, executable, and header
  contain only 44/6/53/0/31 treeless blocks respectively. Five measured
  follow-ups were rejected: libzstd's generic X1/X2 cost selector was only
  1.0009x across reusable row geometric means with several slightly negative
  controls; length-aware 64/32/16-byte wildcopy fell to 0.9940x across rows;
  and batching absent-symbol writes reduced SVG/log medians to
  0.9928x/0.9951x. Incremental remaining/threshold width tracking reduced the
  same rows to 0.9939x/0.9936x, while a differential-tested `ctz` repeat scan
  was neutral on SVG at 1.0012x median / 1.0022x geometric with 9/15 wins.
  These results keep the next target on dominant split sequence execution
  rather than lookup reuse or narrower copy dispatch.

- Split-decoder profiling now classifies each sequence-bearing block into
  all-FSE split, generic split, non-Huffman literals, below-policy, one-stream,
  or incomplete-lookup paths, with block, sequence, literal-byte, and
  match-byte weights. Across six compressed Downloads inputs, no block is
  rejected for an incomplete lookup. Five inputs already send at least 96% of
  sequence-block output through a split path; the SVG is the exception, with
  916 of 1,377 blocks and 66.38% of output below the current threshold. This
  narrows the next production experiment to its 512--1023-sequence blocks
  instead of globally widening the split decoder.

- The resulting SVG routing experiment rejected 512/768/896 split thresholds:
  seven matched-layout pairs produced 0.9642x/0.9629x/0.9556x medians and 0/7
  wins at every threshold. A dedicated 512-byte-scratch executor for only the
  512--1023-sequence, at-most-512-literal subset was neutral at 1.0017x median /
  1.0021x geometric with 8/15 wins. A 1 kHz pure-Vort profile instead places
  45.42% of samples in the retained interleaved all-FSE/Huffman loop and 24.57%
  in the existing split loop. Small interleaved-loop changes were also rejected:
  fixed loop padding was neutral, a matched direct-offset shortcut and local
  sequence reader did not improve, borrowed Huffman-state variants exposed a
  large code-layout cliff, and two-symbol literal lookup fell to about 0.86x.
  A persistent Huffman reservoir also failed the full-SVG correctness check at
  a four-stream boundary. Production code is restored; future work should use
  a separately isolated execution kernel rather than grow this fragile loop.

- Added `run-zstd-interleaved-block-bench`, which prepares every matching
  medium all-FSE/four-stream-Huffman block and repeatedly executes its
  production literal, sequence, and match-copy kernel against the original
  frame history. The SVG contributes 824 blocks, 771,365 sequences, and
  107,914,672 output bytes. Borrowing its 5,240-byte Huffman state improved the
  first block by a misleading 1.1736x; the complete stage measured only 1.0137x
  median / 1.0122x geometric, and the longer complete frame only 1.0044x /
  1.0030x with 10/15 wins. The production change was removed; the stage remains
  as a representative lower-noise screen before complete-frame acceptance.

- The aggregate medium-block stage rejected another set of apparently common
  shortcuts. A hybrid Huffman state with a local cursor and borrowed immutable
  tables removed the 5,240-byte entry copy and improved the stage by 1.0132x
  median / 1.0115x geometric with 14/15 wins, but complete-frame reusable
  decode reached only 1.0051x / 1.0059x; normalization by the simultaneously
  measured libzstd control leaves 1.0016x geometric, so it was removed. Shape
  profiling found no <=512-literal target blocks, 596/824 <=1 KiB and 818/824
  <=2 KiB, yet both dedicated split-staging sizes reduced the complete-frame
  Vort/libzstd snapshot to about 0.60x. Aggregate screens also rejected a
  128-byte match wildcopy (0.9442x broad, 0.9655x long-only), an exact 48-byte
  match branch (0.9629x), and a two-sequence zero-bit-offset path (0.9666x).
  Production code is restored. Future work should shorten the existing
  interleaved dependency chain without another per-sequence dispatch branch or
  separate literal-copy pass.

- Per-PC sampling now divides the medium interleaved executor into 44.73%
  sequence-field/repcode work, 33.44% Huffman literal work, 19.89% match work,
  and 1.94% tail/exit work. The file-backed sequence-stage benchmark accepts
  256 MiB inputs and measures all 1,287,096 SVG sequences at 12.882 ns each.
  All 824 medium blocks prove a <=53-bit table maximum; 765,970/771,365 actual
  sequences take the 64-bit group path and the other 5,395 are block tails.
  Nevertheless, retaining that proof was neutral at 1.0012x. Three alternative
  group extraction forms measured 0.9698x, 0.9720x, and 0.9939x; local
  repcodes measured 0.9116x, a corrected persistent Huffman reservoir 0.9919x,
  and removing the medium instance's fixed-71 branch 0.9786x. All were removed.
  This closes more local rewrites and points the next work toward a genuinely
  smaller sequence-state representation or separately compiled executor.

- Added that separately compiled medium split executor for dictionary-free,
  known-size, 512--1023-sequence all-FSE/four-stream-Huffman blocks with at
  most 4 KiB of literals. Its 3.6 KiB machine-code body predecodes literals
  once and keeps only grouped sequence fields, short literal copies, adaptive
  match wildcopy, and a checked fallback; the established interleaved and
  general split helpers remain isolated. Across all 824 SVG blocks the stage
  improves 1.2484x median / 1.2451x geometric with 15/15 wins. Complete SVG
  reusable decode improves 1.1240x / 1.1226x and one-shot improves 1.1173x /
  1.1189x, both 15/15; normalized gains remain 1.1198x and 1.1210x. Five
  15-pair real compressed-file controls are neutral or positive geometrically,
  with robot log improving 1.0181x after normalization. The six-file reusable
  geometric ratio rises from 0.7579x to 0.7755x libzstd. Final policy cleanup
  preserves byte-identical medium-executor and reusable-dispatch disassembly
  against the measured candidate.

- Medium all-FSE/four-stream-Huffman blocks now have a separate 4 KiB-literal
  split executor instead of adding more branches to the 4.8 KiB interleaved or
  7.9 KiB general split helpers. It expands literals once, then keeps only the
  grouped FSE loop, short literal copy, adaptive match wildcopy, and checked
  fallback. The 824-block SVG stage improves 1.2484x median / 1.2451x geometric
  with 15/15 wins; complete reusable and one-shot frames improve 1.1240x /
  1.1226x and 1.1173x / 1.1189x, both 15/15. After simultaneous libzstd-control
  normalization the geometric gains remain 1.1198x and 1.1210x. Reusable Vort
  reaches 6,800.1 MiB/s and 0.7072x libzstd on the SVG. Fifteen-pair robot-log,
  trace-JSON, shared-library, executable, and header controls are neutral or
  positive geometrically after normalization; the six-file compressed-corpus
  geometric ratio rises from 0.7579x to 0.7755x. The direct executor oracle,
  all 675 Zstd tests, 276 compatibility cases, 9,900 decodecorpus frames, both
  reference gates, and x86_64 Linux compile-only validation pass. The broad
  `zig build check -j1` was stopped after six silent minutes, matching the
  repository's known build-server stall rather than reporting a false pass. A
  post-change 10,702-sample profile moves the leading leaves to the compact
  medium executor at 35.42% and the established large split executor at 27.44%;
  their common sequence/copy core is now the next optimization target.

- Extended the compact split route through 1,535 sequences after the
  production-selected stage showed that 457/461 SVG large blocks fall in this
  range, while the 1,834-sequence synthetic `large_json` fixture remains on its
  tuned path. The large-block stage screen improves 1.2562x. Fifteen complete
  SVG pairs improve reusable decode by 1.0866x median / 1.0860x geometric and
  one-shot by 1.0872x / 1.0868x, both 15/15; normalized gains remain 1.0914x
  and 1.0869x. Five 15-pair real-file controls have normalized geometric means
  between 1.0002x and 1.0026x. SVG now reaches 0.7754x libzstd reusable and the
  six compressed-file geometric mean reaches 0.7881x. The 675-test suite and
  9,900-frame decodecorpus pass on the final source. A new 9,534-sample profile
  puts 63.19% in the compact executor and only 1.00% in the displaced large
  split helper, making the compact loop itself the next optimization target.

- The compact split executor now keeps its LL/ML/OF FSE states in three scalar
  locals and commits them only after the block succeeds. This removes the
  per-sequence state-pointer reload/store chain across literal and match copies
  without changing routing or adding a shape branch. Against frozen
  `f9403697`/`f9ec1c79` stage binaries, 21 alternating full-stage pairs improve
  1.0152x median / 1.0160x geometric with 19/21 wins; independent medium and
  large ranges improve 1.0125x and 1.0159x geometrically. Fifteen complete SVG
  pairs improve 1.0144x reusable and 1.0111x one-shot geometrically after the
  simultaneous libzstd control, both with 14/15 normalized wins. Five 15-pair
  real-file controls are neutral at a 1.0002x normalized row-geometric mean.
  SVG reaches 0.7855x libzstd reusable and 0.7867x one-shot, while the six-file
  compressed-corpus geometric means reach 0.7898x/0.7922x. A packed-`u32`
  variant was rejected at 0.9683x geometric with 0/11 wins. All 675 direct Zstd
  tests, both 13-row reference gates, 276 compatibility cases, 9,900
  decodecorpus frames, and x86_64 Linux ReleaseFast compile-only validation
  pass. The remaining work stays inside grouped-field extraction and match copy.

- The compact split executor now also advances a local output cursor instead
  of passing the caller-owned `written` pointer through every literal and match
  copy. This removes an output-alias reload/store chain while a `defer` commits
  the cursor on both success and error, preserving partial-progress behavior.
  Frozen 256-byte-aligned stage binaries improve 1.0997x median / 1.1022x
  geometric across 21 alternating pairs with 21/21 wins; independent medium
  and large ranges improve 1.0985x/1.1003x geometrically with 15/15 wins each.
  Complete SVG decode improves 1.0804x reusable and 1.0698x one-shot
  geometrically, or 1.0755x/1.0727x after simultaneous libzstd normalization,
  with every pair ahead. Five 15-pair real-file controls are all neutral to
  positive at a 1.0017x normalized row-geometric mean. SVG reaches 0.8465x
  libzstd reusable and 0.8431x one-shot; the six compressed-file geometric
  means reach 0.7997x/0.8014x. A success-only cursor commit was rejected at
  0.9917x geometric. The 675-test suite, both reference gates, 276 compatibility
  cases, 9,900 decodecorpus frames, and x86_64 Linux compile-only validation
  pass; grouped-field extraction and match copy remain the next hot-loop work.

- Re-evaluated the compact split threshold after its local-state and output-
  cursor optimizations. Starting at 128 rather than 512 sequences selects 88
  additional SVG blocks with 19,238 sequences and 10.4 MiB of output. Their
  frozen stage improves 1.4176x median / 1.4212x geometric with 15/15 wins.
  Complete SVG improves 1.1000x reusable and 1.1058x one-shot geometrically,
  or 1.0960x/1.0978x after simultaneous libzstd normalization, with every pair
  ahead. Five real compressed-file controls have a 1.0049x normalized row-
  geometric mean after extending the noisy header control to 31 pairs. SVG now
  reaches 0.8592x libzstd reusable and 0.8601x one-shot; six-file compressed-
  corpus geometric means reach 0.8017x/0.8041x. Persistent sequence-field
  reservoir, local remaining-bit cursor, direct offset specialization,
  libzstd-style 16+32 wildcopy, and AArch64 64-byte loop alignment experiments
  were all rejected and removed. All 675 tests, both reference gates, 276
  compatibility cases, 9,900 decodecorpus frames, and x86_64 Linux compile-only
  validation pass on the retained route-only change.

- Extended the compact upper bound from 1,535 to 4,095 only for high-sequence,
  low-literal blocks: literals must be non-zero, at most 2 KiB, and fewer than
  the sequence count. Literal-limit-only variants were rejected because a
  2 KiB gate selected two `large_json` blocks and reduced matched-layout one-
  shot/reusable controls to 0.9175x/0.9337x, while a 1 KiB gate improved the
  header frame only 1.0028x. The retained density invariant rejects those
  `large_json` blocks while improving the matched-layout header stage by
  1.0249x geometric and the complete reusable frame by 1.0180x, both 15/15.
  Robot and `large_json` controls remain within 0.06%; SVG, trace, shared-
  library, and executable controls stay within 0.14%. The header reaches
  0.7831x/0.7765x libzstd one-shot/reusable and the six-file compressed-corpus
  geometric means reach 0.8104x/0.8074x. All 675 tests, both reference gates,
  276 compatibility cases, 9,900 decodecorpus frames, and x86_64 Linux compile-
  only validation pass. Robot remains the primary generic-heavy target.

- Replaced the production dense split instantiation of the multi-policy
  sequence template with a dedicated grouped-FSE core. It retains padded
  four-stream Huffman staging, short/bulk literal wildcopy, adaptive match
  wildcopy, and a checked cold fallback, while dropping the small-copy pair,
  fixed-length, and non-grouped branches. The generic dense instantiation stays
  as a direct oracle covering exact output, reader position, LL/ML/OF state,
  and repcodes. Frozen stage binaries improve robot/header by 1.0432x/1.0610x
  geometrically with 15/15 wins. Complete reusable frames improve 1.0269x/
  1.0515x after libzstd normalization; one-shot improves 1.0268x/1.0482x, all
  15/15. SVG, trace, shared-library, and executable reusable controls improve
  1.0051x/1.0447x/1.0077x/1.0100x; `large_json` remains neutral. Loaded-host
  six-file ratios reach 0.8318x one-shot and 0.8255x reusable. All 675 tests,
  both reference gates, 276 compatibility cases, 9,900 decodecorpus frames,
  and x86_64 Linux compile-only validation pass.

- Extended the existing 11-bit Huffman X2 decoder only to the measured
  1,536--2,047-sequence band when regenerated literals are at least 4 KiB,
  average at least four bytes per sequence, and the four compressed streams
  occupy at most 55% of them. Fifteen alternating robot-log pairs improve
  reusable decode by 1.0360x median / 1.0362x geometric and one-shot by
  1.0373x / 1.0370x, both 15/15; libzstd-normalized geometric gains remain
  1.0366x/1.0377x. Five 15-pair reusable controls remain within 0.16% of
  neutral geometrically after normalization except SVG at +0.28%. Robot-log
  median Vort/libzstd throughput rises from 0.7827x to 0.8128x reusable and
  0.7956x to 0.8261x one-shot. The final source passes 495 direct Zstd tests
  plus the isolated selector test, both 13-row reference gates, 276
  compatibility cases, all 9,900 decodecorpus frames with complete 64-mode
  coverage, and x86-64 Linux ReleaseFast compile-only validation. This closes
  another bounded Huffman table-amortization gap; compressed real files still
  trail libzstd by roughly 12--19%, so broader leadership remains open.

- Added an x86-64 ERMSB path for complete 128 KiB Zstd raw blocks. The narrow
  size gate leaves shorter copies, non-ERMSB x86 targets, and the established
  Apple M1 policy unchanged. Against frozen `21683c9c` and the local
  `~/Work/zstd` 1.6.0-dev checkout, 15 fixed-CPU alternating pairs improve
  `raw256k` by 1.3469x median / 1.3455x geometric mean with 15/15 wins. The
  final Vort path is 1.0355x/1.0357x versus libzstd and wins every pair, closing
  this bounded x86 raw-block gap. All 676 direct Zstd tests, 276 compatibility
  cases, the 9,900-frame/64-mode decodecorpus, and generic x86-64/AArch64
  compile checks pass. Exact observations are in
  `docs/performance/zstd-raw-copy-x86.md` and its JSON companion; compressed
  sequence-heavy rows remain the next priority.

- Reusable small Zstd frames now cache each parsed Huffman tree together with
  its complete seven-bit lookup and borrow that lookup, the tree, and the
  cached FSE offset table through a validated terminal-block path. A local
  output cursor is compiled only into the reusable executor. Against frozen
  `fc59ccaf` and local libzstd 1.6.0-dev, 15 fixed-CPU `numbered_json` pairs
  improve by 1.1829x median / 1.1853x geometric mean with 15/15 wins; Vort
  reaches 1.0064x/1.0109x of libzstd by median/geometric mean. Nine one-shot
  controls improve 1.0197x/1.0198x but remain 0.7830x of libzstd. The full
  correctness and corpus gates are recorded in
  `docs/performance/zstd-small-reusable-cache-x86.md`; one-shot table building
  and large compressed sequence paths remain open.

- Small one-shot Zstd frames now parse their literal header/tree/streams
  directly and size Huffman-weight and table-log-five offset-FSE scratch to the
  format's actual 64/12 and 32/32 bounds. Against frozen `9b6bdf76`, 15
  fixed-CPU `numbered_json` pairs improve by 1.0278x median / 1.0269x geometric
  mean with 15/15 wins and a 1.0022x minimum. The final path reaches only
  0.8069x/0.8057x of local libzstd 1.6.0-dev by median/geometric mean, so the
  result closes a bounded table-construction cost without claiming one-shot
  leadership. All 676 direct tests, the 276-case compatibility matrix,
  9,900-frame/64-mode decodecorpus, 13-row reference gate, and generic
  x86-64/AArch64 compile checks pass. Exact evidence is in
  `docs/performance/zstd-small-oneshot-tables-x86.md`; broader Huffman table
  construction and large compressed sequence paths remain open.

- The small one-shot path now passes compact borrowed literal metadata instead
  of constructing a generic section with an unused owned Huffman tree. Frozen
  x86-64 disassembly shows its stack frame shrinking from `0xad8` to `0x6c8`
  bytes and removes a `0x404`-byte clear. Against frozen `e9cad21b`, 15
  fixed-CPU `numbered_json` pairs improve by 1.1419x median / 1.1410x geometric
  mean with 15/15 wins and a 1.1317x minimum; Vort reaches 0.9203x/0.9215x of
  local libzstd 1.6.0-dev by median/geometric mean. All 676 direct tests, the
  276-case compatibility matrix, 9,900-frame/64-mode decodecorpus, 13-row
  reference gate, and generic x86-64/AArch64 compile checks pass. Exact evidence
  is in `docs/performance/zstd-small-borrowed-section-x86.md`; direct narrow
  lookup construction and checked lookup-only stream tails are the next small-
  frame opportunities.

- The same one-shot path now constructs a complete seven-bit Huffman lookup
  directly from direct or FSE-compressed weights, without materializing an
  owned tree, and decodes stream tails only after checking the selected code
  width against remaining bits. The common table-log-five weight stream also
  receives a bounded 32-state decoder. Against frozen `6e287126`, 15 fixed-CPU
  `numbered_json` pairs improve by 1.0805x median / 1.0797x geometric mean with
  15/15 wins and a 1.0654x minimum. Vort reaches 0.9911x median of local
  libzstd 1.6.0-dev, with one observed lead but no stable parity claim. Random
  parser acceptance, exact lookup tables, full literal-payload bit mutation,
  676 direct tests, the 276-case matrix, 9,900-frame/64-mode decodecorpus,
  13-row reference gate, and generic x86-64/AArch64 builds pass. Exact evidence
  is in `docs/performance/zstd-small-direct-lookup-x86.md`; normalized-count
  parsing and canonical fill remain the final small-frame setup targets before
  returning to large compressed sequence paths.

- The x86-64 compact split-Huffman pair path now copies its 71-byte match with
  two 32-byte moves and an exact eight-byte tail at offsets 63--70. The
  one-byte overlap stays inside the logical destination and removes the former
  suffix load/merge. Against frozen `89ce6618`, 15 fixed-CPU `large_json`
  pairs improve by 1.0096x median / 1.0105x geometric mean with 14/15 wins;
  a nearby 1,835-sequence prepared stage improves 1.0032x geometrically with
  10/15 wins. The final row remains only 0.7940x local libzstd 1.6.0-dev, so
  the broader gap remains open. The 677-test suite, 276-case matrix,
  9,900-frame/64-mode decodecorpus, 13-row reference gate, and generic
  x86-64/AArch64 builds pass. Exact evidence is in
  `docs/performance/zstd-large-json-overlap-tail-x86.md`.

- The dense 256-state no-low-probability FSE table builder now uses its sparse-
  gap, four-entry packed fill on x86-64 as well as AArch64. Against frozen
  `4c7c3db0`, 15 fixed-CPU `large_json` pairs improve by 1.0175x median /
  1.0183x geometric mean with 15/15 wins and a 1.0051x minimum. A seven-pair
  matrix also improves `binary_mixed` by 1.0178x geometrically with 7/7 wins;
  large Huffman/text controls remain near neutral. Thresholds 160 and 224 and
  an eight-entry write batch were independently slower and removed. All 677
  direct tests, the 276-case compatibility matrix, 9,900-frame/64-mode
  decodecorpus, 13-row reference gate, and generic x86-64/AArch64 builds pass.
  Exact evidence is in `docs/performance/zstd-dense-fse-x86.md`; large compressed
  sequence execution remains below libzstd on this host.

- The large raw-literal FSE/FSE/RLE sequence executor now borrows its literal
  payload directly, removes an impossible Huffman-state branch, and uses an
  exact 16-byte vector copy for the dominant `binary_mixed` literal length.
  Its frozen x86-64 symbol shrinks by 896 bytes. Against frozen `f7e95936`, 15
  alternating fixed-CPU pairs improve complete `binary_mixed` decode by
  1.0968x median / 1.0954x geometric mean with 15/15 wins and a 1.0874x
  minimum. A seven-pair complete 13-row matrix confirms 1.0985x geometric on
  the target, keeps `large_json`/`huffman80k` neutral-positive, and has a
  0.9941x row-median floor. Vort still reaches only 0.8946x median local
  libzstd 1.6.0-dev throughput, so broader sequence-decode leadership remains
  open. The direct generic oracle, all 678 Zstd tests, profile/reference gates,
  276 compatibility cases, 9,900 decodecorpus frames with 64/64 modes,
  generic x86-64/AArch64 builds, and full repository check pass. Exact evidence
  is in `docs/performance/zstd-fse-fse-rle-raw-x86.md`.

- The following three raw-literal FSE/RLE/RLE blocks now execute their dominant
  16-byte-literal/48-byte-match shape two sequences at a time. A separate
  656-byte core validates both LL entries, six extra/transition fields, rep0,
  literal/output bounds, and history from one 64-bit reverse group before
  committing progress; any mismatch retains the original single-sequence
  decoder. Against frozen `df5d2b84`, 15 alternating fixed-CPU pairs improve
  complete `binary_mixed` decode by 1.4299x median / 1.4290x geometric with
  15/15 wins and a 1.4117x minimum. Vort reaches 1.2831x median / 1.2829x
  geometric local libzstd 1.6.0-dev throughput, wins all 15 pairs, and has a
  1.2745x floor, establishing a bounded shape-specific lead. A seven-pair
  13-row matrix has a 0.9941x row-median floor; separate 15-pair `large_json`,
  `large_text`, and `huffman80k` controls remain near neutral. Exact partial-
  progress oracles, all 678 Zstd tests, profile/reference gates, 276
  compatibility cases, 9,900 corpus frames with 64/64 modes, generic
  x86-64/AArch64 builds, and the full repository check pass. Exact evidence is
  in `docs/performance/zstd-fse-rle-rle-pair-x86.md`.

- Re-profiled the remaining x86-64 `large_json` gap against local libzstd
  1.6.0-dev. Vort remains at 0.8045x median reference throughput; four prepared
  split blocks account for about 92% of complete-frame time. Frozen stage and
  frame A/B rejected an external pair run (0.7728x geometric), inline pair run
  (0.9535x), same-length pair fusion (0.9918x median), local FSE states
  (0.9620x geometric), low-literal X2 (0.9943x median), wider lookup fills
  (1.0028x geometric), and width-ten six-symbol batching: the latter reached
  1.0085x on the isolated stage but only 1.0030x on the complete frame and
  0.9988x after libzstd normalization. A long distance-82 exact-64 copy for
  `large_text` was decisively worse at 0.5689x. All production candidates were
  removed. Exact shapes, hashes, safety findings, and commands are in
  `docs/performance/zstd-large-json-followups-x86.md`; the next credible step is
  a genuinely smaller split executor/state representation rather than another
  local branch or copy variant.

- Flat 16--64-literal-tree Brotli meta-blocks with at most four command trees
  now reuse the single-tree executor's 32-bit zero-insert command root for each
  command block type. The root embeds copy bases, copy extra-bit widths, and
  implicit-distance state; command-tree switches refresh the cached root while
  the established canonical fallbacks preserve malformed/truncated behavior.
  Against frozen `52fb2bf9`, 15 alternating fixed-CPU-2 `clustered_q8` pairs
  improve by 1.0152x median / 1.0210x geometric throughput with 14/15 wins;
  libbrotli-normalized gains are 1.0197x / 1.0150x. Candidate throughput is
  still only 0.8450x median local libbrotli 1.2.0-dev, so broad leadership is
  not claimed. A seven-pair 13-row matrix has a 1.0031x row-median geometric
  mean; longer controls expose a bounded 0.7% geometric cost on `structured`,
  neutral `repetitive_q11`, and neutral-positive `structured_q11`. All 540
  direct Brotli tests, the 13-row reference gate, 7,056 one-shot and 7,056
  progressive upstream cases, 1,401 fragmentation cases, 64 high-tree
  truncations, seven Large Window cases, and the real-corpus differential pass.
  The full repository check also passes. Exact evidence and the rejected
  literal-block batching precursor are in
  `docs/performance/brotli-multi-tree-zero-insert-x86.md` and its JSON record.

- Nine follow-ups to the retained multi-tree Brotli command root were measured
  against its frozen binary and removed. Restricting the route to multiple
  command types was neutral at 1.0000x median / 0.9986x geometric and did not
  recover a stable single-tree control cost. Removing countdown or block-type
  guards was likewise neutral. Direct lookup construction cut the setup helper
  from `0xb19` to `0x459` bytes but regressed the complete frame to 0.9894x
  geometric. Direct dictionary output, broader zero-extra insert fusion, and
  cached literal context state measured 0.9954x, 0.9883x, and 0.9898x
  geometrically. Carrying the LUT's two-bit distance context through the
  command result lost 2.53%, and outlining the hot dictionary branch lost
  7.01%, both with 0/15 wins. All variants were removed; the next useful
  `clustered_q8` work must reduce actual distance/copy execution without
  expanding returned state or adding hot call boundaries.

- A complete non-timing copy-shape audit found only 24 overlapping LZ77 copies
  in `clustered_q8`. Lengths 5--8 account for 7,808 short copies, while exact
  lengths 193/292/732/979 account for 1,150 large copies and 812,072 decoded
  bytes. Transform zero supplies 3,749/4,255 dictionary commands and 3,378
  dictionary outputs are only 4--8 bytes. Despite this concentration, an
  8/16-byte short tier, packed or exact small dictionary stores, a 128-byte
  vector loop, and a constant 979-byte memcpy all regressed complete decode to
  0.9883x, 0.9870x/0.9747x, 0.9421x, and 0.9845x geometrically. Removing the
  nonzero-length check was also negative at 0.9964x. All code was removed;
  the retained fixed-16 short move and dynamic system memcpy remain the
  measured best x86 copy kernels.

- The multi-tree Brotli executor now caches the active distance block's
  context-three tree index and refreshes that byte on each block switch. A
  non-timing audit found context three on 15,997/16,663 explicit distances
  (96.0%) with only 17 switches; the other contexts keep their parsed-map path
  and every tree index remains checked. Against frozen `a74d1d1b`, 21
  fixed-CPU-2 long pairs improve `clustered_q8` by 1.0039x median / 1.0050x
  geometric throughput with 17/21 wins and a 0.9949x minimum. Seven full-
  matrix pairs win 7/7 on target; long `structured` and `text_q3` controls are
  positive, while source q1 stays neutral and remains above libbrotli.
  Candidate/libbrotli 1.2.0-dev reaches only 0.8570x median, so broader Brotli
  leadership remains open. All 541 direct tests, the 13-row reference gate,
  upstream and real-corpus differentials, and the full repository check pass.

- Direct recent-distance shortcuts after the context-three cache were rejected.
  Symbols zero through three occur 1,960 times, including 1,835 symbol-one
  hits, but direct ring indexing expanded the hot executor by 124 bytes and
  measured 0.9985x median with 5/15 wins. Restricting the shortcut to symbol
  one still added 108 bytes and measured 0.9994x median with 6/15 wins; a
  single 1.53x host outlier made its geometric mean misleading. Both variants
  were removed, retaining the compact noinline short-distance resolver.

- Extending the retained context-three cache from one tree index to one index
  plus its external lookup pointer was rejected. The extra live pointer grew
  the executor from `0x119e` to `0x11da` bytes and measured 0.9863x median /
  0.9889x geometric throughput with 2/15 wins. This reproduces the register-
  pressure failure of the earlier four-pointer cache; production retains only
  the byte-sized tree index.

- The current x86-64 65--256-literal-tree gap was re-measured on repository
  source and roadmap q5/q9 streams at only 0.6613x/0.6652x and
  0.6399x/0.6175x libbrotli 1.2.0-dev. A global 9-bit wide root improved source
  by 1.0317x/1.0248x geometrically but regressed roadmap to 0.9870x/0.9881x.
  A format-derived policy (`ten_bit_symbols <= 2 * tree_count`) selected the
  intended rows, and O(1) header-histogram accounting removed the metadata
  rescan, but duplicating 9- and 10-bit payload executors still moved the
  established 10-bit layout: roadmap q5 remained 0.9940x geometric with 1/7
  wins. Reversing instantiation order did not change LLVM emission order, and
  Zig 0.16 function sections cannot depend on a generic comptime parameter.
  All variants were removed rather than worsening the slowest row. Exact data
  is in `docs/performance/brotli-wide-root-x86.md` and its JSON companion.

- The retained Brotli wide-root policy now gives only the 65--128 literal-tree
  middle tier a 9-bit root and places its explicit setup/payload executors in
  the isolated `.vort_br_wide_lookup9` section; 129--256-tree streams keep the
  original 10-bit full tier, with no header metadata or runtime width branch.
  Fifteen fixed-CPU-2 source-q9 pairs improve by 1.0231x median / 1.0222x
  geometric throughput with 15/15 wins and a 1.0093x minimum. Source q5 and
  roadmap q5/q9 10-bit controls are neutral-positive at 1.0033x/1.0050x/
  1.0014x medians; `clustered_q8` is neutral at 0.9997x median. Candidate
  source-q9 throughput reaches 0.6814x local libbrotli, so the wide literal
  loop remains a major open gap. All 541 direct tests, reference/upstream/real-
  corpus gates, and the full check pass.

- The isolated 9-bit middle-tier executor now retains its active literal
  context-map pointer, mode, and block countdown across commands. A non-timing
  source-q9 pass found 20,486 literals, only 204 root misses, 10,965 short
  insert runs, and just ten literal block switches, making repeated header
  state traffic the next bounded target. Against frozen `0ae320e3`, 15
  fixed-CPU-2 pairs improve by another 1.0127x median / 1.0116x geometric
  throughput with 15/15 wins and a 1.00035x minimum. Final throughput reaches
  0.6910x median local libbrotli. All 541 tests, reference/upstream/real-corpus
  gates, and the full repository check pass.

- A non-timing pass over the retained 9-bit wide executor found only 204 root
  misses among 20,486 literals (1.0%), plus 10,965 insert runs and ten literal
  block switches. A 9-bit-only seven-byte refill shrank the two payload
  instances by 177/441 bytes but regressed 15/15 source-q9 pairs to 0.9763x
  median / 0.9770x geometric throughput. The variant was removed, confirming
  that the established six-byte refill remains faster even with a nine-bit
  root; further work should shorten context/tree dependencies or loop
  transitions rather than change root coverage or refill width.

- A 64-entry current-block context-to-lookup pointer table for the 9-bit wide
  executor was rejected. It removed the tree-index load and scaled lookup-base
  address on root hits, but its 512-byte table expanded the two payload
  instances by 606/311 bytes and regressed 15/15 source-q9 pairs to 0.9698x
  median / 0.9662x geometric throughput. The retained byte context map plus
  indexed root lookup has the better cache/register tradeoff.

- The retained 9-bit executor now handles its dominant single-literal insert
  through the shared literal body with `run_len = 1`. A shape audit counted
  50,530 commands, 39,571 zero inserts, and 7,166 single-literal runs among
  10,959 non-zero inserts. Duplicating the whole single-literal transition grew
  the executors by about 1.6 KiB and regressed to 0.9914x geometric; the shared
  run-length shortcut instead improves 15/15 source-q9 pairs by 1.0071x median /
  1.0083x geometric throughput with a 1.00265x minimum. Final throughput is
  0.6971x median local libbrotli. All 541 tests, compatibility/reference gates,
  and the full check pass.

- Extending the retained single-literal shortcut to block-local runs of two
  and three literals was rejected. Those lengths occur 1,634/825 times, but
  the extra remaining-count and boundary condition measured 0.9949x median /
  0.9944x geometric throughput with 2/15 wins. Production keeps only the exact
  `insert_len == 1` invariant.
